pūrvāhṇe ca tvayā tena madhyāhne cāpareṇa tu ..3 3
oṃ namo bhagavate jñānātmane tvāṃ ca .
viṣṇostatparamaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ ..34
1.143.d:
देवानां गीर्भिरभितः संस्तुतः शाश्वतो दिवि ।
पूर्वाह्णे च त्वया तेन मध्याह्ने चापरेण तु ॥3 3
ओं नमो भगवते ज्ञानात्मने त्वां च ।
विष्णोस्तत्परमं पदं सदा पश्यंति सूरयः ॥34
1.143.m: praised all around by the songs of the gods, eternal in heaven. / And in the morning by you with that, and at midday with another, / 'Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the embodiment of knowledge, and to you. / The sages always behold that supreme step of Viṣṇu.'

1.143.s:
divākarastu sāyāhne mantreṇārghyaṃ nivedayet . oṃ
namo varuṇāya śambhave ..35
1.143.d:
दिवाकरस्तु सायाह्ने मन्त्रेणार्घ्यं निवेदयेत् । ओं
नमो वरुणाय शम्भवे ॥35
1.143.m: In the evening, he should present the arghya to the Maker of Day with the mantra: / 'Oṃ, homage to Varuṇa, to Śambhu.'

1.143.s:
oṃ ākṛṣṇena rajasā vartamāno niveśayannamṛtaṃ martyaṃ ca .
hiraṇyayena savitā rathenādevo yāti bhuvanāni paśyan..36
1.143.d:
ओं आकृष्णेन रजसा वर्तमानो निवेशयन्नमृतं मर्त्यं च ।
हिरण्ययेन सविता रथेनादेवो याति भुवनानि पश्यन्॥36
1.143.m: "Oṃ, circling through the dark space, laying to rest the immortal and the mortal, / the god Savitṛ comes on his golden chariot, beholding the worlds."

1.143.s:
anena vidhinā dattvā dhūpaṃ sūryāya bhojakaḥ .
utkṣipeccaiva dhūpena viśedgarbhagṛhaṃ tataḥ . . 37
1.143.d:
अनेन विधिना दत्त्वा धूपं सूर्याय भोजकः ।
उत्क्षिपेच्चैव धूपेन विशेद्गर्भगृहं ततः ॥ 37
1.143.m: Having offered incense to the Sun according to this rule, the bhojaka / should raise [the vessel] and enter the sanctum sanctorum with the incense.

1.143.s:
tataḥ praviśya dhūpaṃ tu pratimārthaṃ nivedayet .
mantreṇa mihirāyeti nikṣubhāyeti nityaśaḥ . . 38
1.143.d:
ततः प्रविश्य धूपं तु प्रतिमार्थं निवेदयेत् ।
मन्त्रेण मिहिरायेति निक्षुभायेति नित्यशः ॥ 38
1.143.m: Then having entered, he should present the incense for the image / daily with the mantra 'To Mihira', 'To Nikṣubhā';

1.143.s:
tato rājñai namaśceti nikṣubhāyai tato namaḥ .
daṇḍanāyakasaṃjñāya piṅgalāya ca vai namaḥ . . 39
1.143.d:
ततो राज्ञै नमश्चेति निक्षुभायै ततो नमः ।
दण्डनायकसंज्ञाय पिङ्गलाय च वै नमः ॥ 39
1.143.m: then 'Homage to Rājñī' and then 'Homage to Nikṣubhā', / and indeed 'Homage to the one named Daṇḍanāyaka and to Piṅgala',

1.143.s:
tathā rājñāya srauṣāya tatheśāya garutmate .
tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kurvandigdevebhyo nivedayet . . 1.143.40
1.143.d:
तथा राज्ञाय स्रौषाय तथेशाय गरुत्मते ।
ततः प्रदक्षिणं कुर्वन्दिग्देवेभ्यो निवेदयेत् ॥ 1.143.40
1.143.m: likewise to Rājña, to Srauṣa, likewise to the lord Garuḍa. / Then, circumambulating, he should present it to the deities of the directions.

1.143.s:
diṇḍine tu tato dadyāddhemantāya yadūttama .
maheśvarāya dadyāttu tathā vyomāya yādava . .4 1
(viśvebhyo devebhyo namaḥ . rudrebhyo namaḥ) .
oṃ brahmaṇe muṇḍapataye ādityāya puruṣeśvarāya sūryāya namonamaḥ . . 42
1.143.d:
दिण्डिने तु ततो दद्याद्धेमन्ताय यदूत्तम ।
महेश्वराय दद्यात्तु तथा व्योमाय यादव ॥4 1
(विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो नमः । रुद्रेभ्यो नमः) ।
ओं ब्रह्मणे मुण्डपतये आदित्याय पुरुषेश्वराय सूर्याय नमोनमः ॥ 42
1.143.m: Then one should give to Diṇḍin, and to Hemanta, O best of the Yadus; / and one should give to Maheśvara, and likewise to Vyoman, O Yādava. / (Obeisance to the Viśvedevas. Obeisance to the Rudras.) / Oṃ, obeisance, obeisance to Brahmā, to Muṇḍapati, to Āditya, to Puruṣeśvara, to Sūrya.

1.143.s:
oṃ anekakāntaye natvā śeṣāya vāsukitakṣakakarkoṭakāya padmaśaṅkhakulikebhyo nāgarājebhyo namaḥ . .4 3
talasutalapātālātalavitalarasātalādivāsibhyo daityādānavapiśācebhyo namaḥ .
tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryānmātṛkābhyo namonamaḥ ( oṃ grahebhyo namaḥ . . 44
1.143.d:
ओं अनेककान्तये नत्वा शेषाय वासुकितक्षककर्कोटकाय पद्मशङ्खकुलिकेभ्यो नागराजेभ्यो नमः ॥4 3
तलसुतलपातालातलवितलरसातलादिवासिभ्यो दैत्यादानवपिशाचेभ्यो नमः ।
ततः प्रदक्षिणं कुर्यान्मातृकाभ्यो नमोनमः ( ओं ग्रहेभ्यो नमः ॥ 44
1.143.m: Oṃ, bowing to him of manifold splendour, to Śeṣa, to Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Karkoṭaka, to Padma, Śaṅkha, and Kulika, obeisance to the serpent kings. / Obeisance to the Daityas, Dānavas, and piśācas dwelling in Tala, Sutala, Pātāla, Atala, Vitala, Rasātala, and the other [nether worlds]. / Then one should circumambulate: obeisance, obeisance to the Mothers. (Oṃ, obeisance to the planets.

1.143.s:
oṃ daṇḍanāyakāya namaḥ . oṃ mārtaṃḍāya namaḥ . oṃ vināyakāya namaḥ . . 45)
evamuddiśya nāmāni dhūpaṃ dattvā varānana .
utkṣipto yatra vai dhūpo muktvā tatraiva taṃ punaḥ . . 46
1.143.d:
ओं दण्डनायकाय नमः । ओं मार्तंडाय नमः । ओं विनायकाय नमः ॥ 45)
एवमुद्दिश्य नामानि धूपं दत्त्वा वरानन ।
उत्क्षिप्तो यत्र वै धूपो मुक्त्वा तत्रैव तं पुनः ॥ 46
1.143.m: Oṃ, obeisance to Daṇḍanāyaka. Oṃ, obeisance to Mārtaṇḍa. Oṃ, obeisance to Vināyaka.) / Having thus addressed their names and offered incense, O fair-faced one, / where the incense was lifted up, leaving it again right there,

1.143.s:
sūryaguptairabhiṣṭūya evaṃ vijñāya te tataḥ .
arcitastvaṃ yathā śaktyā mayā bhaktyā vibhāvaso . .
aihikāmuṣmikīṃ nātha kāryasiddhiṃ vadasva me . . 47
1.143.d:
सूर्यगुप्तैरभिष्टूय एवं विज्ञाय ते ततः ।
अर्चितस्त्वं यथा शक्त्या मया भक्त्या विभावसो ॥
ऐहिकामुष्मिकीं नाथ कार्यसिद्धिं वदस्व मे ॥ 47
1.143.m: praising [him] with the hymns concealed for the Sun, and having thus acknowledged them, then: / 'You have been worshipped by me according to my capacity and with devotion, O Vibhāvasu; / tell me, O Lord, of the accomplishment of my aims in this world and the next.'

1.143.s:
evaṃ triṣavaṇaṃ snātvā yo'rcayetpraṇato ravim .
vidhinā tu yathoktena so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet . . 48
1.143.d:
एवं त्रिषवणं स्नात्वा योऽर्चयेत्प्रणतो रविम् ।
विधिना तु यथोक्तेन सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥ 48
1.143.m: Whoever, having bathed at the three junctures of the day, thus worships the sun with bowed head / according to the prescribed rule, obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice.

1.143.s:
yaścaivaṃ kurute nityaṃ yathoktaṃ dhūpavistaram .
sa putravānarogī ca mṛtaḥ saṃlīyate ravau . . 49
1.143.d:
यश्चैवं कुरुते नित्यं यथोक्तं धूपविस्तरम् ।
स पुत्रवानरोगी च मृतः संलीयते रवौ ॥ 49
1.143.m: And he who constantly performs the elaborate incense offering as prescribed, / has sons, remains free from disease, and upon death is dissolved into the sun.

1.143.s:
vidhinā tu yathoktena kriyamāṇāni yatnataḥ .
sarvakāryāṇi siddhyanti saphalāni bhavanti ca . . 1.143.50
1.143.d:
विधिना तु यथोक्तेन क्रियमाणानि यत्नतः ।
सर्वकार्याणि सिद्ध्यन्ति सफलानि भवन्ति च ॥ 1.143.50
1.143.m: When performed with effort according to the prescribed rule, / all undertakings succeed and become fruitful.

1.143.s:
puṣpaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yadā na syātpatrāṇi samupāharet .
patraṃ na syāttato dhūpaṃ dhūpo na syāttato jalam . . 51
1.143.d:
पुष्पं श्रेष्ठं यदा न स्यात्पत्राणि समुपाहरेत् ।
पत्रं न स्यात्ततो धूपं धूपो न स्यात्ततो जलम् ॥ 51
1.143.m: When excellent flowers are not available, one should bring leaves; / if leaves are not available, then incense; if incense is not available, then water.

1.143.s:
sarvaṃ na syādyadā caiva praṇipātena pūjayet .
aśaktaḥ praṇipātasya manasā pūjayedravim . . 52
1.143.d:
सर्वं न स्याद्यदा चैव प्रणिपातेन पूजयेत् ।
अशक्तः प्रणिपातस्य मनसा पूजयेद्रविम् ॥ 52
1.143.m: And when nothing at all is available, one should worship by prostration; / if unable to prostrate, one should worship the sun mentally.

1.143.s:
asambhave tu dravyāṇāṃ vidhireṣa prakīrtitaḥ .
dravyāṇāṃ sambhave caiva sarvamevopahārayet . . 53
1.143.d:
असम्भवे तु द्रव्याणां विधिरेष प्रकीर्तितः ।
द्रव्याणां सम्भवे चैव सर्वमेवोपहारयेत् ॥ 53
1.143.m: This rule is proclaimed for when materials are unavailable; / but when materials are available, one must offer everything indeed.

1.143.s:
mantraiḥ karmayuto yastu mitre dhūpaṃ nivedayet .
uccāraṇācca vai teṣāṃ dhūpaprīto bhavedraviḥ . . 54
1.143.d:
मन्त्रैः कर्मयुतो यस्तु मित्रे धूपं निवेदयेत् ।
उच्चारणाच्च वै तेषां धूपप्रीतो भवेद्रविः ॥ 54
1.143.m: He who, engaged in the rite, offers incense to Mitra with mantras— / from the very recitation of those, the sun becomes pleased with the incense.

1.143.s:
śiro nāsāmukhaṃ caiva bhṛśamāvṛtya yatnataḥ .
pūjayedbhāskaraṃ vīra śithilaṃ1 tu na kārayet . . 55
1.143.d:
शिरो नासामुखं चैव भृशमावृत्य यत्नतः ।
पूजयेद्भास्करं वीर शिथिलं1 तु न कारयेत् ॥ 55
1.143.m: Covering the head, nose, and mouth very tightly with care, / one should worship the Sun, O hero; one should not let it become loose.

1.143.s:
nalinena tu rājendra naro yāti divākaram .
tasmādyuktaṃ sadā kāryaṃ pūjyate ca divākaraḥ . . 56
1.143.d:
नलिनेन तु राजेन्द्र नरो याति दिवाकरम् ।
तस्माद्युक्तं सदा कार्यं पूज्यते च दिवाकरः ॥ 56
1.143.m: By means of the lotus-stalk, O king of kings, a man goes to the Sun; / therefore that which is proper should always be done, and the Sun is worshipped.

1.143.s:
te'śvamedhaphalaṃ prāpya sūryalokaṃ vrajanti hi .
dhūpena pūjyamānaṃ tu narāḥ paśyanti yādava . . 57
1.143.d:
तेऽश्वमेधफलं प्राप्य सूर्यलोकं व्रजन्ति हि ।
धूपेन पूज्यमानं तु नराः पश्यन्ति यादव ॥ 57
1.143.m: Having obtained the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice, they indeed go to the world of the sun; / men who behold him being worshipped with incense, O Yādava,

1.143.s:
yānti te paramaṃ sthānaṃ yanna paśyanti sūrayaḥ .
kriyamāṇaṃ tathārkaṃ ca bhaktyā paśyanti ye narāḥ . .
sarvānkāmāniha prāpya te yānti paramaṃ padam . . 58
1.143.d:
यान्ति ते परमं स्थानं यन्न पश्यन्ति सूरयः ।
क्रियमाणं तथार्कं च भक्त्या पश्यन्ति ये नराः ॥
सर्वान्कामानिह प्राप्य ते यान्ति परमं पदम् ॥ 58
1.143.m: they go to the supreme abode which [even] sages do not see. / And those men who behold the Sun being thus worshipped with devotion, / having obtained all desires in this world, go to the supreme state.

1.143.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sāmbopākhyāne
dhūpādivividhavarṇanaṃ nāma tricatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 143 .
bhojakasyotpattivarṇanam
1.143.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे साम्बोपाख्याने
धूपादिविविधवर्णनं नाम त्रिचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 143 ।
भोजकस्योत्पत्तिवर्णनम्
1.143.m:
Thus, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the Saptamīkalpa, in the Sāmba narrative, / the one hundred and forty-third chapter, entitled 'The Description of Various Matters such as Incense'.
Description of the Origin of the Bhojaka.

1.144.s:
sumanturuvāca
athājagāma bhagavānvyāso dvāravatīṃ purīm .
draṣṭuṃ nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam . . 1
1.144.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
अथाजगाम भगवान्व्यासो द्वारवतीं पुरीम् ।
द्रष्टुं नारायणं देवं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् ॥ 1
1.144.m: Sumantu said: / Then the blessed Vyāsa came to the city of Dvāravatī / to see the god Nārāyaṇa, who bears the conch, discus, and mace.

1.144.s:
tamāgatamṛṣiṃ dṛṣṭvā vāsudevo viśāṃpate .
abhyutthāya mahātejāḥ pūjayāmāsa bhārata . . 2
1.144.d:
तमागतमृषिं दृष्ट्वा वासुदेवो विशांपते ।
अभ्युत्थाय महातेजाः पूजयामास भारत ॥ 2
1.144.m: Seeing that the sage had arrived, Vāsudeva of great splendour, / O ruler of men, rose up and honoured him, O Bhārata.

1.144.s:
svayamevāsanaṃ dattvā pādyamarghyaṃ tathaiva ca .
papraccha prayato bhūtvā vyāsaṃ satyavatīsutam . . 3
1.144.d:
स्वयमेवासनं दत्त्वा पाद्यमर्घ्यं तथैव च ।
पप्रच्छ प्रयतो भूत्वा व्यासं सत्यवतीसुतम् ॥ 3
1.144.m: Having himself offered a seat, water for the feet, and the respectful offering of arghya, / he became attentive and questioned Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī:

1.144.s:
ya ete bhojakā viprā ānītā matsutena vai .
śākadvīpamito gatvā jñānino mokṣagāminaḥ . . 4
1.144.d:
य एते भोजका विप्रा आनीता मत्सुतेन वै ।
शाकद्वीपमितो गत्वा ज्ञानिनो मोक्षगामिनः ॥ 4
1.144.m: 'These Bhojaka brāhmaṇas who were brought by my son, / having gone from here to Śākadvīpa—wise men bound for liberation—

1.144.s:
tāndṛṣṭvā rūpato vipra praveśātkarmatastathā.
kautūhalaṃ samutpannaṃ harṣaśca paramo mama . . 5
1.144.d:
तान्दृष्ट्वा रूपतो विप्र प्रवेशात्कर्मतस्तथा।
कौतूहलं समुत्पन्नं हर्षश्च परमो मम ॥ 5
1.144.m: having seen them by their appearance, O brāhmaṇa, by their conduct, and by their rites, / curiosity arose in me, as well as supreme joy.

1.144.s:
kathamete kṣaṇamapi tiṣṭhante pṛthivītale .
yeṣāṃ raviḥ sadā pūjyasteṣāṃ muktiḥ sadā vaset . . 6
1.144.d:
कथमेते क्षणमपि तिष्ठन्ते पृथिवीतले ।
येषां रविः सदा पूज्यस्तेषां मुक्तिः सदा वसेत् ॥ 6
1.144.m: How do these men remain even for a moment on the surface of the earth? / For those by whom the sun is always to be worshipped, liberation must always abide.

1.144.s:
nāgatvā bhojakatvaṃ hi mokṣamāpnoti kaścana .
idaṃ me manaso brahmansadā sampratibhāti vai . . 7
1.144.d:
नागत्वा भोजकत्वं हि मोक्षमाप्नोति कश्चन ।
इदं मे मनसो ब्रह्मन्सदा सम्प्रतिभाति वै ॥ 7
1.144.m: Indeed, without attaining the state of a Bhojaka, no one attains liberation; / this, O holy one, ever appears true to my mind.'

1.144.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evameva yathāttha tvaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādhara .
dhanyā ete mahātmāno bhojakā nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 8
1.144.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवमेव यथात्थ त्वं शङ्खचक्रगदाधर ।
धन्या एते महात्मानो भोजका नात्र संशयः ॥ 8
1.144.m: Vyāsa said: / 'It is just as you have said, O bearer of the conch, discus, and mace. / Blessed are these great-souled Bhojakas; of this there is no doubt,

1.144.s:
ye pūjayanti satataṃ bhānumantaṃ divākaram .
jñāninaḥ karmaniṣṭhāśca sadā mokṣagatiṃ gatāḥ . . 9
1.144.d:
ये पूजयन्ति सततं भानुमन्तं दिवाकरम् ।
ज्ञानिनः कर्मनिष्ठाश्च सदा मोक्षगतिं गताः ॥ 9
1.144.m: who constantly worship the radiant Sun; / wise, steadfast in action, they have always attained the path of liberation.

1.144.s:
yajante satataṃ bhānuṃ balipuṣpaphalaistathā .
annenauṣadhibhiścaiva ājyahomaiśca kṛtsnaśaḥ . . 1.144.10
1.144.d:
यजन्ते सततं भानुं बलिपुष्पफलैस्तथा ।
अन्नेनौषधिभिश्चैव आज्यहोमैश्च कृत्स्नशः ॥ 1.144.10
1.144.m: They worship the Sun continually with offerings, flowers, and fruits, / with food, medicinal herbs, and oblation of clarified butter in their entirety.

1.144.s:
homaṃ ca śāśvataṃ kṛtvā paraṃ homaṃ tataḥ śritāḥ .
parahomasya karaṇātpūtātmāno hyakalmaṣāḥ . . 11
1.144.d:
होमं च शाश्वतं कृत्वा परं होमं ततः श्रिताः ।
परहोमस्य करणात्पूतात्मानो ह्यकल्मषाः ॥ 11
1.144.m: And having performed the perpetual homa, they then take resort in the supreme homa; / through performing the supreme homa, their souls purified and free from defilement,

1.144.s:
viśanti paramāṃ divyāṃ bhāskarīṃ taijasīṃ kalām .
karmaṇaḥ sādhane caikā tatra cāgnau pratiṣṭhitā . . 12
1.144.d:
विशन्ति परमां दिव्यां भास्करीं तैजसीं कलाम् ।
कर्मणः साधने चैका तत्र चाग्नौ प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ 12
1.144.m: they enter the supreme, divine, fiery portion belonging to the Sun. / And for the accomplishment of ritual action, one [portion] is established there in the fire;

1.144.s:
vāyumārgasthitā vyomni dvitīyāntaḥ prakāśikā .
tataḥ paraṃ tṛtīyā tu tatsmṛtaṃ sūryamaṇḍale . . 13
1.144.d:
वायुमार्गस्थिता व्योम्नि द्वितीयान्तः प्रकाशिका ।
ततः परं तृतीया तु तत्स्मृतं सूर्यमण्डले ॥ 13
1.144.m: the second, standing in the path of the wind in the sky, illuminates within; / and beyond that is the third, which is known [to abide] in the orb of the sun.

1.144.s:
maṇḍalaṃ tacca saviturdivyaṃ hyajaramavyayam .
tasyā'sau puruṣo madhye yo'sau sadasadātmakaḥ . . 14
1.144.d:
मण्डलं तच्च सवितुर्दिव्यं ह्यजरमव्ययम् ।
तस्याऽसौ पुरुषो मध्ये योऽसौ सदसदात्मकः ॥ 14
1.144.m: And that orb of the sun is divine, ageless, and imperishable; / in the middle of it is that Person whose self consists of the real and the unreal.

1.144.s:
kṣarākṣarastu vijñeyo mahāsūryastathaiva ca .
niṣkalaḥ sakalaścāpi dvau ca tasya prakalpitau . . 15
1.144.d:
क्षराक्षरस्तु विज्ञेयो महासूर्यस्तथैव च ।
निष्कलः सकलश्चापि द्वौ च तस्य प्रकल्पितौ ॥ 15
1.144.m: He is to be known as both perishable and imperishable, and likewise as the Great Sun; / he is both without parts and with parts—two [forms] of his are conceived.

1.144.s:
akṣaraḥ sakalaścaiva sarvabhūtavyavasthitaḥ .
satattvaḥ sakalaḥ proktastattvahīnastu niṣkalaḥ . . 16
1.144.d:
अक्षरः सकलश्चैव सर्वभूतव्यवस्थितः ।
सतत्त्वः सकलः प्रोक्तस्तत्त्वहीनस्तु निष्कलः ॥ 16
1.144.m: He is imperishable and with parts, residing in all beings; / having tattvas, he is called "with parts"; but devoid of tattvas, he is "without parts".

1.144.s:
tṛṇagulmalatāvṛkṣavṛkasiṃhadvijādhipān .
surasiddhamanuṣyāṃśca sthalajāñjalajānharet . . 17
1.144.d:
तृणगुल्मलतावृक्षवृकसिंहद्विजाधिपान् ।
सुरसिद्धमनुष्यांश्च स्थलजाञ्जलजान्हरेत् ॥ 17
1.144.m: Grasses, shrubs, creepers, trees, wolves, lions, lords of birds, / gods, siddhas, humans, land-dwellers, and water-dwellers—he takes them [all].

1.144.s:
vyavasthitaḥ sa sarvatra sarveṣāmantarātmani .
yadā kalpātmakaścaiva dvitīyāṃ tanumāśritaḥ . . 18
1.144.d:
व्यवस्थितः स सर्वत्र सर्वेषामन्तरात्मनि ।
यदा कल्पात्मकश्चैव द्वितीयां तनुमाश्रितः ॥ 18
1.144.m: He is stationed everywhere in the inner self of all beings; / when he is composed of eons, he assumes a second body.

1.144.s:
niṣkalastu sadā jñeyaḥ saṃsthitastaijasīṃ kalām .
himaṃ gharmaṃ ca varṣaṃ ca trailokye kurute sadā . . 19
1.144.d:
निष्कलस्तु सदा ज्ञेयः संस्थितस्तैजसीं कलाम् ।
हिमं घर्मं च वर्षं च त्रैलोक्ये कुरुते सदा ॥ 19
1.144.m: He is always to be known as without parts, abiding in the fiery portion; / he always produces cold, heat, and rain in the three worlds.

1.144.s:
dvitīyā yā tanustasya akṣaraṃ tatparaṃ padam .
devayānaṃ tu panthānaṃ karmayogena saṃsthitā . 1.144.20
1.144.d:
द्वितीया या तनुस्तस्य अक्षरं तत्परं पदम् ।
देवयानं तु पन्थानं कर्मयोगेन संस्थिता । 1.144.20
1.144.m: That second body of his is the imperishable, supreme state; / established on the path of the gods by the yoga of action,

1.144.s:
ādityasiddhāntaritāḥ sāṅkhyayogavidaśca ye .
te'bhigacchanti tatsthānaṃ sa mokṣaḥ parikīrtitaḥ . . 21
1.144.d:
आदित्यसिद्धान्तरिताः साङ्ख्ययोगविदश्च ये ।
तेऽभिगच्छन्ति तत्स्थानं स मोक्षः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 21
1.144.m: those devoted to the solar doctrine, and those who know Sāṅkhya and Yoga, / reach that abode; that is proclaimed as liberation.

1.144.s:
nirdvandvo nirgamaścaiva tatra gatvā na śocati .
vedeṣu brahma vadanti dhyāyante tattvavedinaḥ . . 22
1.144.d:
निर्द्वन्द्वो निर्गमश्चैव तत्र गत्वा न शोचति ।
वेदेषु ब्रह्म वदन्ति ध्यायन्ते तत्त्ववेदिनः ॥ 22
1.144.m: Free from the pairs of opposites and departed [from saṃsāra], having gone there one does not grieve. / In the Vedas they speak of it as Brahman; those who know the truth meditate upon it.

1.144.s:
akāraṃ tattvataścāpi dhyāyante puruṣottama .
tryakṣaraṃ ca tamoṃkāraṃ sārdhamātrātraye sthitam . . 23
1.144.d:
अकारं तत्त्वतश्चापि ध्यायन्ते पुरुषोत्तम ।
त्र्यक्षरं च तमोंकारं सार्धमात्रात्रये स्थितम् ॥ 23
1.144.m: And in reality, O supreme among men, they meditate on the letter "A", / and on that three-lettered Oṃkāra abiding in three and a half measures.

1.144.s:
vadanti cārdhamātrasthaṃ makāraṃ vyañjanātmakam.
dhyāyanti ye makārīyaṃ jñānaṃ te hi sadātmakam . . 24
1.144.d:
वदन्ति चार्धमात्रस्थं मकारं व्यञ्जनात्मकम्।
ध्यायन्ति ये मकारीयं ज्ञानं ते हि सदात्मकम् ॥ 24
1.144.m: And they declare the consonant "M" to reside in the half-measure; / those who meditate on the knowledge pertaining to "M" [meditate] indeed on that which consists of eternal being.'

1.144.s:
makāro bhagavāndevo bhāskaraḥ parikīrtitaḥ .
makāradhyānayogācca magā hyete prakīrtitāḥ . . 25
1.144.d:
मकारो भगवान्देवो भास्करः परिकीर्तितः ।
मकारध्यानयोगाच्च मगा ह्येते प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 25
1.144.m: The letter Ma is proclaimed to be the blessed god Bhāskara, / and through the practice of meditation upon the letter Ma, these are indeed proclaimed as Magas.

1.144.s:
dhūpamālyairyutaścāpi upahāraistathaiva ca .
bhojayanti sahasrāṃśuṃ tena te bhojakāḥ smṛtāḥ . . 26
bhojakajñānavarṇanam
1.144.d:
धूपमाल्यैर्युतश्चापि उपहारैस्तथैव च ।
भोजयन्ति सहस्रांशुं तेन ते भोजकाः स्मृताः ॥ 26
भोजकज्ञानवर्णनम्
1.144.m:
Equipped with incense and garlands, and likewise with offerings, / they feed the thousand-rayed Sun; for that reason, they are traditionally known as Bhojakas.
Description of the Knowledge of the Bhojakas

1.145.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
jñānopalabdhiṃ viprendra bhojakānāṃ mahāmune .
brūhi tattvaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha kautukaṃ paramaṃ mama . . 1
1.145.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
ज्ञानोपलब्धिं विप्रेन्द्र भोजकानां महामुने ।
ब्रूहि तत्त्वं द्विजश्रेष्ठ कौतुकं परमं मम ॥ 1
1.145.m: Vāsudeva said: / O foremost of sages, leader of the brahmins, declare to me the true reality of the attainment of knowledge / of the Bhojakas, O best of the twice-born; great is my curiosity.

1.145.s:
vyāsa uvāca
imāṃ jñānopalabdhiṃ tu nibodha gadato mama .
asthisthūlaṃ snāyuyutaṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepanam . .
carmāvanaddhaṃ durgaṃdhipūrṇaṃ mūtrapurīṣayoḥ . . 2
1.145.d:
व्यास उवाच
इमां ज्ञानोपलब्धिं तु निबोध गदतो मम ।
अस्थिस्थूलं स्नायुयुतं मांसशोणितलेपनम् ॥
चर्मावनद्धं दुर्गंधिपूर्णं मूत्रपुरीषयोः ॥ 2
1.145.m: Vyāsa said: / Listen as I proclaim this attainment of knowledge: / Thick with bones, joined with sinews, smeared with flesh and blood, / bound with skin, foul-smelling, and filled with urine and feces,

1.145.s:
jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ rogāyatanamāturam .
rajasvalamanityaṃ ca bhūtāvāsamimaṃ tyajet . . 3
1.145.d:
जराशोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनमातुरम् ।
रजस्वलमनित्यं च भूतावासमिमं त्यजेत् ॥ 3
1.145.m: overcome with old age and grief, an afflicted abode of disease, / impure and impermanent—one should abandon this dwelling of the elements.

1.145.s:
kapālaṃ vṛkṣamūlāni kucailamasahāyatā .
samatā sarvabhūteṣu evaṃ muktasya lakṣaṇam . . 4
1.145.d:
कपालं वृक्षमूलानि कुचैलमसहायता ।
समता सर्वभूतेषु एवं मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ 4
1.145.m: A skull-bowl, the roots of trees, ragged garments, solitude, / and equanimity toward all beings: such is the mark of a liberated one.

1.145.s:
tile tailaṃ gavi kṣīraṃ kāṣṭhe pāvakasantatiḥ .
upāyaṃ cintayedasya dhiyā dhīraḥ samāhitaḥ . . 5
1.145.d:
तिले तैलं गवि क्षीरं काष्ठे पावकसन्ततिः ।
उपायं चिन्तयेदस्य धिया धीरः समाहितः ॥ 5
1.145.m: Oil in sesame, milk in a cow, the continuity of fire in wood— / the steadfast, concentrated man should contemplate the means to [attain] this with his intellect.

1.145.s:
pramāthi ca prayatnena manaḥ saṃyamya cañcalam .
buddhīndriyāṇi saṃyamya śakunāniva pañjare . . 6
1.145.d:
प्रमाथि च प्रयत्नेन मनः संयम्य चञ्चलम् ।
बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि संयम्य शकुनानिव पञ्जरे ॥ 6
1.145.m: Restraining with effort the turbulent, fickle mind, / and holding in check the cognitive senses like birds in a cage,

1.145.s:
indriyairniyatairdehī dhārābhiriva tṛpyate .
satatamamṛtasyaiva janārdana mahāmate . . 7
1.145.d:
इन्द्रियैर्नियतैर्देही धाराभिरिव तृप्यते ।
सततममृतस्यैव जनार्दन महामते ॥ 7
1.145.m: the embodied soul, with senses restrained, is continuously satisfied / as if by streams of nectar, O great-minded Janārdana.

1.145.s:
prāṇāyāmairdaheddoṣāndhāraṇābhiśca1 kilbiṣam .
pratyāhāreṇa saṃsargāndhyānenānīśvarānguṇān . . 8
1.145.d:
प्राणायामैर्दहेद्दोषान्धारणाभिश्च1 किल्बिषम् ।
प्रत्याहारेण संसर्गान्ध्यानेनानीश्वरान्गुणान् ॥ 8
1.145.m: Through breath-controls one should burn away faults, and through concentrations, sin; / through sensory withdrawal, attachments; and through meditation, the qualities alien to the Lord.

1.145.s:
dhyāyamānasya dahyante cānte doṣā yathāgninā .
tathendriyakṛtā doṣā dahyante prāṇanigrahāt . . 9
1.145.d:
ध्यायमानस्य दह्यन्ते चान्ते दोषा यथाग्निना ।
तथेन्द्रियकृता दोषा दह्यन्ते प्राणनिग्रहात् ॥ 9
1.145.m: Just as impurities in what is being smelted are burned away at last by fire, / so the faults caused by the senses are burned away through control of the breath.

1.145.s:
cittaṃ cittena saṃśodhya bhāvaṃ bhāvena śodhayet .
manastu manasā śodhyaṃ buddhiṃ buddhyā tu śodhayet . . 1.145.10
1.145.d:
चित्तं चित्तेन संशोध्य भावं भावेन शोधयेत् ।
मनस्तु मनसा शोध्यं बुद्धिं बुद्ध्या तु शोधयेत् ॥ 1.145.10
1.145.m: One should purify the mind with the mind, and purify disposition with disposition; / the thought-organ must be purified by the thought-organ, and the intellect purified by the intellect.

1.145.s:
cittasyātiprasādena bhāti karma śubhāśubham .
śubhāśubhavinirmukto nirdvandvo niṣparigrahaḥ . .
nirmamo nirahaṅkārastato yāti parāṃ gatim . . 11
1.145.d:
चित्तस्यातिप्रसादेन भाति कर्म शुभाशुभम् ।
शुभाशुभविनिर्मुक्तो निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः ॥
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारस्ततो याति परां गतिम् ॥ 11
1.145.m: Through the supreme serenity of the mind, good and bad action shine forth [clearly]; / freed from good and bad, beyond the dualities, free of possessions, / devoid of mineness and free of egoism, one then goes to the supreme state.

1.145.s:
parvāhṇe lohitaṃ rūpaṃ prathamamṛṅmamayaṃ smṛtam .
yajurmayaṃ dvitīyaṃ tu śvetaṃ mādhyāhnikaṃ smṛtam . . 12
1.145.d:
पर्वाह्णे लोहितं रूपं प्रथममृङ्ममयं स्मृतम् ।
यजुर्मयं द्वितीयं तु श्वेतं माध्याह्निकं स्मृतम् ॥ 12
1.145.m: In the morning, the first form is remembered as red and made of the Ṛgveda; / the second, made of the Yajurveda, is remembered as white, belonging to midday.

1.145.s:
kṛṣṇaṃ tṛtīyaṃ sāyāhne sāmno rūpaṃ tu tatkṛtam .
prathamaṃ rājasaṃ deva dvitīyaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam . 13
1.145.d:
कृष्णं तृतीयं सायाह्ने साम्नो रूपं तु तत्कृतम् ।
प्रथमं राजसं देव द्वितीयं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् । 13
1.145.m: The third, in the evening, is black, made of the Sāmaveda. / The first is remembered as passionate, O god, and the second as pure;

1.145.s:
tṛtīyaṃ tāmasaṃ rūpaṃ traiguṇyaṃ tasya kalpitam .
trayāṇāṃ vyatirekeṇa caturthaṃ sūryamaṇḍalam . . 14
1.145.d:
तृतीयं तामसं रूपं त्रैगुण्यं तस्य कल्पितम् ।
त्रयाणां व्यतिरेकेण चतुर्थं सूर्यमण्डलम् ॥ 14
1.145.m: the third is the dark form: thus is his threefold nature conceived. / Distinct from these three is the fourth, the solar disc,

1.145.s:
jyotiḥ prakāśakaṃ sūkṣmaṃ proktaṃ devanirañjanam .
caturthaṃ tu vedavidaḥ sūryasiddhāntavedinaḥ . . 15
1.145.d:
ज्योतिः प्रकाशकं सूक्ष्मं प्रोक्तं देवनिरञ्जनम् ।
चतुर्थं तु वेदविदः सूर्यसिद्धान्तवेदिनः ॥ 15
1.145.m: a subtle, illuminating light, proclaimed to be the immaculate god. / Knowers of the Vedas and knowers of the Sūryasiddhānta [know] the fourth.

1.145.s:
oṃkārapraṇavairyuktā dhyānanirbhūtakalmaṣāḥ .
sthitāḥ padmāsane vīrā nābhisaṃnyastapāṇayaḥ . . 16
1.145.d:
ओंकारप्रणवैर्युक्ता ध्याननिर्भूतकल्मषाः ।
स्थिताः पद्मासने वीरा नाभिसंन्यस्तपाणयः ॥ 16
1.145.m: Endowed with the syllable Om, the praṇava, with their impurities wiped away by meditation, / the heroes, seated in the lotus posture, place their hands upon the navel.

1.145.s:
suṣumnānāḍikāmārgaṃ kumbharecakapūrakaiḥ .
tribhiḥ saṃśodhya tānpañca maruto dehamadhyagān .. 17
1.145.d:
सुषुम्नानाडिकामार्गं कुम्भरेचकपूरकैः ।
त्रिभिः संशोध्य तान्पञ्च मरुतो देहमध्यगान् ॥ 17
1.145.m: Purifying the pathway of the suṣumnā channel by the three— / retention, expulsion, and inhalation—along with those five winds moving in the middle of the body,

1.145.s:
padāṅguṣṭhānvitaḥ svinnamūrdhvamutkṣepayetkramāt .
nābhideśe tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā devamagnimanāmayam .. 18
1.145.d:
पदाङ्गुष्ठान्वितः स्विन्नमूर्ध्वमुत्क्षेपयेत्क्रमात् ।
नाभिदेशे तु तं दृष्ट्वा देवमग्निमनामयम् ॥ 18
1.145.m: connected through the big toes, one should gradually cast the heated [breath] upward. / Having seen in the region of the navel that god, the flawless fire,

1.145.s:
somaṃ ca hadaye dṛṣṭvā mūrdhni vāgniśikhāṃ tataḥ .
vātaraśmibhirāsādya taṃ bhittvā maṇḍalaṃ param .. 19
1.145.d:
सोमं च हदये दृष्ट्वा मूर्ध्नि वाग्निशिखां ततः ।
वातरश्मिभिरासाद्य तं भित्त्वा मण्डलं परम् ॥ 19
1.145.m: and having seen Soma in the heart, and then the flame of fire in the crown of the head, / having approached with the rays of wind and pierced that supreme disc,

1.145.s:
tataḥ paraṃ tu yo gacchedyogasthaḥ sūryamaṇḍalam .
yatra gatvā na śocanti tatsauraṃ paramaṃ padam ..1.145.2 0
devārcanaṃ mahābāho kīrtitaḥ keśisūdana .
prathamaṃ hadayaṃ sthānaṃ dvitīyaṃ cāgnimāśritam ..2 1
tṛtīyaṃ nābhisaṃsthaṃ ca caturthaṃ sūryamaṇḍalam ..22
1.145.d:
ततः परं तु यो गच्छेद्योगस्थः सूर्यमण्डलम् ।
यत्र गत्वा न शोचन्ति तत्सौरं परमं पदम् ॥1.145.2 0
देवार्चनं महाबाहो कीर्तितः केशिसूदन ।
प्रथमं हदयं स्थानं द्वितीयं चाग्निमाश्रितम् ॥2 1
तृतीयं नाभिसंस्थं च चतुर्थं सूर्यमण्डलम् ॥22
1.145.m: one who, established in yoga, would then go beyond to the solar disc— / having gone where they grieve no more, that is the supreme solar abode. / Worship of the god, O mighty-armed one, has been proclaimed, O slayer of Keśin: / the first place is the heart, the second resides in fire, / the third is located in the navel, and the fourth is the solar disc.

1.145.s:
sthānaṃ paraṃ vai paramātmasaṃsthaṃ bhānoḥ sureśasya vadanti tajjñāḥ .
jñeyaḥ sa mokṣaśca nṛṇāṃ sa eva saṃsāravicchittikaraṃ padaṃ tataḥ ..23
1.145.d:
स्थानं परं वै परमात्मसंस्थं भानोः सुरेशस्य वदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः ।
ज्ञेयः स मोक्षश्च नृणां स एव संसारविच्छित्तिकरं पदं ततः ॥23
1.145.m: Those who know that reality declare the supreme station of the Sun, the lord of the gods, to abide in the Supreme Self; / that is to be known as liberation for men, and that very station cuts off worldly existence.

1.145.s:
idamamṛtasamaṃ parasya vedyaṃ kiraṇasahasramṛto hitaṃ janānām .
ṛṣicaritamavetya tattvasāraṃ vyapagatamohadhiyaḥ prayānti mokṣam ..24
1.145.d:
इदममृतसमं परस्य वेद्यं किरणसहस्रमृतो हितं जनानाम् ।
ऋषिचरितमवेत्य तत्त्वसारं व्यपगतमोहधियः प्रयान्ति मोक्षम् ॥24
1.145.m: This truth of the supreme [deity], equal to nectar, is to be known; the thousand-rayed Sun is beneficial for people. / Understanding this conduct of the sages as the essence of reality, those whose minds are freed from delusion attain liberation.

1.145.s:
idaṃ magānāṃ caritaṃ mayā te prakhyāpitaṃ yānavareṇa yuktam .
jñātvātvimaṃ mokṣavido vadanti siddhāśca tatsthānamavāpnuvanti ..25
1.145.d:
इदं मगानां चरितं मया ते प्रख्यापितं यानवरेण युक्तम् ।
ज्ञात्वात्विमं मोक्षविदो वदन्ति सिद्धाश्च तत्स्थानमवाप्नुवन्ति ॥25
1.145.m: This conduct of the Magas has been proclaimed by me to you, endowed with the foremost vehicle. / Having known this, the knowers of liberation speak [of it], and the perfected ones attain that state.

1.145.s:
yanmayoktamidaṃ jñānaṃ deyaṃ śraddhāvatāṃ nṛṇām .
nāstikānāmabuddhīnāṃ na deyaṃ bhūtimicchatā ..26
1.145.d:
यन्मयोक्तमिदं ज्ञानं देयं श्रद्धावतां नृणाम् ।
नास्तिकानामबुद्धीनां न देयं भूतिमिच्छता ॥26
1.145.m: This knowledge declared by me should be given to faithful men; / one who desires prosperity should not give it to atheists or the unintelligent.

1.145.s:
sumanturuvāca
ityuktvā bhagavānvyāso bhojakajñānamuttamam .
nārāyaṇaṃ mahābāho jagāmāyatanaṃ hareḥ ..27
1.145.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्व्यासो भोजकज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
नारायणं महाबाहो जगामायतनं हरेः ॥27
1.145.m: Sumantu said: / Having thus spoken the supreme knowledge of the Bhojakas, the blessed Vyāsa, / O mighty-armed one, went to the hermitage of Nārāyaṇa, the abode of Hari,

1.145.s:
khyāto yastriṣu lokeṣu gaṃgayā paritoṣitaḥ .
badaryā maṇḍito vīra naranārāyaṇāśramaḥ . . 28
1.145.d:
ख्यातो यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु गंगया परितोषितः ।
बदर्या मण्डितो वीर नरनारायणाश्रमः ॥ 28
1.145.m: which is renowned in the three worlds, made joyful by the Gaṅgā, / and adorned with jujube trees, O hero: the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

1.145.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe bhojakajñānavarṇanaṃ
nāma pañcacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 145 .
bhojakavarṇanam
1.145.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे भोजकज्ञानवर्णनं
नाम पञ्चचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 145 ।
भोजकवर्णनम्
1.145.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-fifth chapter, entitled "Description of the Knowledge of the Bhojakas," in the section on the Seventh Lunar Day, in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Bhojakas

1.146.s:
śatānīka uvāca
ya ete bhojakāḥ proktā devadevasya pūjakāḥ .
nānyaṃ bhojyamathaiteṣāṃ brāhmaṇaiśca kadācana . . 1
1.146.d:
शतानीक उवाच
य एते भोजकाः प्रोक्ता देवदेवस्य पूजकाः ।
नान्यं भोज्यमथैतेषां ब्राह्मणैश्च कदाचन ॥ 1
1.146.m: Śatānīka said: / These who are proclaimed as Bhojakas, the worshipers of the god of gods— / [is it true that] food from them is never to be eaten by brahmins?

1.146.s:
bhāskarasya priyā hyete pūjyatvaṃ ca tathā gatāḥ .
divyāścaite smṛtā viprā ādityāmbhaḥ samudbhavāḥ . . 2
1.146.d:
भास्करस्य प्रिया ह्येते पूज्यत्वं च तथा गताः ।
दिव्याश्चैते स्मृता विप्रा आदित्याम्भः समुद्भवाः ॥ 2
1.146.m: For they are dear to Bhāskara and have likewise attained worshipfulness; / these twice-born are remembered as divine, born from the waters of the Sun.

1.146.s:
abhojyatvaṃ kathaṃ yātā bhojakāstadvadasva me .
kiṃ kurvāṇāstathā karma bhojyatāṃ yānti me vada . . 3
1.146.d:
अभोज्यत्वं कथं याता भोजकास्तद्वदस्व मे ।
किं कुर्वाणास्तथा कर्म भोज्यतां यान्ति मे वद ॥ 3
1.146.m: How have the Bhojakas fallen into being those whose food cannot be eaten? Tell me that. / Performing what work do they become those whose food may be eaten? Tell me.

1.146.s:
sumanturuvāca
imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭo vāsudevo mahīpate .
kṛtavarmaṇā purā rājaṃstathā sāmbo mahābalaḥ . . 4
1.146.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
इममर्थं पुरा पृष्टो वासुदेवो महीपते ।
कृतवर्मणा पुरा राजंस्तथा साम्बो महाबलः ॥ 4
1.146.m: Sumantu said: / Concerning this matter, Vāsudeva was questioned in ancient times, O protector of the earth, / by Kṛtavarman of old, O king, and likewise by the mighty Sāmba.

1.146.s:
gatau sāmbapurīṃ vīra tathā nāradaparvatau .
bhuktavanto gṛhe sarve bhojakasya mahātmanaḥ . . 5
1.146.d:
गतौ साम्बपुरीं वीर तथा नारदपर्वतौ ।
भुक्तवन्तो गृहे सर्वे भोजकस्य महात्मनः ॥ 5
1.146.m: Having gone to Sāmbapurī, O hero, both Nārada and Parvata / ate in the house of the high-souled Bhojaka.

1.146.s:
ādityakarmaṇo loke devānnakhyātimāgatāḥ .
tena te pūjitāḥ sarve bhaktyā bhojyairanekaśaḥ . . 6
1.146.d:
आदित्यकर्मणो लोके देवान्नख्यातिमागताः ।
तेन ते पूजिताः सर्वे भक्त्या भोज्यैरनेकशः ॥ 6
1.146.m: By virtue of their solar rite, they had attained fame in the world as having divine food; / therefore, they were all honored with devotion through various foods.

1.146.s:
āgatāste purīṃ vīra puṇyāṃ dvāravatīṃ vibhoḥ .
tāvṛṣī divamāruḍhau rājannāradaparvatau . 7
1.146.d:
आगतास्ते पुरीं वीर पुण्यां द्वारवतीं विभोः ।
तावृषी दिवमारुढौ राजन्नारदपर्वतौ । 7
1.146.m: They arrived, O hero, at the lord's holy city of Dvāravatī, / and those two sages, O king, Nārada and Parvata, ascended to heaven.

1.146.s:
vāsudevaṃ mahātejā hārdikyo vākyamabravīt .
ya ete bhojakā vipra pūjakā bhāskarasya tu . . 8
1.146.d:
वासुदेवं महातेजा हार्दिक्यो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
य एते भोजका विप्र पूजका भास्करस्य तु ॥ 8
1.146.m: The descendant of Hṛdīka, endowed with great splendor, spoke these words to Vāsudeva: / "These who are Bhojaka brahmins, worshipers of Bhāskara—

1.146.s:
annameṣāṃ kathaṃ viprau bhuktavantau janārdana .
tāvṛṣī divyamākhyātau yau tau nāradaparvatau . .
abhojyāḥ kila ete vai brāhmaṇānāṃ janārdana . . 9
1.146.d:
अन्नमेषां कथं विप्रौ भुक्तवन्तौ जनार्दन ।
तावृषी दिव्यमाख्यातौ यौ तौ नारदपर्वतौ ॥
अभोज्याः किल एते वै ब्राह्मणानां जनार्दन ॥ 9
1.146.m: how did those two brahmins eat their food, O Janārdana, / those two sages renowned as divine, namely Nārada and Parvata? / For it is said that they are indeed those whose food must not be eaten by brahmins, O Janārdana."

1.146.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
na te bhojyā mahābāho bhojyā bhojāśca sarvadā .
abhivādyāṃ prayatnena yathādityo mahāmate . . 1.146.10
1.146.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
न ते भोज्या महाबाहो भोज्या भोजाश्च सर्वदा ।
अभिवाद्यां प्रयत्नेन यथादित्यो महामते ॥ 1.146.10
1.146.m: Vāsudeva said: / "They are not those whose food is forbidden, O mighty-armed one; they are always those whose food may be eaten, and they are Bhojas. / They are to be saluted with effort, just like the Sun, O great-minded one."

1.146.s:
ācarantaśra tatkarma bhojyatvaṃ pravajanti te .
tacchrūyatāṃ yaduśreṣṭha yatkāryaṃ cāpi tairvibho . .
yatamānairmahābāho tadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu . . 11
1.146.d:
आचरन्तश्र तत्कर्म भोज्यत्वं प्रवजन्ति ते ।
तच्छ्रूयतां यदुश्रेष्ठ यत्कार्यं चापि तैर्विभो ॥
यतमानैर्महाबाहो तदिहैकमनाः शृणु ॥ 11
1.146.m: Performing that duty, they attain the status of those whose food may be eaten. / Hear, O best of the Yadus, what is also to be done by them, O lord; / as they strive, O mighty-armed one, listen to that here with an attentive mind:

1.146.s:
vṛṣalī yasya vai bhāryā yaścāvyaṅgaṃ na dhārayet .
abhojyaḥ sa tu vijñeyo bhojako nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 12
1.146.d:
वृषली यस्य वै भार्या यश्चाव्यङ्गं न धारयेत् ।
अभोज्यः स तु विज्ञेयो भोजको नात्र संशयः ॥ 12
1.146.m: He whose wife is a Śūdra woman, and who does not wear an avyaṅga, / should be known as one whose food may not be eaten; he is a Bhojaka, without a doubt.

1.146.s:
asnātaḥ pūjayedyastu tathābhyaṅgavivarjitaḥ .
ādityaṃ yaduśārdūla tathā ca vidhinā vibho . . 13
1.146.d:
अस्नातः पूजयेद्यस्तु तथाभ्यङ्गविवर्जितः ।
आदित्यं यदुशार्दूल तथा च विधिना विभो ॥ 13
1.146.m: He who, unbathed and devoid of the avyaṅga, / should worship Āditya, O tiger among the Yadus, and [not] according to the rule, O lord;

1.146.s:
sevako bhojako yastu śūdrānnaṃ yena bhujyate .
kṛṣiṃ ca kurute yastu devārcāmapi varjayet . . 14
1.146.d:
सेवको भोजको यस्तु शूद्रान्नं येन भुज्यते ।
कृषिं च कुरुते यस्तु देवार्चामपि वर्जयेत् ॥ 14
1.146.m: or the Bhojaka who is a servant, by whom the food of a Śūdra is eaten, / who practices agriculture, or neglects the worship of the deity;

1.146.s:
jātakarmādayo yasya na saṃskārāḥ kṛtā vibho .
āruṇeyaiśca mantraiśca sāvitrīṃ na ca vai paṭhet . .
tasya gehe dvijo bhuktvā kṛcchrapādena śudhyati . . 15
1.146.d:
जातकर्मादयो यस्य न संस्काराः कृता विभो ।
आरुणेयैश्च मन्त्रैश्च सावित्रीं न च वै पठेत् ॥
तस्य गेहे द्विजो भुक्त्वा कृच्छ्रपादेन शुध्यति ॥ 15
1.146.m: for whom the life-cycle rites beginning with the birth-rite have not been performed, O lord, / and who does not recite the Sāvitrī with the Āruṇeya mantras— / by eating in his house, a twice-born is purified by a quarter-kṛcchra.

1.146.s:
pitṛdevamanuṣyāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhāskarasya tu .
akṛtvā vidhivatpūjāṃ yastu bhuṅkte sa dharmahā . . 16
1.146.d:
पितृदेवमनुष्याणां भूतानां भास्करस्य तु ।
अकृत्वा विधिवत्पूजां यस्तु भुङ्क्ते स धर्महा ॥ 16
1.146.m: He who eats without having properly performed the worship / of the ancestors, gods, men, spirits, and Bhāskara, destroys dharma.

1.146.s:
abhyaṅgena vihīno yaḥ śaṃkhahīnastathaiva ca .
śirasā dhārayetkeśānsa jñeyo bhojakādhamaḥ . . 17
1.146.d:
अभ्यङ्गेन विहीनो यः शंखहीनस्तथैव च ।
शिरसा धारयेत्केशान्स ज्ञेयो भोजकाधमः ॥ 17
1.146.m: He who is destitute of the avyaṅga and likewise destitute of the conch, / and bears long hair on his head, is to be known as the lowest of Bhojakas.

1.146.s:
devārcanaṃ tathā homaṃ snānaṃ tarpaṇameva ca .
dānaṃ brāhmaṇapūjāṃ ca kurvato bhojakasya tu . .
abhyaṅgena vihīnasya sarvaṃ bhavati niṣphalam . . 18
1.146.d:
देवार्चनं तथा होमं स्नानं तर्पणमेव च ।
दानं ब्राह्मणपूजां च कुर्वतो भोजकस्य तु ॥
अभ्यङ्गेन विहीनस्य सर्वं भवति निष्फलम् ॥ 18
1.146.m: When a Bhojaka destitute of the avyaṅga / performs the worship of the gods, fire offerings, bathing, libations, / gift-giving, and the veneration of Brahmins, / all of it becomes fruitless.

1.146.s:
sarvadevamayo hyeṣa sarvavedamayastathā .
abhyaṅgo yaduśārdūla pavitraḥ paramaḥ smṛtaḥ . . 19
1.146.d:
सर्वदेवमयो ह्येष सर्ववेदमयस्तथा ।
अभ्यङ्गो यदुशार्दूल पवित्रः परमः स्मृतः ॥ 19
1.146.m: For this [avyaṅga] consists of all the gods and likewise consists of all the Vedas; / the avyaṅga, O tiger among the Yadus, is traditionally held to be the supreme purifier.

1.146.s:
bhojakānāṃ yaduśreṣṭha tasya mūle sthito hariḥ .
madhye brahmā mahātejā agre gośrutibhūṣaṇaḥ . . 1.146.20
1.146.d:
भोजकानां यदुश्रेष्ठ तस्य मूले स्थितो हरिः ।
मध्ये ब्रह्मा महातेजा अग्रे गोश्रुतिभूषणः ॥ 1.146.20
1.146.m: For the Bhojakas, O best of the Yadus, Hari resides at its root, / Brahmā of great splendour in the middle, and at the tip the one adorned with the bull and the Veda.

1.146.s:
ṛgvedo yasya mūlastho madhye sāmāni kṛtsnaśaḥ .
yajurvedastathā śreṣṭhaścātharvasahitaḥ sthitaḥ . . 21
1.146.d:
ऋग्वेदो यस्य मूलस्थो मध्ये सामानि कृत्स्नशः ।
यजुर्वेदस्तथा श्रेष्ठश्चाथर्वसहितः स्थितः ॥ 21
1.146.m: The Ṛgveda stands at its root, in the middle the Sāmans entirely, / and the supreme Yajurveda stands together with the Atharva[veda].

1.146.s:
trayo'gnayastathā rājaṃstrayo lokāḥ sthitāḥ kramāt .
evameva pavitrastu abhyaṅgo bhojakasya tu . . 22
1.146.d:
त्रयोऽग्नयस्तथा राजंस्त्रयो लोकाः स्थिताः क्रमात् ।
एवमेव पवित्रस्तु अभ्यङ्गो भोजकस्य तु ॥ 22
1.146.m: The three fires likewise, O king, and the three worlds stand in order; / thus indeed the avyaṅga is a sacred purifier for a Bhojaka.

1.146.s:
yastvanena vihīnastu bhojako bhojakādhamaḥ .
abhojyaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ so'śucirnātra saṃśayaḥ . . 23
1.146.d:
यस्त्वनेन विहीनस्तु भोजको भोजकाधमः ।
अभोज्यः स तु विज्ञेयः सोऽशुचिर्नात्र संशयः ॥ 23
1.146.m: A Bhojaka who is destitute of this is the lowest of Bhojakas; / he should be known as one whose food may not be eaten; he is impure, there is no doubt.

1.146.s:
nirmālyamatha naivedyaṃ kuṅkumaṃ devahelinām .
ye prayacchanti śūdrāṇāṃ vikrīṇanti ca bhojakāḥ . .
te'dhamā bhojakā jñeyā ye ca devasvahāriṇaḥ . . 24
1.146.d:
निर्माल्यमथ नैवेद्यं कुङ्कुमं देवहेलिनाम् ।
ये प्रयच्छन्ति शूद्राणां विक्रीणन्ति च भोजकाः ॥
तेऽधमा भोजका ज्ञेया ये च देवस्वहारिणः ॥ 24
1.146.m: Those Bhojakas who give over to Śūdras or sell / the leftover offerings, food offerings, and saffron to those who scorn the gods, / are to be known as vile Bhojakas, as well as those who seize the property of the god.

1.146.s:
na pūjayanti deveśaṃ devasvaṃ kṣapayanti ca .
na te deva priyāstāta vijñeyā bhojakādhamāḥ . . 25
1.146.d:
न पूजयन्ति देवेशं देवस्वं क्षपयन्ति च ।
न ते देव प्रियास्तात विज्ञेया भोजकाधमाः ॥ 25
1.146.m: They do not worship the lord of the gods and waste the god's property; / they are not dear to the god, my dear, and are to be recognized as the lowest of Bhojakas.

1.146.s:
yasminna bhukte naivedyaṃ bhojako'śnāti mānada .
tadannaṃ bhuṅjatastasya narakāya na śāntaye . . 26
1.146.d:
यस्मिन्न भुक्ते नैवेद्यं भोजकोऽश्नाति मानद ।
तदन्नं भुङ्जतस्तस्य नरकाय न शान्तये ॥ 26
1.146.m: In whose house a Bhojaka eats before the food offering is eaten, O giver of honour, / for him who eats that food it leads to hell, not to peace.

1.146.s:
naivedyaṃ bhojayettasmādbhāskarasya naraḥ sadā .
prathamaṃ yaduśārdūla tacca dehaviśodhanam . . 27
1.146.d:
नैवेद्यं भोजयेत्तस्माद्भास्करस्य नरः सदा ।
प्रथमं यदुशार्दूल तच्च देहविशोधनम् ॥ 27
1.146.m: Therefore, a person should always feed the food offering of Bhāskara / first, O tiger among the Yadus, for that purifies the body.

1.146.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ puroḍāśo yathā kāyaviśodhanaḥ .
bhojakānāṃ tathā vīra naivedyaṃ kāyaśodhanam . . 28
1.146.d:
ब्राह्मणानां पुरोडाशो यथा कायविशोधनः ।
भोजकानां तथा वीर नैवेद्यं कायशोधनम् ॥ 28
1.146.m: Just as the sacrificial cake is the purifier of the body for Brahmins, / so the food offering, O hero, is the purifier of the body for Bhojakas.

1.146.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sāmbopākhyāne bhojakavarṇanaṃ
nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 146 .
bhojakabrāhmaṇavarṇanam
1.146.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे साम्बोपाख्याने भोजकवर्णनं
नाम षट्चत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 146 ।
भोजकब्राह्मणवर्णनम्
1.146.m:
Thus, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the context of the Saptamī Kalpa, in the narrative of Sāmba, the one hundred forty-sixth chapter, named "Description of the Bhojakas."
Description of the Bhojaka Brahmins.

1.147.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
atra pṛṣṭo yathā devo bhāskaro devapūjitaḥ .
aruṇena mahābāho ke priyā bhojakāstathā . . 1
1.147.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
अत्र पृष्टो यथा देवो भास्करो देवपूजितः ।
अरुणेन महाबाहो के प्रिया भोजकास्तथा ॥ 1
1.147.m: Vāsudeva said: / In this regard, as the god Bhāskara, worshipped by the gods, / was asked by Aruṇa, O mighty-armed one: "Which Bhojakas are dear to you,

1.147.s:
pūjāyāṃ tava ke yogyāḥ ke na yogyā bhavanti ca .
iti pṛṣṭaḥ sa bhagavānaruṇena divākaraḥ . .
yaduvāca mahābāho tadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu . . 2
1.147.d:
पूजायां तव के योग्याः के न योग्या भवन्ति च ।
इति पृष्टः स भगवानरुणेन दिवाकरः ॥
यदुवाच महाबाहो तदिहैकमनाः शृणु ॥ 2
1.147.m: and who are fit for your worship, and who are not fit?" / Having been thus questioned by Aruṇa, what the divine maker of day / spoke, O mighty-armed one, listen to that here with an attentive mind.

1.147.s:
bhāskara uvāca
paradārānparadravyaṃ ye na hiṃsanti bhojakāḥ .
te priyā mama vai nityaṃ ye na niṃdanti daivatān . . 3
1.147.d:
भास्कर उवाच
परदारान्परद्रव्यं ये न हिंसन्ति भोजकाः ।
ते प्रिया मम वै नित्यं ये न निंदन्ति दैवतान् ॥ 3
1.147.m: Bhāskara said: / Those Bhojakas who do not violate another's wife or another's wealth, / and who do not revile the deities, are always dear to me.

1.147.s:
vāṇijyaṃ kṛṣisevāṃ tu vedānāṃ nindanaṃ ca ye .
kurvanti bhojakā jñeyāḥ sarve te mama vairiṇaḥ . . 4
1.147.d:
वाणिज्यं कृषिसेवां तु वेदानां निन्दनं च ये ।
कुर्वन्ति भोजका ज्ञेयाः सर्वे ते मम वैरिणः ॥ 4
1.147.m: Those Bhojakas who engage in trade, the service of agriculture, / and the reviling of the Vedas are all to be known as my enemies.

1.147.s:
yeṣāṃ bhāryāsaṅgrahaṇaṃ karṣaṇaṃ ye prakurvate .
nṛpasevāṃ khagaśreṣṭha vijñeyāḥ patitāstu te . .
bhuñjate ye ca śūdrānnaṃ jñeyāste śatravo mama . . 5
1.147.d:
येषां भार्यासङ्ग्रहणं कर्षणं ये प्रकुर्वते ।
नृपसेवां खगश्रेष्ठ विज्ञेयाः पतितास्तु ते ॥
भुञ्जते ये च शूद्रान्नं ज्ञेयास्ते शत्रवो मम ॥ 5
1.147.m: Those who commit adultery, who practice ploughing, / or who serve kings, O best of birds, are to be known as fallen; / and those who eat the food of Śūdras are to be known as my foes.

1.147.s:
pūjā kṛtā tu yā taistu tathārghyaṃ ca khagottama .
pūjāṃ tāmatha cāpyarghyaṃ nāhaṃ gṛhṇāmi khecara . . 6
1.147.d:
पूजा कृता तु या तैस्तु तथार्घ्यं च खगोत्तम ।
पूजां तामथ चाप्यर्घ्यं नाहं गृह्णामि खेचर ॥ 6
1.147.m: The worship performed by them, as well as the water offering, O best of birds— / that worship and that water offering I do not accept, O sky-wanderer.

1.147.s:
ya ete kathitā vīra ye ca śaṅkhavivarjitāḥ .
nirmālyaṃ ye madīyaṃ tu naivedyaṃ kuṅkumaṃ tathā . . 7
1.147.d:
य एते कथिता वीर ये च शङ्खविवर्जिताः ।
निर्माल्यं ये मदीयं तु नैवेद्यं कुङ्कुमं तथा ॥ 7
1.147.m: Those who have been mentioned, O hero, and those who are destitute of the conch, / and who give my leftover offerings, food offerings, and saffron

1.147.s:
śūdrāya ye prayacchanti vikīrṇanti ca ye khaga .
yacchanti ye ca vaiśyāya bhojakā me na te priyāḥ . . 8
1.147.d:
शूद्राय ये प्रयच्छन्ति विकीर्णन्ति च ये खग ।
यच्छन्ति ये च वैश्याय भोजका मे न ते प्रियाः ॥ 8
1.147.m: to a Śūdra, or who sell them, O bird, / or who give them to a Vaiśya—those Bhojakas are not dear to me;

1.147.s:
yajante ye ca sāvitrīṃ mahāśvetāṃ ca gopateḥ .
ye na jānanti me mudrāṃ kiṅkarāṇāṃ ca nāmataḥ . . 9
1.147.d:
यजन्ते ये च सावित्रीं महाश्वेतां च गोपतेः ।
ये न जानन्ति मे मुद्रां किङ्कराणां च नामतः ॥ 9
1.147.m: and those who worship Sāvitrī and Mahāśvetā of the lord of cattle, / and do not know my mudrā and my attendants by name.

1.147.s:
ya ete1 kathitā vīra bhojakāste mayā khaga .
naite pūjayituṃ śaktā ye priyā mama bhojakāḥ . .
tāñchṛṇuṣva khagaśreṣṭha bhūtvā caikāgramānasaḥ . . 1.147.10
1.147.d:
य एते1 कथिता वीर भोजकास्ते मया खग ।
नैते पूजयितुं शक्ता ये प्रिया मम भोजकाः ॥
ताञ्छृणुष्व खगश्रेष्ठ भूत्वा चैकाग्रमानसः ॥ 1.147.10
1.147.m: These Bhojakas who have been declared by me, O hero, O bird— / they are not capable of worshipping [me]. As for those Bhojakas who are dear to me, / listen to them, O best of birds, becoming one-pointed in mind.

1.147.s:
devadvijamanuṣyāṇāṃ pitṝṇāṃ cāpi pūjakāḥ .
te priyā mama vai nityaṃ śaktāḥ pūjayituṃ ravim . . 11
1.147.d:
देवद्विजमनुष्याणां पितॄणां चापि पूजकाः ।
ते प्रिया मम वै नित्यं शक्ताः पूजयितुं रविम् ॥ 11
1.147.m: Those who worship gods, twice-borns, humans, and ancestors / are constantly dear to me; they are capable of worshipping the sun.

1.147.s:
yeṣāṃ muṇḍaṃ śiro nityaṃ ye cābhyaṅgasamanvitāḥ .
vādayanti ca ye śaṅkhaṃ divyāste bhojakā matāḥ . . 12
1.147.d:
येषां मुण्डं शिरो नित्यं ये चाभ्यङ्गसमन्विताः ।
वादयन्ति च ये शङ्खं दिव्यास्ते भोजका मताः ॥ 12
1.147.m: Those whose heads are always shaved, who are endowed with the avyaṅga, / and who blow the conch—they are regarded as divine Bhojakas.

1.147.s:
trikālaṃ ye ca māṃ nityaṃ susnātāḥ krodhavarjitāḥ .
pūjayanti khagaśreṣṭha te priyā mama bhojakāḥ . . 13
1.147.d:
त्रिकालं ये च मां नित्यं सुस्नाताः क्रोधवर्जिताः ।
पूजयन्ति खगश्रेष्ठ ते प्रिया मम भोजकाः ॥ 13
1.147.m: Those who, well-bathed and free from anger, constantly worship me / at the three junctures of the day, O best of birds, are the Bhojakas dear to me.

1.147.s:
vāre madīye naktaṃ tu ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ye ca prakurvate .
saptamyāmupavāsaṃ tu tathā saṅkramaṇe mama . . 14
1.147.d:
वारे मदीये नक्तं तु षष्ठ्यां ये च प्रकुर्वते ।
सप्तम्यामुपवासं तु तथा सङ्क्रमणे मम ॥ 14
1.147.m: Those who take a nocturnal meal on my day [Sunday], on the sixth lunar day, / and fast on the seventh lunar day and on my transit,

1.147.s:
divyāste brāhmaṇā jñeyā bhojakā mama pūjakāḥ .
pūjayanti ca ye viprānmadbhaktā matparāyaṇāḥ . .
te priyāḥ satataṃ mahyaṃ bhojakā garuḍāgraja . . 15
1.147.d:
दिव्यास्ते ब्राह्मणा ज्ञेया भोजका मम पूजकाः ।
पूजयन्ति च ये विप्रान्मद्भक्ता मत्परायणाः ॥
ते प्रियाः सततं मह्यं भोजका गरुडाग्रज ॥ 15
1.147.m: are to be known as divine Brahmins, Bhojakas who worship me. / And those who, devoted to me and intent on me, worship Brahmins— / those Bhojakas, O elder brother of Garuḍa, are always dear to me.

1.147.s:
mayi bhaktiṃ na kurvanti brāhmaṇānpūjayanti no .
na te pūjyā na vandyāśca ye dviṣanti ca māṃ sadā . . 16
1.147.d:
मयि भक्तिं न कुर्वन्ति ब्राह्मणान्पूजयन्ति नो ।
न ते पूज्या न वन्द्याश्च ये द्विषन्ति च मां सदा ॥ 16
1.147.m: Those who do not show devotion to me, do not venerate Brahmins, / and always hate me are neither to be worshipped nor revered.

1.147.s:
ye kurvanti mahāyajñānbhojakā garuḍāgraja .
pitṛdevamanuṣyāṇāṃ pūjārthaṃ santataṃ khaga . . 17
1.147.d:
ये कुर्वन्ति महायज्ञान्भोजका गरुडाग्रज ।
पितृदेवमनुष्याणां पूजार्थं सन्ततं खग ॥ 17
1.147.m: Those Bhojakas, O elder brother of Garuḍa, who continually perform the great sacrifices / for the worship of the ancestors, gods, and men, O bird,

1.147.s:
priyāste satataṃ vīra bhojakānāṃ tathottamāḥ .
tasmātsarvaprayatnena pañcayajñānpravartayet . . 18
1.147.d:
प्रियास्ते सततं वीर भोजकानां तथोत्तमाः ।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन पञ्चयज्ञान्प्रवर्तयेत् ॥ 18
1.147.m: are always dear [to me], O hero, and are the best of Bhojakas. / Therefore, with all effort one should conduct the five sacrifices.

1.147.s:
ekabhaktena ye nityaṃ vartante kaśyapātmaja .
bhuñjate na ca ye rātrau bhojakāste priyā mama . . 19
1.147.d:
एकभक्तेन ये नित्यं वर्तन्ते कश्यपात्मज ।
भुञ्जते न च ये रात्रौ भोजकास्ते प्रिया मम ॥ 19
1.147.m: Those Bhojakas who constantly subsist on a single meal, O son of Kaśyapa, / and who do not eat at night, are dear to me.

1.147.s:
mama vāre ca ye vīra tathā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca keśava .
na rātrau bhuñjate prājñā matpriyāste magāḥ khaga . . 1.147.20
1.147.d:
मम वारे च ये वीर तथा षष्ठ्यां च केशव ।
न रात्रौ भुञ्जते प्राज्ञा मत्प्रियास्ते मगाः खग ॥ 1.147.20
1.147.m: And those wise Magas, O hero, who do not eat at night on my day / and on the sixth lunar day, O Keśava, O bird, are dear to me.

1.147.s:
pratisaṃvatsaraṃ ye tu bhojakā garuḍāgraja .
na yacchanti piturmāturdivase tena me priyāḥ . . 21
1.147.d:
प्रतिसंवत्सरं ये तु भोजका गरुडाग्रज ।
न यच्छन्ति पितुर्मातुर्दिवसे तेन मे प्रियाः ॥ 21
1.147.m: Those Bhojakas, O elder brother of Garuḍa, who do not [neglect to] give / every year on the day of the father and the mother, are therefore dear to me.

1.147.s:
itthaṃ bhūtā bhojakā yā māghamāse ca saptamī .
puṣpāṇāṃ karavīrāṇi tathā raktaṃ ca candanam . . 22
1.147.d:
इत्थं भूता भोजका या माघमासे च सप्तमी ।
पुष्पाणां करवीराणि तथा रक्तं च चन्दनम् ॥ 22
1.147.m:
Such are the Bhojakas. And on the saptamī in the month of Māgha,
among flowers, oleanders, as well as red sandalwood;

1.147.s:
vācako brāhmaṇānāṃ tu naivedyaṃ modakāstathā .
ghṛtāhutyo guggulaśca kṣīreṇa snapanaṃ tathā . . 23
1.147.d:
वाचको ब्राह्मणानां तु नैवेद्यं मोदकास्तथा ।
घृताहुत्यो गुग्गुलश्च क्षीरेण स्नपनं तथा ॥ 23
1.147.m:
a reciter among Brahmins; and modakas as food-offering;
oblations of ghee, bdellium incense, and bathing with milk;

1.147.s:
vādyānāṃ śaṅkhaśabdaśca nṛtyaṃ nāṭyaṃ mataṃ mama .
pañcavarṇā patākāstu śvetaṃ chatraṃ ca me priyam . . 24
1.147.d:
वाद्यानां शङ्खशब्दश्च नृत्यं नाट्यं मतं मम ।
पञ्चवर्णा पताकास्तु श्वेतं छत्रं च मे प्रियम् ॥ 24
1.147.m:
among musical instruments, the sound of the conch; and dancing and drama are my delight.
Five-coloured pennants and a white royal parasol are dear to me.

1.147.s:
nānyavarṇaiḥ kṛtā pūjā tathā prīṇāti māṃ khaga .
yathā kṛtā bhojakena pūjā prīṇāti māṃ sadā . .
nānyadevapratiṣṭhā tu kartavyā bhojakena tu . . 25
1.147.d:
नान्यवर्णैः कृता पूजा तथा प्रीणाति मां खग ।
यथा कृता भोजकेन पूजा प्रीणाति मां सदा ॥
नान्यदेवप्रतिष्ठा तु कर्तव्या भोजकेन तु ॥ 25
1.147.m:
Worship performed by other castes does not please me, O bird,
as worship performed by a Bhojaka always pleases me.
Moreover, installation [of the image] of no other deity must be performed by a Bhojaka.

1.147.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
ityuktvā bhagavāndevaścāruṇāya purānagha .
lakṣaṇaṃ bhojakānāṃ tu tato merumathākramat . . 26
1.147.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्देवश्चारुणाय पुरानघ ।
लक्षणं भोजकानां तु ततो मेरुमथाक्रमत् ॥ 26
1.147.m:
Vāsudeva said:
Having spoken thus to Aruṇa in the past, O sinless one,
about the characteristic marks of the Bhojakas, the lordly god then ascended Mount Meru.

1.147.s:
evaṃ bhojyā bhojakāstu na cābhojyāḥ kadācana .
anuṣṭhānavihīnā ye na te bhojyāstu bhojakāḥ . . 27
1.147.d:
एवं भोज्या भोजकास्तु न चाभोज्याः कदाचन ।
अनुष्ठानविहीना ये न ते भोज्यास्तु भोजकाः ॥ 27
1.147.m:
Thus the Bhojakas are fit to be fed, and never unfit to be fed;
[yet] those Bhojakas who are devoid of proper religious observance are not fit to be fed.

1.147.s:
bhaumāstu brāhmaṇā ye tu anuṣṭhānavivarjitāḥ .
te'pyabhojyā bhavantīha vikarmasthā viśeṣataḥ . . 28
1.147.d:
भौमास्तु ब्राह्मणा ये तु अनुष्ठानविवर्जिताः ।
तेऽप्यभोज्या भवन्तीह विकर्मस्था विशेषतः ॥ 28
1.147.m:
Even Brahmins of the earth who are devoid of proper religious observance
become unfit to be fed here, especially those engaged in improper conduct.

1.147.s:
nāsti pūjyatamaṃ kiñcinmāṅgalyaṃ pāvanaṃ tathā .
caturṇāmiha varṇānāṃ muktvā bhojakamuttamam . .
pūjite bhojake vīra ādityaḥ pūjito bhavet . . 29
1.147.d:
नास्ति पूज्यतमं किञ्चिन्माङ्गल्यं पावनं तथा ।
चतुर्णामिह वर्णानां मुक्त्वा भोजकमुत्तमम् ॥
पूजिते भोजके वीर आदित्यः पूजितो भवेत् ॥ 29
1.147.m:
There is nothing more worthy of worship, auspicious, and purifying
for the four castes here than the excellent Bhojaka.
When a Bhojaka is worshipped, O hero, the Sun becomes worshipped.

1.147.s:
bhuñjate yasya vai gehe bhojakā yadunaṃdana .
tasya bhuṅkte svayaṃ bhānurbrahmā viṣṇustathā śivaḥ . . 1.147.30
1.147.d:
भुञ्जते यस्य वै गेहे भोजका यदुनंदन ।
तस्य भुङ्क्ते स्वयं भानुर्ब्रह्मा विष्णुस्तथा शिवः ॥ 1.147.30
1.147.m:
In whose house the Bhojakas eat, O joy of the Yadus,
in his [house] the Sun himself eats, as do Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.

1.147.s:
yatheha sarvasattvānāṃ pradhānatve sthito raviḥ .
tatheha sarvabhūtānāṃ bhojakaḥ pūjya ucyate . . 31
1.147.d:
यथेह सर्वसत्त्वानां प्रधानत्वे स्थितो रविः ।
तथेह सर्वभूतानां भोजकः पूज्य उच्यते ॥ 31
1.147.m:
Just as the Sun stands pre-eminent among all living beings here,
so the Bhojaka is declared worthy of worship among all creatures here.

1.147.s:
tīrthānāṃ tu kurukṣetraṃ sarasāṃ sāgaro yathā .
tathā pūjyatamo jñeyaḥ pūjyānāṃ bhojako vibho . . 32
1.147.d:
तीर्थानां तु कुरुक्षेत्रं सरसां सागरो यथा ।
तथा पूज्यतमो ज्ञेयः पूज्यानां भोजको विभो ॥ 32
1.147.m:
Just as Kurukṣetra is foremost among sacred fords, and the ocean among lakes,
so the Bhojaka should be known as the most worthy of worship among the venerable, O lord.

1.147.s:
viśeṣeṇa ca saurāṇāṃ bhojakaḥ pūjya ucyate .
bhartā pūjyo yayā strīṇāṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ ca yathā guruḥ . .
bhojakastu tathā pūjyaḥ saurāṇāṃ hṛdikātmaja . . 33
1.147.d:
विशेषेण च सौराणां भोजकः पूज्य उच्यते ।
भर्ता पूज्यो यया स्त्रीणां शिष्याणां च यथा गुरुः ॥
भोजकस्तु तथा पूज्यः सौराणां हृदिकात्मज ॥ 33
1.147.m:
And particularly for Sauras, the Bhojaka is declared worthy of worship.
As a husband is worthy of worship for wives, and a guru for disciples,
so the Bhojaka is worthy of worship for Sauras, O son of Hṛdīka.

1.147.s:
yasya bhuṅkte bhojakastu gandhapuṣpādinārcitaḥ .
tasya bhuṅkte svayaṃ bhānuḥ pitaro devatāstathā . . 34
1.147.d:
यस्य भुङ्क्ते भोजकस्तु गन्धपुष्पादिनार्चितः ।
तस्य भुङ्क्ते स्वयं भानुः पितरो देवतास्तथा ॥ 34
1.147.m:
In whose [house] a Bhojaka eats after being honoured with scents, flowers, and the like,
in his [house] the Sun himself eats, as do the ancestors and the gods.

1.147.s:
evaṃ pūjyāstathā bhojyā bhojakā hṛdikātmaja .
ye saurā bhojakasyānnaṃ bhuñjate nirvikalpataḥ . .
te sarve pāpanirmuktā yānti sūryasalokatām . . 35
1.147.d:
एवं पूज्यास्तथा भोज्या भोजका हृदिकात्मज ।
ये सौरा भोजकस्यान्नं भुञ्जते निर्विकल्पतः ॥
ते सर्वे पापनिर्मुक्ता यान्ति सूर्यसलोकताम् ॥ 35
1.147.m:
Thus, O son of Hṛdīka, Bhojakas are worthy of worship and fit to be fed.
Those Sauras who eat the food of a Bhojaka without hesitation,
all of them, freed from sin, attain the world of Sūrya.

1.147.s:
kathito yatra yo bhojyo yathā bhojyaḥ sa varjitaḥ .
atha kiṃ bahunoktena śrūyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama . . 36
1.147.d:
कथितो यत्र यो भोज्यो यथा भोज्यः स वर्जितः ।
अथ किं बहुनोक्तेन श्रूयतां वचनं मम ॥ 36
1.147.m:
Where and who is fit to be fed has been told, as well as who is fit to be fed, and who is excluded.
Now what is the use of speaking much? Let my word be heard:

1.147.s:
nāsti vedātparaṃ śāstraṃ nāsti gaṅgāsamā sarit .
aśvamedhasamaṃ puṇyaṃ nāsti putrasamaṃ sukham . . 37
1.147.d:
नास्ति वेदात्परं शास्त्रं नास्ति गङ्गासमा सरित् ।
अश्वमेधसमं पुण्यं नास्ति पुत्रसमं सुखम् ॥ 37
1.147.m:
There is no scripture higher than the Veda; there is no river equal to the Gaṅgā;
there is no merit equal to the horse sacrifice; there is no happiness equal to a son;

1.147.s:
nāsti bhānusamo devo nāsti mātṛsamā gatiḥ .
yathaitāni samastāni uttamāni yadūttama ..
tathottamo bhojakastu samprokto bhāskareṇa tu . . 38
kālacakravarṇanam
1.147.d:
नास्ति भानुसमो देवो नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः ।
यथैतानि समस्तानि उत्तमानि यदूत्तम ॥
तथोत्तमो भोजकस्तु सम्प्रोक्तो भास्करेण तु ॥ 38
कालचक्रवर्णनम्
1.147.m:
there is no god equal to the Sun; there is no refuge equal to a mother.
Just as all these are supreme, O best of the Yadus,
so the Bhojaka has been proclaimed supreme by the Sun.
Description of the Wheel of Time

1.148.s:
sumanturuvāca
adha sāmbo mahātejā dṛṣṭvā cakraṃ pituḥ kare .
jvālāmālākarālaṃ tu mahatā tejasānvitam . . 1
1.148.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
अध साम्बो महातेजा दृष्ट्वा चक्रं पितुः करे ।
ज्वालामालाकरालं तु महता तेजसान्वितम् ॥ 1
1.148.m:
Sumantu said:
Then Sāmba of great splendour, seeing the discus in his father's hand,
terrific with a garland of flames and endowed with great brilliance,

1.148.s:
papraccha pitaraṃ sāmbo bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
kutastāta tvayā prāptaṃ cakramādityasannibham . . 2
1.148.d:
पप्रच्छ पितरं साम्बो भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
कुतस्तात त्वया प्राप्तं चक्रमादित्यसन्निभम् ॥ 2
1.148.m:
Sāmba asked his father with devotion, filled with faith:
"From where, father, did you obtain this discus resembling the Sun?

1.148.s:
kimarthaṃ vahate deva divyamāyudhamuttamam .
etadākhyāhi me sarvaṃ śrotukāmasya1 kautukāt . . 3
1.148.d:
किमर्थं वहते देव दिव्यमायुधमुत्तमम् ।
एतदाख्याहि मे सर्वं श्रोतुकामस्य1 कौतुकात् ॥ 3
1.148.m:
For what purpose, O god, do you carry this supreme celestial weapon?
Explain all this to me, who am eager to hear out of curiosity."

1.148.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
sādhusādhu2 mahābāho sādhu pṛṣṭosmya'haṃ tvayā .
śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ putra cakrasya vidhinirṇayam . .4
1.148.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
साधुसाधु2 महाबाहो साधु पृष्टोस्म्यऽहं त्वया ।
शृणुष्वैकमनाः पुत्र चक्रस्य विधिनिर्णयम् ॥4
1.148.m:
Vāsudeva said:
"Excellent, excellent, O mighty-armed one! You have questioned me well.
Listen with a single-minded focus, my son, to the definitive explanation of the discus.

1.148.s:
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu bhānumārādhya śraddhayā .
prāptaṃ cakraṃ mayā tasmādbhāskarāllokapūjitāt . .5
1.148.d:
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं तु भानुमाराध्य श्रद्धया ।
प्राप्तं चक्रं मया तस्माद्भास्कराल्लोकपूजितात् ॥5
1.148.m:
Having worshipped the Sun with faith for a celestial thousand years,
the discus was obtained by me from that Sun, honoured by the world.

1.148.s:
nabhogaḥ pañcakārūḍhaḥ sthitaḥ sākṣāddivākaraḥ .
grahāḥ somādayo yasya saṃsthitā nābhimaṇḍale . . 6
1.148.d:
नभोगः पञ्चकारूढः स्थितः साक्षाद्दिवाकरः ।
ग्रहाः सोमादयो यस्य संस्थिता नाभिमण्डले ॥ 6
1.148.m:
Moving in the sky, mounted on the five [elements], the Sun is present manifest [in it];
the planets, the Moon and others, reside upon its hub.

1.148.s:
ādityā dvādaśa samā areṣu kramaśastathā .
proktaṃ pathiṣu tattvāni pṛthivyādīni yāni vai . .7
1.148.d:
आदित्या द्वादश समा अरेषु क्रमशस्तथा ।
प्रोक्तं पथिषु तत्त्वानि पृथिव्यादीनि यानि वै ॥7
1.148.m:
The twelve Ādityas are equally placed in order upon its spokes;
the principles, beginning with earth, are declared to be on its felly-tracks.

1.148.s:
etaistattvaiḥ parivyāptaṃ cakraṃ kālātmakaṃ param .
saṃkṣepātte mayākhyātaṃ dattaṃ cakramivāparam . . 8
1.148.d:
एतैस्तत्त्वैः परिव्याप्तं चक्रं कालात्मकं परम् ।
संक्षेपात्ते मयाख्यातं दत्तं चक्रमिवापरम् ॥ 8
1.148.m:
The supreme wheel of time is completely pervaded by these principles.
It has been described in brief to you by me, given as if it were a second discus.

1.148.s:
sāmba uvāca
kathaṃ kālamayaṃ deva cakraṃ kamalamucyate .
idaṃ tāvanmamācakṣva jñātumicchāmi tattvataḥ . . 9
1.148.d:
साम्ब उवाच
कथं कालमयं देव चक्रं कमलमुच्यते ।
इदं तावन्ममाचक्ष्व ज्ञातुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥ 9
1.148.m:
Sāmba said:
How, O god, is the wheel consisting of time called a lotus?
First explain this to me; I wish to understand it in truth.

1.148.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
kamalaṃ hyṛtubhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ ṣaṭdalaṃ cākṣayāśritam .
puruṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ taddhi tatra sāṅgo raviḥ sthitaḥ . . 1.148.10
1.148.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
कमलं ह्यृतुभिः षड्भिः षट्दलं चाक्षयाश्रितम् ।
पुरुषाधिष्ठितं तद्धि तत्र साङ्गो रविः स्थितः ॥ 1.148.10

1.148.s:
yacca kālatrayaṃ loke tannābhitrayamucyate .
māsā arā mahābāho pakṣāśca pradhayaḥ smṛtāḥ . . 11
1.148.d:
यच्च कालत्रयं लोके तन्नाभित्रयमुच्यते ।
मासा अरा महाबाहो पक्षाश्च प्रधयः स्मृताः ॥ 11
1.148.m:
And what is the threefold time in the world, that is called its three hubs;
the months are the spokes, O mighty-armed one, and the fortnights are remembered as the felly-bands.

1.148.s:
nemī caiva pare prokte ayane dakṣiṇottare .
pathinābhiṣu yoge ca yogākhyāstapanādibhiḥ . . 12
1.148.d:
नेमी चैव परे प्रोक्ते अयने दक्षिणोत्तरे ।
पथिनाभिषु योगे च योगाख्यास्तपनादिभिः ॥ 12
1.148.m:
The two rims, moreover, are declared to be the southern and northern solstices.
In the conjunction upon the paths and hubs are those known as Yogas, beginning with Tapana and others.

1.148.s:
nakṣatrāṇi grahāścaiva sadā cātra sthitāḥ smṛtāḥ .
etairvyāptamidaṃ cakraṃ sthūlasūkṣmaprabhedataḥ . . 13
1.148.d:
नक्षत्राणि ग्रहाश्चैव सदा चात्र स्थिताः स्मृताः ।
एतैर्व्याप्तमिदं चक्रं स्थूलसूक्ष्मप्रभेदतः ॥ 13
1.148.m:
The lunar mansions and the planets are also remembered as always residing here;
this wheel is pervaded by them through gross and subtle distinctions.

1.148.s:
atroddiṣṭeṣu kāleṣu ye noddiṣṭā mayā tava .
yugādikalpaparyantāste'pi cātra sthitāḥ kramāt . . 14
1.148.d:
अत्रोद्दिष्टेषु कालेषु ये नोद्दिष्टा मया तव ।
युगादिकल्पपर्यन्तास्तेऽपि चात्र स्थिताः क्रमात् ॥ 14
1.148.m:
Among the divisions of time designated here, those which I have not mentioned to you,
ranging from the beginnings of yugas to kalpas, they too are placed here in succession.

1.148.s:
yatte kālātmakaṃ cakramidaṃ saṃkṣepato mayā .
kathitaṃ tadviniṣkrāntaṃ pradīptātsūryamaṇḍalāt . . 15
1.148.d:
यत्ते कालात्मकं चक्रमिदं संक्षेपतो मया ।
कथितं तद्विनिष्क्रान्तं प्रदीप्तात्सूर्यमण्डलात् ॥ 15
1.148.m:
This wheel consisting of time, which has been described in brief to you by me,
issued forth from the blazing solar orb.

1.148.s:
asurāṇāṃ vadhāyedaṃ mayā labdhaṃ divākarāt .
ārādhya tapasā sūryaṃ purā kalpe jagadgurum . .
ataḥ sampūjyayāmyenaṃ grahaistattvairvṛtaṃ sadā . . 16
1.148.d:
असुराणां वधायेदं मया लब्धं दिवाकरात् ।
आराध्य तपसा सूर्यं पुरा कल्पे जगद्गुरुम् ॥
अतः सम्पूज्ययाम्येनं ग्रहैस्तत्त्वैर्वृतं सदा ॥ 16
1.148.m:
For the slaying of the asuras, this was obtained by me from the Sun,
having worshipped the Sun, the teacher of the universe, with austerity in a previous kalpa.
Therefore, I continually worship this [discus] encircled by planets and principles.

1.148.s:
arkaṃ bhakto hi cakrasthaṃ yaḥ pūjayati bhaktimān .
tejasā ravisaṃkāśaḥ puṣpottarapuraṃ vrajet . . 17
1.148.d:
अर्कं भक्तो हि चक्रस्थं यः पूजयति भक्तिमान् ।
तेजसा रविसंकाशः पुष्पोत्तरपुरं व्रजेत् ॥ 17
1.148.m:
For that devoted worshipper who worships the Sun residing in the wheel,
resembling the Sun in splendour, he goes to the city of Puṣpottara.

1.148.s:
tasmāttaṃ matkulānandaṃ mitraṃ sampūjayāmyaham .
grahaistattvairvṛtaṃ bhaktyā svamantraiḥ satataṃ vibhum . . 18
1.148.d:
तस्मात्तं मत्कुलानन्दं मित्रं सम्पूजयाम्यहम् ।
ग्रहैस्तत्त्वैर्वृतं भक्त्या स्वमन्त्रैः सततं विभुम् ॥ 18
1.148.m:
Therefore, with devotion I continually worship that Mitra, the joy of my lineage, the omnipresent lord,
encircled by the planets and principles, with his own mantras.

1.148.s:
saptamyāṃ cakramālikhya ye yajanti divākaram .
raktacandanapūrṇena kuṃkumena sugaṃdhinā . . 19
1.148.d:
सप्तम्यां चक्रमालिख्य ये यजन्ति दिवाकरम् ।
रक्तचन्दनपूर्णेन कुंकुमेन सुगंधिना ॥ 19
1.148.m:
Those who, having drawn the wheel on the saptamī, worship the Sun
with saffron fragrant and full of red sandalwood,

1.148.s:
piṣṭagandhādibhirvāpi raktavarṇakamiśrakaiḥ .
raktaiśca kamalaiḥ śuddhaiḥ karavīraiḥ sugandhibhiḥ . . 1.148.20
1.148.d:
पिष्टगन्धादिभिर्वापि रक्तवर्णकमिश्रकैः ।
रक्तैश्च कमलैः शुद्धैः करवीरैः सुगन्धिभिः ॥ 1.148.20
1.148.m:
or with ground perfumes and the like mixed with red colour,
and with pure red lotuses and fragrant oleanders,

1.148.s:
anyairvā kusumairvanyaiḥ pratyagrairjantuvarjitaiḥ .
aparyuṣitaniśchidraiḥ śubhadhanyairdalairapi . . 21
1.148.d:
अन्यैर्वा कुसुमैर्वन्यैः प्रत्यग्रैर्जन्तुवर्जितैः ।
अपर्युषितनिश्छिद्रैः शुभधन्यैर्दलैरपि ॥ 21
1.148.m:
or with other wild flowers, fresh and free of vermin,
not stale, free from holes, and with auspicious, fortunate leaves,

1.148.s:
phalaiḥ pakvairoṣadhibhistathā dūrvāṅkuraiḥ kuśaiḥ .
dhūpaiśca vividhairgandhaistathā vastraiśca bhūṣaṇaiḥ . . 22
1.148.d:
फलैः पक्वैरोषधिभिस्तथा दूर्वाङ्कुरैः कुशैः ।
धूपैश्च विविधैर्गन्धैस्तथा वस्त्रैश्च भूषणैः ॥ 22
1.148.m:
with ripe fruits, medicinal herbs, and likewise with sprouts of dūrvā and kuśa grass,
and with various kinds of incense, scents, garments, and ornaments—

1.148.s:
bhakṣyairbhojyaiśca peyaiśca coṣyairlehyaiśca śaktitaḥ .
vitānaśobhāsikataiḥ palāśairupaśobhitaiḥ . . 23
1.148.d:
भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैश्च पेयैश्च चोष्यैर्लेह्यैश्च शक्तितः ।
वितानशोभासिकतैः पलाशैरुपशोभितैः ॥ 23
1.148.m: With chewable food, meals, drinks, foods to be sucked, and licking foods, according to capacity, / adorned with white sand showing off awnings, [and] with palāśa leaves,

1.148.s:
chatracāmaraghaṇṭābhirbhūṣaṇairdarpaṇādibhiḥ .
nṛtyavāditragītaiśca vedaiḥ puṇyakathāsvanaiḥ . . 24
1.148.d:
छत्रचामरघण्टाभिर्भूषणैर्दर्पणादिभिः ।
नृत्यवादित्रगीतैश्च वेदैः पुण्यकथास्वनैः ॥ 24
1.148.m: with royal parasols, chowries, bells, ornaments, mirrors, and so forth, / with dance, instruments, songs, the Vedas, and the sounds of holy stories,

1.148.s:
sarvatra jayaghoṣaiśca sampūrṇe pūjayanti ye .
sampūrṇānvividhānkāmānnirvighnānprāpnuvanti te . . 25
1.148.d:
सर्वत्र जयघोषैश्च सम्पूर्णे पूजयन्ति ये ।
सम्पूर्णान्विविधान्कामान्निर्विघ्नान्प्राप्नुवन्ति ते ॥ 25
1.148.m: and with shouts of victory on all sides, when [the cycle] is complete, those who worship [thus], / they attain complete desires of diverse kinds, without obstacles.

1.148.s:
svacakraṃ cāpi nirvighnaṃ vṛddhimāyāti suvrata .
hanyate paracakraṃ ca yatredaṃ pūjyate sakṛt . . 26
1.148.d:
स्वचक्रं चापि निर्विघ्नं वृद्धिमायाति सुव्रत ।
हन्यते परचक्रं च यत्रेदं पूज्यते सकृत् ॥ 26
1.148.m: And one's own realm flourishes without obstacle, O true-vowed one; / and an enemy's realm is crushed where this is worshipped even once.

1.148.s:
saṅkrāntau grahaṇe cāpi likhitvā yo japedidam .
bhavanti niyatāḥ sāmba tasya sānugrahā grahāḥ . . 27
1.148.d:
सङ्क्रान्तौ ग्रहणे चापि लिखित्वा यो जपेदिदम् ।
भवन्ति नियताः साम्ब तस्य सानुग्रहा ग्रहाः ॥ 27
1.148.m: Having inscribed this, whoever recites it at an equinox/solstice or eclipse, / for him, O Sāmba, the planets become unfailingly benevolent.

1.148.s:
sarvarogavihīnastu sarvaduḥkhavivarjitaḥ .
ciraṃ jīvati dharmātmā sarvaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ . . 28
1.148.d:
सर्वरोगविहीनस्तु सर्वदुःखविवर्जितः ।
चिरं जीवति धर्मात्मा सर्वैश्वर्यसमन्वितः ॥ 28
1.148.m: Freed from all diseases and abandoned by all sorrow, / the righteous man lives long, endowed with all sovereign power.

1.148.s:
eṣa vai kathito vatsa cakrayogo mayā tava .
arkasya sarvayajñānāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ siddhiprado bhṛśam . . 29
1.148.d:
एष वै कथितो वत्स चक्रयोगो मया तव ।
अर्कस्य सर्वयज्ञानां श्रेष्ठं सिद्धिप्रदो भृशम् ॥ 29
1.148.m: Truly this wheel-discipline has been declared by me to you, my child, / the best among all sacrifices to the Sun, granting success in abundance.

1.148.s:
puṇyo dharmastathā puṣṭyaḥ śatrughnaśca viśeṣataḥ .
śveto rakto'tha pītaśca kṛṣṇaścāpi vibhāgaśaḥ . . 1.148.30
1.148.d:
पुण्यो धर्मस्तथा पुष्ट्यः शत्रुघ्नश्च विशेषतः ।
श्वेतो रक्तोऽथ पीतश्च कृष्णश्चापि विभागशः ॥ 1.148.30
1.148.m: It is meritorious, righteous, bringing prosperity, and especially destroys foes; / [it has] white, red, yellow, and black sections by division.

1.148.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sāmbopākhyāne kālacakravarṇanaṃ
nāmāṣṭacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 148 .
sūryadīkṣāvarṇanam
1.148.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे साम्बोपाख्याने कालचक्रवर्णनं
नामाष्टचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 148 ।
सूर्यदीक्षावर्णनम्
1.148.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-eighth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Wheel of Time," in the narrative of Sāmba, in the Kalpa of the Seventh, in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Solar Initiation

1.149.s:
sāmba uvāca
kiṃ pramāṇaṃ likheccakraṃ tatra padmaṃ ca kiṃ bhavet .
nemipradhyāranābhīnāṃ vibhāgaḥ kriyate katham . . 1
1.149.d:
साम्ब उवाच
किं प्रमाणं लिखेच्चक्रं तत्र पद्मं च किं भवेत् ।
नेमिप्रध्यारनाभीनां विभागः क्रियते कथम् ॥ 1
1.149.m: Sāmba said: / What measure should one draw the wheel, and what should be the lotus upon it? / How is the division of the rim, felly, spokes, and hub made?

1.149.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
catuḥṣaṣṭyaṅgulaṃ cakraṃ kṛtvā vṛttaṃ pramāṇataḥ .
aṣṭāṅgulā bhavennemiḥ seyaṃ vibhavataḥ sadā . . 2
1.149.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
चतुःषष्ट्यङ्गुलं चक्रं कृत्वा वृत्तं प्रमाणतः ।
अष्टाङ्गुला भवेन्नेमिः सेयं विभवतः सदा ॥ 2
1.149.m: Vāsudeva said: / Having made a wheel sixty-four digits [in diameter], circular according to measure, / the rim should be eight digits, depending on the means at hand, always.

1.149.s:
nābhikṣetraṃ tathaiva syātpadmaṃ tattriguṇaṃ bhavet .
arakṣetraṃ ca padmasya kaṇikākesarāṇi ca . . 3
1.149.d:
नाभिक्षेत्रं तथैव स्यात्पद्मं तत्त्रिगुणं भवेत् ।
अरक्षेत्रं च पद्मस्य कणिकाकेसराणि च ॥ 3
1.149.m: The space of the hub should be just the same; the lotus should be threefold that. / And the area of the spokes of the lotus, the pericarp, and the filaments,

1.149.s:
kesarasya ca pādena śeṣapatrāṇi kalpayet .
patrasandhiśca pādāṅgaṃ kramāttatrāpi bhidyate . .4
1.149.d:
केसरस्य च पादेन शेषपत्राणि कल्पयेत् ।
पत्रसन्धिश्च पादाङ्गं क्रमात्तत्रापि भिद्यते ॥4
1.149.m: and one-fourth of the filament should be set aside for the remaining petals. / And the junction of the petals is a fourth part; there too it is differentiated in order.

1.149.s:
unnataṃ kamalaṃ tattu kuryānnābhyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
ākīrṇāḥ saṃvibhaktāśca kartavyāḥ pradhayaḥ kramāt . .5
1.149.d:
उन्नतं कमलं तत्तु कुर्यान्नाभ्यां न संशयः ।
आकीर्णाः संविभक्ताश्च कर्तव्याः प्रधयः क्रमात् ॥5
1.149.m: One should fashion that lotus raised upon the hub, no doubt; / the fellies should be made densely set and well-proportioned in succession.

1.149.s:
aṅgulasthūlamūlaṃ syādarāgraṃ triguṇaṃ tataḥ .
bhūmiḥ pītā bahirjñeyā karṇikākesarāṇi ca . . 6
1.149.d:
अङ्गुलस्थूलमूलं स्यादराग्रं त्रिगुणं ततः ।
भूमिः पीता बहिर्ज्ञेया कर्णिकाकेसराणि च ॥ 6
1.149.m: The base should be one digit thick; the tip of the spoke threefold that. / The ground outside is to be known as yellow, as well as the pericarp and the filaments.

1.149.s:
sitaṃ nābhisthalaṃ tatra dvārāṇi parikalpayet .
hastamātraṃ bhavettasya tanmānaṃ dvārasannibham . .7
1.149.d:
सितं नाभिस्थलं तत्र द्वाराणि परिकल्पयेत् ।
हस्तमात्रं भवेत्तस्य तन्मानं द्वारसन्निभम् ॥7
1.149.m: The site of the hub is white; there one should fashion doors. / Its measure should be a cubit, corresponding to the door.

1.149.s:
śeṣaṃ raktaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ saṃhatāḥ patrasandhayaḥ .
nābhinemyantare lekhāḥ sitāścāṅgulamānataḥ . . 8
1.149.d:
शेषं रक्तं समुद्दिष्टं संहताः पत्रसन्धयः ।
नाभिनेम्यन्तरे लेखाः सिताश्चाङ्गुलमानतः ॥ 8
1.149.m: The remainder is indicated as red; the junctions of the petals are joined. / Between the hub and the rim are white lines, measuring one digit.

1.149.s:
sitaraktasitābhiśca samantādupaśobhitam .
kapolaṃ dvārapadmaṃ ca dvārakoṇe prakalpayet . . 9
1.149.d:
सितरक्तसिताभिश्च समन्तादुपशोभितम् ।
कपोलं द्वारपद्मं च द्वारकोणे प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 9
1.149.m: And adorned all around with white, red, and white lines, / one should fashion the door-wing and the door-lotus at the corner of the door.

1.149.s:
caturdvāraṃ bhavedevamaindradvāraṃ prakalpayet .
aparāhṇe'tha pūrvāhṇe varuṇamāvāhayetsadā . . 1.149.10
1.149.d:
चतुर्द्वारं भवेदेवमैन्द्रद्वारं प्रकल्पयेत् ।
अपराह्णेऽथ पूर्वाह्णे वरुणमावाहयेत्सदा ॥ 1.149.10
1.149.m: Thus it should have four doors; one should fashion the eastern door. / In the afternoon and the forenoon, one should always invoke Varuṇa.

1.149.s:
dvārāṇyetāni saṃvartya yathoktavidhinā yajet .
yathoktā devatāḥ sarvāḥ svamantraireva bhaktitaḥ . . 1 1
cakramevaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ yajanārthaṃ mayā tava .
yajñenānena sambaddho dīkṣitaścārkamaṇḍale . .
itthaṃ me bhānunā pūrvamidamuktaṃ varānana . . 12
1.149.d:
द्वाराण्येतानि संवर्त्य यथोक्तविधिना यजेत् ।
यथोक्ता देवताः सर्वाः स्वमन्त्रैरेव भक्तितः ॥ 1 1
चक्रमेवं समुद्दिष्टं यजनार्थं मया तव ।
यज्ञेनानेन सम्बद्धो दीक्षितश्चार्कमण्डले ॥
इत्थं मे भानुना पूर्वमिदमुक्तं वरानन ॥ 12
1.149.m: Having enclosed these doors, one should worship according to the prescribed rite, / all the deities as spoken with their own mantras in devotion. / Thus the wheel was declared by me to you for the sake of worship. / Linked by this sacrifice, one is initiated in the solar orb; / so this was spoken to me formerly by the Sun, O handsome one.

1.149.s:
sāmba uvāca
ke mantrāścakrayajñe'smindevatānāṃ prakīrtitāḥ .
yajñakramaśca kaḥ prokto rūpaṃ kiṃ ca pṛthakpṛthak . . 13
1.149.d:
साम्ब उवाच
के मन्त्राश्चक्रयज्ञेऽस्मिन्देवतानां प्रकीर्तिताः ।
यज्ञक्रमश्च कः प्रोक्तो रूपं किं च पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 13
1.149.m: Sāmba said: / Which mantras are proclaimed for the deities in this wheel-sacrifice? / And what is taught as the sequence of the sacrifice, and what are their individual forms?

1.149.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
khaṣolkaṃ hadayādhyakṣaṃ pūrvokte kamale yajet .
karṇikāyāṃ daleṣvevamaṅgāni hṛdayādi ca . . 14
1.149.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
खषोल्कं हदयाध्यक्षं पूर्वोक्ते कमले यजेत् ।
कर्णिकायां दलेष्वेवमङ्गानि हृदयादि च ॥ 14
1.149.m: Vāsudeva said: / One should worship Khaṣolka, the presiding deity of the heart, upon the previously mentioned lotus, / in the pericarp, and likewise the limbs—the heart and the rest—upon the petals.

1.149.s:
nāmamantrāścaturthyaṃtāsteṣāṃ pūrvoktakoṭayaḥ .
namaskāraśca sarvatra eṣa eva vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ . . 15
1.149.d:
नाममन्त्राश्चतुर्थ्यंतास्तेषां पूर्वोक्तकोटयः ।
नमस्कारश्च सर्वत्र एष एव विधिः स्मृतः ॥ 15
1.149.m: Their name-mantras end in the dative case; there are the previously stated millions of them. / And an obeisance (namaḥ) is [added] everywhere; this is remembered as the rule.

1.149.s:
svāhāntā homakāle ca karmasvanyeṣu te punaḥ .
yathā karmāvasānāśca prayoktavyāḥ samāsataḥ . . 16
1.149.d:
स्वाहान्ता होमकाले च कर्मस्वन्येषु ते पुनः ।
यथा कर्मावसानाश्च प्रयोक्तव्याः समासतः ॥ 16
1.149.m: They end in svāhā at the time of the fire oblation; and in other rituals, / they should be applied according to the conclusion of the ritual, briefly stated:

1.149.s:
oṃ khaṣolkāya vidmahe divākarāya dhīmahi .
tannaḥ sūryaḥ pracodayāt . . 17
1.149.d:
ओं खषोल्काय विद्महे दिवाकराय धीमहि ।
तन्नः सूर्यः प्रचोदयात् ॥ 17
1.149.m: "Oṃ, we know Khaṣolka; we meditate upon the Maker of the Day. / May the Sun impel us toward that."

1.149.s:
sāvitrī ca mahābāho caturviṃśākṣarā matā .
sarvatattvamayī puṇyā brahmagotrārkavallabhā . . 18
1.149.d:
सावित्री च महाबाहो चतुर्विंशाक्षरा मता ।
सर्वतत्त्वमयी पुण्या ब्रह्मगोत्रार्कवल्लभा ॥ 18
1.149.m: And the Sāvitrī [verse] is taught as having twenty-four syllables, O mighty-armed one; / consisting of all cosmic principles, holy, belonging to the lineage of Brahman, beloved of the Sun.

1.149.s:
evaṃ mantrāḥ prayoktavyāḥ sarvakarmasvataṃdritaiḥ .
anyathā viphalaṃ karma bhavediha paratra ca . . 19
1.149.d:
एवं मन्त्राः प्रयोक्तव्याः सर्वकर्मस्वतंद्रितैः ।
अन्यथा विफलं कर्म भवेदिह परत्र च ॥ 19
1.149.m: Thus the mantras should be employed with untiring attention in all rites; / otherwise, the rite would become fruitless here and in the hereafter.

1.149.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena mantrāñjñātvā vidhiṃ tathā .
yathāvatkarma tatkṛtvā sādhayedīpsitaṃ phalam . . 1.149.20
1.149.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन मन्त्राञ्ज्ञात्वा विधिं तथा ।
यथावत्कर्म तत्कृत्वा साधयेदीप्सितं फलम् ॥ 1.149.20
1.149.m: Therefore, having known the mantras and the rite with every effort, / performing that rite properly, one achieves the desired fruit.

1.149.s:
sāmba uvāca
ādityamaṇḍale dīkṣā kasya kāryā kathaṃ ca sā .
kadā kena kimarthaṃ ca kathayedaṃ mamākhilam . . 21
1.149.d:
साम्ब उवाच
आदित्यमण्डले दीक्षा कस्य कार्या कथं च सा ।
कदा केन किमर्थं च कथयेदं ममाखिलम् ॥ 21
1.149.m: Sāmba said: / For whom is initiation into the solar orb to be performed, and how is it done? / When, by whom, and for what purpose? Tell me all this.

1.149.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vaiśyaṃ kulīnaṃ śūdrameva ca .
puruṣaṃ vā striyaṃ vāpi dīkṣayetsūryamaṇḍale . . 22
1.149.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
ब्राह्मणं क्षत्रियं वैश्यं कुलीनं शूद्रमेव च ।
पुरुषं वा स्त्रियं वापि दीक्षयेत्सूर्यमण्डले ॥ 22
1.149.m: Vāsudeva said: / A Brahmin, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, or a Śūdra of good family, / whether a man or a woman, one should initiate into the solar orb.

1.149.s:
svayaṃ bhaktyopapannaśca praṇipatya guruṃ tathā .
gurustaṃ dīkṣayedvipraḥ kalpajñaḥ satyavākchuciḥ . . 23
1.149.d:
स्वयं भक्त्योपपन्नश्च प्रणिपत्य गुरुं तथा ।
गुरुस्तं दीक्षयेद्विप्रः कल्पज्ञः सत्यवाक्छुचिः ॥ 23
1.149.m: Endowed with devotion of his own accord, having bowed down to the guru, / the guru, a Brahmin who knows the ritual, who speaks the truth and is pure, should initiate him.

1.149.s:
ṣaṣṭhyāmagniṃ samādhāya pūrvoktavidhinā kramāt .
sampūjyārkaṃ tathā vahnau hutvā vai haviṣā ravim . . 24
1.149.d:
षष्ठ्यामग्निं समाधाय पूर्वोक्तविधिना क्रमात् ।
सम्पूज्यार्कं तथा वह्नौ हुत्वा वै हविषा रविम् ॥ 24
1.149.m: Having established the fire on the sixth lunar day according to the rule previously stated, in succession, / and having worshipped the Sun, having offered oblations into the fire to the Sun with sacrificial butter,

1.149.s:
śiṣyaṃ snātamathācāntaṃ khaṣolkākṛtivigraham .
svāṅgairālabhya cāṅgeṣu darbhavadbhistathākṣataiḥ . . 25
1.149.d:
शिष्यं स्नातमथाचान्तं खषोल्काकृतिविग्रहम् ।
स्वाङ्गैरालभ्य चाङ्गेषु दर्भवद्भिस्तथाक्षतैः ॥ 25
1.149.m: the disciple, bathed and having sipped water, his body assumed the form of Khaṣolka, / touching [him] on his limbs with his own limbs, with darbha grass and whole grains of rice,

1.149.s:
puṣpaiḥ sampūjya cāṅgāni deyaḥ kāryo balistathā .
ādityo varuṇo'rko'gniḥ sādhito hṛdayena ca . . 26
1.149.d:
पुष्पैः सम्पूज्य चाङ्गानि देयः कार्यो बलिस्तथा ।
आदित्यो वरुणोऽर्कोऽग्निः साधितो हृदयेन च ॥ 26
1.149.m: and having worshipped his limbs with flowers, the offering is to be made. / Āditya, Varuṇa, Arka, and Agni are invoked with the heart [mantra].

1.149.s:
bhaved ghṛtaguḍakṣīraistandulaiśca1 pramāṇataḥ .
tribhirañjalibhirhutvā devāyāgnau hutaṃ punaḥ . . 27
1.149.d:
भवेद् घृतगुडक्षीरैस्तन्दुलैश्च1 प्रमाणतः ।
त्रिभिरञ्जलिभिर्हुत्वा देवायाग्नौ हुतं पुनः ॥ 27
1.149.m: It should be done with ghee, jaggery, milk, and rice in measured quantity; / having offered into the fire for the deity with three palmfuls, an oblation is made again.

1.149.s:
