dattvā śiṣṭāya muktvaivaṃ dattvānte dantadhāvanam .
kṣīraṃ vṛkṣodbhavaṃ tasmai dvādaśāṅgulasannibham . . 28
1.149.d:
दत्त्वा शिष्टाय मुक्त्वैवं दत्त्वान्ते दन्तधावनम् ।
क्षीरं वृक्षोद्भवं तस्मै द्वादशाङ्गुलसन्निभम् ॥ 28
1.149.m: Having given [it] to the remaining one, releasing [him] thus, having given at the end a tooth-stick, / [and] milk produced from a tree, measuring twelve digits,

1.149.s:
dantaśliṣṭe'panīte ca tena prācyāṃ kṣipettataḥ .
dantadhāvanamāsyaṃ ca tadā tasyopari kṣipet . . 29
1.149.d:
दन्तश्लिष्टेऽपनीते च तेन प्राच्यां क्षिपेत्ततः ।
दन्तधावनमास्यं च तदा तस्योपरि क्षिपेत् ॥ 29
1.149.m: and when the particles sticking to the teeth are removed, he should then throw it toward the east; / then he should throw water on the tooth-stick above it.

1.149.s:
maitrāvāruṇamīśānaṃ vakraṃ saumyasamāśritam .
praśastaṃ dantakāṣṭhasya mukhamanyatra ninditam . . 1.149.30
1.149.d:
मैत्रावारुणमीशानं वक्रं सौम्यसमाश्रितम् ।
प्रशस्तं दन्तकाष्ठस्य मुखमन्यत्र निन्दितम् ॥ 1.149.30
1.149.m: The tip of the tooth-stick facing north-west, north-east, curved, or leaning toward the north, / is praised; in any other direction it is condemned.

1.149.s:
yāṃ diśaṃ dantakāṣṭhasya mukhaṃ paśyati tatpatim .
arcayettena śāṃtiḥ syādityuktaṃ bhānunā svayam . . 31
1.149.d:
यां दिशं दन्तकाष्ठस्य मुखं पश्यति तत्पतिम् ।
अर्चयेत्तेन शांतिः स्यादित्युक्तं भानुना स्वयम् ॥ 31
1.149.m: The direction in which the tip of the tooth-stick faces, one should worship the lord of that [direction]; / peace will result through that—thus it was spoken by the Sun himself.

1.149.s:
punastadvacanaṃ śrutvā aṅgairālabhya ca kramāt .
sampūjya locane tatra sañciṃtya parijapya ca . . 32
1.149.d:
पुनस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा अङ्गैरालभ्य च क्रमात् ।
सम्पूज्य लोचने तत्र सञ्चिंत्य परिजप्य च ॥ 32
1.149.m: Having heard his instruction again, and touching [him] with the limbs in order, / having worshipped the eyes there, having meditated and murmured [the mantra],

1.149.s:
kārayitvā ca saṅkalpaṃ tathā cendriyasaṃyamam .
sthāpayeta svayaṃ cāpi varaṃ śrutvā samāhitaḥ . . 33
1.149.d:
कारयित्वा च सङ्कल्पं तथा चेन्द्रियसंयमम् ।
स्थापयेत स्वयं चापि वरं श्रुत्वा समाहितः ॥ 33
1.149.m: and having made him form the ritual intention and likewise restrain his senses, / he should establish [him], himself also composed, having listened to the blessing.

1.149.s:
ācamya kṛtarakṣastu kṛtadravyādhivāsanaḥ .
hadayena nametprātaḥ snātvā hutvā hutāśanam . . 34
1.149.d:
आचम्य कृतरक्षस्तु कृतद्रव्याधिवासनः ।
हदयेन नमेत्प्रातः स्नात्वा हुत्वा हुताशनम् ॥ 34
1.149.m: Having sipped water, having performed the protective rite, and having consecrated the ritual items, / in the morning, having bathed and offered into the fire, he should bow with the heart [mantra].

1.149.s:
svapnaṃ pṛcchedyathā dṛṣṭaṃ śubhaṃ saṃvādayecca tam .
hadayenāśubhe dṛṣṭe śatahomaṃ samācaret . . 35
1.149.d:
स्वप्नं पृच्छेद्यथा दृष्टं शुभं संवादयेच्च तम् ।
हदयेनाशुभे दृष्टे शतहोमं समाचरेत् ॥ 35
1.149.m: He should ask about the dream as it was seen, and confirm it if auspicious. / If an inauspicious one is seen, he should perform a hundred oblations with the hṛdaya-mantra.

1.149.s:
svapne paśyati harmyāṇi devatānāṃ hutāśanam .
nadīyānāni ramyāṇi udyānopavanāni ca . . 36
1.149.d:
स्वप्ने पश्यति हर्म्याणि देवतानां हुताशनम् ।
नदीयानानि रम्याणि उद्यानोपवनानि च ॥ 36
1.149.m: If in a dream he sees palaces of the gods, fire, / pleasant river-boats, and parks and gardens,

1.149.s:
patrapuṣpaphalāḍhyāni kamalāni ca rājatam .
sampaśyati yadi svapne brāhmaṇaṃ vedapāragam . . 37
1.149.d:
पत्रपुष्पफलाढ्यानि कमलानि च राजतम् ।
सम्पश्यति यदि स्वप्ने ब्राह्मणं वेदपारगम् ॥ 37
1.149.m: abundant leaves, flowers, and fruits, lotuses, silver, / [or] if in a dream he sees a brāhmaṇa who has mastered the Vedas,

1.149.s:
rājānaṃ śauryasampannaṃ dhanāḍhyaṃ kṣatriyottamam .
śuśrūṣaṇaparaṃ śūdraṃ yadi tattvārthamādiśet . . 38
1.149.d:
राजानं शौर्यसम्पन्नं धनाढ्यं क्षत्रियोत्तमम् ।
शुश्रूषणपरं शूद्रं यदि तत्त्वार्थमादिशेत् ॥ 38
1.149.m: a king endowed with valor, a wealthy, foremost kṣatriya, / or a śūdra devoted to service, if one would indicate true meaning,

1.149.s:
praśastaṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ caiva yathāsambhavato matam .
etaiḥ sparśanameteṣāṃ śreṣṭhamārohaṇaṃ tataḥ . . 39
1.149.d:
प्रशस्तं भाषणं चैव यथासम्भवतो मतम् ।
एतैः स्पर्शनमेतेषां श्रेष्ठमारोहणं ततः ॥ 39
1.149.m: and conversation [with them] is considered praiseworthy, as far as possible; / touching them is good, and mounting [them] is even better than that.

1.149.s:
vāhanāni praśastāni prāsādaṃ nāvameva ca .
parvataṃ ca samāruhya vipulāṃ bhārgavīṃ bhajet . . 1.149.40
1.149.d:
वाहनानि प्रशस्तानि प्रासादं नावमेव च ।
पर्वतं च समारुह्य विपुलां भार्गवीं भजेत् ॥ 1.149.40
1.149.m: Having mounted auspicious vehicles, a palace, a boat, / and a mountain, he would obtain the vast earth.

1.149.s:
pītvā surāṃ samudraṃ ca dadhyājyaṃ kṣīrameva ca .
somaṃ māṃsaṃ havirbhuktvā kāśyapīṃ labhate naraḥ . . 41
1.149.d:
पीत्वा सुरां समुद्रं च दध्याज्यं क्षीरमेव च ।
सोमं मांसं हविर्भुक्त्वा काश्यपीं लभते नरः ॥ 41
1.149.m: Having drunk wine, an ocean, curd, clarified butter, or milk, / [or] having consumed soma, meat, and sacrificial offering, a man obtains the earth.

1.149.s:
labdhvā vastrāṇi ratnāni vividhābharaṇāni ca .
vāhanāni mahīṃ gāśca dhānyopakaraṇāni ca . . 42
1.149.d:
लब्ध्वा वस्त्राणि रत्नानि विविधाभरणानि च ।
वाहनानि महीं गाश्च धान्योपकरणानि च ॥ 42
1.149.m: Having obtained clothes, jewels, various ornaments, / mounts, land, cattle, and agricultural implements,

1.149.s:
samṛddhimāpnuyātkiñcitsvapnānāṃ darśanaṃ śubham .
śubhakarmānugaṃ yacca tatsarvaṃ śubhamucyate . .4 3
tasmādanyadaniṣṭaṃ syāttasmādyuktā pratikriyā .
kramādālikhya saptamyāṃ tatra sampūjya bhāskaram .44
1.149.d:
समृद्धिमाप्नुयात्किञ्चित्स्वप्नानां दर्शनं शुभम् ।
शुभकर्मानुगं यच्च तत्सर्वं शुभमुच्यते ॥4 3
तस्मादन्यदनिष्टं स्यात्तस्माद्युक्ता प्रतिक्रिया ।
क्रमादालिख्य सप्तम्यां तत्र सम्पूज्य भास्करम् .44
1.149.m: he would attain prosperity: such a vision of dreams is auspicious. / Whatever follows an auspicious action, all that is called auspicious. / What is other than that is undesirable; therefore a counter-rite is prescribed. / Having drawn [the maṇḍala] in due order on the saptamī, having worshipped the Sun there,

1.149.s:
tarpayitvā dvijāñcchiṣṭānānamya pūrvavadgurum .
sṛṣṭikrameṇa bhṛtyarthaṃ muktyarthaṃ nānyathā bhavet . .45
1.149.d:
तर्पयित्वा द्विजाञ्च्छिष्टानानम्य पूर्ववद्गुरुम् ।
सृष्टिक्रमेण भृत्यर्थं मुक्त्यर्थं नान्यथा भवेत् ॥45
1.149.m: having gratified cultivated twice-borns, and having bowed to the guru as before, / [the rite must be performed] according to the order of creation for enjoyment, and for liberation; it must not be otherwise.

1.149.s:
divākaraṃ samālabhya puruṣo'tha yathākramam .
sarvagraheṣu tattveṣu yathāvattanniyojayet . .46
1.149.d:
दिवाकरं समालभ्य पुरुषोऽथ यथाक्रमम् ।
सर्वग्रहेषु तत्त्वेषु यथावत्तन्नियोजयेत् ॥46
1.149.m: Then, having anointed the Sun in due order, the man / should properly assign it to all planets and realities.

1.149.s:
viśuddheṣu viśuddhaṃ taṃ dhyātvā cādityavatkramāt .
niyojayetpṛthivyāśca tataḥ prabhṛti sarvaśaḥ . .47
1.149.d:
विशुद्धेषु विशुद्धं तं ध्यात्वा चादित्यवत्क्रमात् ।
नियोजयेत्पृथिव्याश्च ततः प्रभृति सर्वशः ॥47
1.149.m: Having meditated on that pure [Self] among the purified elements, in the manner of Āditya in order, / he should assign it everywhere beginning from the earth onwards.

1.149.s:
ādityamaṇḍalaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvamuktaṃ niyojayet .
evaṃ tu manasā dhyātvā juhuyāccaiva taṃ śatam .. 48
1.149.d:
आदित्यमण्डलं शुद्धं सर्वमुक्तं नियोजयेत् ।
एवं तु मनसा ध्यात्वा जुहुयाच्चैव तं शतम् ॥ 48
1.149.m: He should assign the pure orb of Āditya, all as prescribed; / meditating thus in mind, he should offer a hundred oblations to it.

1.149.s:
sarvairmantraiḥ kramādevaṃ dīkṣā proktā varāparā .
kṛtvaiva puṣpapātaṃ tu tasminnādityamaṇḍale . . 49
1.149.d:
सर्वैर्मन्त्रैः क्रमादेवं दीक्षा प्रोक्ता वरापरा ।
कृत्वैव पुष्पपातं तु तस्मिन्नादित्यमण्डले ॥ 49
1.149.m: In this way, with all mantras in sequence, the supreme initiation is declared. / Having indeed dropped a flower into that orb of Āditya,

1.149.s:
baddhvāsyamañjalau puṣpaṃ kṛtvā dattvā ca mantritam .
kṣipedvai kulaśuddhyarthaṃ nāmārthaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ . 1.149.50
1.149.d:
बद्ध्वास्यमञ्जलौ पुष्पं कृत्वा दत्त्वा च मन्त्रितम् ।
क्षिपेद्वै कुलशुद्ध्यर्थं नामार्थं च विशेषतः । 1.149.50
1.149.m: having bound his eyes, having placed a flower consecrated with mantra in his cupped hands, / he should cast it for the purity of his lineage and especially for the purpose of a name.

1.149.s:
yatra tatpatitaṃ puṇyaṃ tasya tatkulamādiśet .
nāma cādityasaṃyuktamityuktaṃ bhānunā svayam . . 51
1.149.d:
यत्र तत्पतितं पुण्यं तस्य तत्कुलमादिशेत् ।
नाम चादित्यसंयुक्तमित्युक्तं भानुना स्वयम् ॥ 51
1.149.m: Where that holy [flower] falls, he should assign him that family, / and a name connected with Āditya; so it was spoken by the Sun himself.

1.149.s:
sampūjya śrāvayettatra samayānarkabhāṣitān .
prātaḥ sāyaṃ madhyāhne raverabhimukhaḥ sthitaḥ . . 52
1.149.d:
सम्पूज्य श्रावयेत्तत्र समयानर्कभाषितान् ।
प्रातः सायं मध्याह्ने रवेरभिमुखः स्थितः ॥ 52
1.149.m: Having worshipped him, he should recite the rules spoken by the Sun: / In the morning, evening, and midday, standing facing the Sun,

1.149.s:
upasthānaṃ sadā kuryādarcanaṃ ca sadā naraḥ .
adṛṣṭvārkaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ divā rātrau hutāśanam . .5 3
dṛṣṭvā bhoktavyamarkākhyaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ kadācana .
na ca padyā spṛśettadvannāsanaṃ parivarjayet . . 54
1.149.d:
उपस्थानं सदा कुर्यादर्चनं च सदा नरः ।
अदृष्ट्वार्कं न भोक्तव्यं दिवा रात्रौ हुताशनम् ॥5 3
दृष्ट्वा भोक्तव्यमर्काख्यं न भोक्तव्यं कदाचन ।
न च पद्या स्पृशेत्तद्वन्नासनं परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 54
1.149.m: a man should always perform worship and perpetual adoration. / One should not eat without seeing the Sun by day or fire by night; / having seen that called the Sun, one may eat; never [otherwise]. / And likewise one must not touch it with feet, nor abandon one's seat [carelessly].

1.149.s:
na laṅghyā pratimācchāyā na laṅghyāstithayaḥ kvacit .
nakṣatrāṇi grahā yogā māsā māsādhipāśca ye . . 55
1.149.d:
न लङ्घ्या प्रतिमाच्छाया न लङ्घ्यास्तिथयः क्वचित् ।
नक्षत्राणि ग्रहा योगा मासा मासाधिपाश्च ये ॥ 55
1.149.m: One must not step over the shadow of an image, nor ever violate the lunar days, / lunar mansions, planets, yogas, months, and the rulers of months,

1.149.s:
ayane ṛtavaḥ pakṣāstathaiva divasāni ca .
kālaḥ saṃvatsaraścāpi yaḥ kaścitkāla ucyate . . 56
1.149.d:
अयने ऋतवः पक्षास्तथैव दिवसानि च ।
कालः संवत्सरश्चापि यः कश्चित्काल उच्यते ॥ 56
1.149.m: the two solstices, seasons, fortnights, and likewise the days, / time, the year, and whatever is called time.

1.149.s:
abhivandyaḥ sa sarvo'pi namasyaḥ pūjya eva ca .
tasmātkālādhipaḥ sūryaḥ svayaṃ kālaśca paṭhyate . .57
1.149.d:
अभिवन्द्यः स सर्वोऽपि नमस्यः पूज्य एव च ।
तस्मात्कालाधिपः सूर्यः स्वयं कालश्च पठ्यते ॥57
1.149.m: All of that is to be saluted, bowed to, and worshipped. / Therefore Sūrya is the lord of time and is proclaimed as Time himself.

1.149.s:
jyotirgaṇasya sarvasya sthāvarāsthāvarasya ca .
cetanācetanasyāpi sarvātmā yaḥ prakīrtitaḥ . . 58
1.149.d:
ज्योतिर्गणस्य सर्वस्य स्थावरास्थावरस्य च ।
चेतनाचेतनस्यापि सर्वात्मा यः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 58
1.149.m: He who is celebrated as the universal Soul of the entire host of luminaries, / of the immovable and the movable, of the conscious and the unconscious—

1.149.s:
stutyo vandyaḥ sadā pūjyastvayāyaṃ sarvathā nṛpa .
manasā karmaṇā vācā devanindāṃ parityajet . .5 9
preṣayitvā1 ca nirmālyaṃ tadaśvebhyo nivedayet .
prakṣālya hastau pādau ca namaskuryāddivākaram . . 1.149.60
1.149.d:
स्तुत्यो वन्द्यः सदा पूज्यस्त्वयायं सर्वथा नृप ।
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा देवनिन्दां परित्यजेत् ॥5 9
प्रेषयित्वा1 च निर्माल्यं तदश्वेभ्यो निवेदयेत् ।
प्रक्षाल्य हस्तौ पादौ च नमस्कुर्याद्दिवाकरम् ॥ 1.149.60
1.149.m: he is ever to be praised, revered, and worshipped by you in every way, O king. / One should avoid reviling the deity in mind, deed, and speech. / And having sent the floral remnants, he should offer them to his horses; / having washed both hands and feet, he should bow to the Maker of Day.

1.149.s:
ityeṣā paramā dīkṣā tava saṃkṣepato mayā .
bhuktimuktikarī cāpi kathitā pravibhāgataḥ . . 61
1.149.d:
इत्येषा परमा दीक्षा तव संक्षेपतो मया ।
भुक्तिमुक्तिकरी चापि कथिता प्रविभागतः ॥ 61
1.149.m: Thus this supreme initiation has been recounted in brief to you by me, / which grants worldly enjoyment and liberation, divided into its parts.

1.149.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sāmbopākhyāne sūryadīkṣāvarṇanaṃ
nāmaikonapañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 149 .
ādityapūjāvidhivarṇanam
1.149.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे साम्बोपाख्याने सूर्यदीक्षावर्णनं
नामैकोनपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 149 ।
आदित्यपूजाविधिवर्णनम्
1.149.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-ninth chapter, named “Description of Initiation into the Solar Rite,” in the Sambopākhyāna of the Saptamīkalpa, in the Brāhmaparvan of the auspicious and great Bhaviṣyapurāṇa.
Description of the Ritual of Worshipping Āditya

1.150.s:
vāsudeva uvāca
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yathā pūjyo divākaraḥ .
sthaṇḍile yaduśārdūla nibodhaikāgramānasaḥ . . 1
1.150.d:
वासुदेव उवाच
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा पूज्यो दिवाकरः ।
स्थण्डिले यदुशार्दूल निबोधैकाग्रमानसः ॥ 1
1.150.m: Vāsudeva said: / Hereafter I shall declare how the Maker of Day is to be worshipped / on a raised mound of earth, O tiger among the Yadus; listen with one-pointed mind.

1.150.s:
maṇḍalairaṣṭabhiḥ kāryaṃ cakraṃ kālātmakaṃ śubham .
madhye padmākṛtaṃ cakramarairdvādaśabhiryutam . . 2
1.150.d:
मण्डलैरष्टभिः कार्यं चक्रं कालात्मकं शुभम् ।
मध्ये पद्माकृतं चक्रमरैर्द्वादशभिर्युतम् ॥ 2
1.150.m: An auspicious wheel of the nature of Time should be made with eight circuits; / in the center is a lotus-shaped wheel endowed with twelve spokes.

1.150.s:
tanmadhye kamalaṃ proktaṃ patrāṣṭakasamanvitam .
sarvātmā sakalo devaḥ khaṣolkaḥ kiraṇojjvalaḥ . . 3
1.150.d:
तन्मध्ये कमलं प्रोक्तं पत्राष्टकसमन्वितम् ।
सर्वात्मा सकलो देवः खषोल्कः किरणोज्ज्वलः ॥ 3
1.150.m: In its center is said to be an eight-petalled lotus. / The god Khaṣolka, radiant with rays, endowed with all parts and the Self of all,

1.150.s:
pūjanīyaḥ sadā madhye sahasrakiraṇāyudhaḥ .
praṇavena mahābāho caturbāhusamanvitaḥ . .4
1.150.d:
पूजनीयः सदा मध्ये सहस्रकिरणायुधः ।
प्रणवेन महाबाहो चतुर्बाहुसमन्वितः ॥4
1.150.m: armed with a thousand rays, endowed with four arms, / is ever to be worshipped in the center with the Praṇava, O mighty-armed one.

1.150.s:
aruṇaṃ1 pūjayetprājñaḥ sadā devāgrajaṃ2 śubham .
dakṣiṇe pūjayeddevīṃ nikṣubhāṃ bhāskarasya tu . . 5
1.150.d:
अरुणं1 पूजयेत्प्राज्ञः सदा देवाग्रजं2 शुभम् ।
दक्षिणे पूजयेद्देवीं निक्षुभां भास्करस्य तु ॥ 5
1.150.m: The wise one should ever worship the auspicious Aruṇa, elder brother of the gods; / and to the south he should worship Nikṣubhā, the goddess of the Sun.

1.150.s:
revataṃ dakṣiṇe pārśve uttare piṅgalaṃ sadā .
saṃjñāṃ ca yaduśārdūla śreyase satataṃ budhaḥ . . 6
1.150.d:
रेवतं दक्षिणे पार्श्वे उत्तरे पिङ्गलं सदा ।
संज्ञां च यदुशार्दूल श्रेयसे सततं बुधः ॥ 6
1.150.m: The wise man should always worship Revanta on the southern side, Piṅgala on the northern, / and Saṃjñā, O tiger among the Yadus, for continuous welfare.

1.150.s:
āgneyyāṃ lekhakaṃ vīra nairṛtyāmaśvinau tathā .
vāyavyāṃ pūjayeddevaṃ manuṃ vaivasvataṃ vibhum . . 7
1.150.d:
आग्नेय्यां लेखकं वीर नैरृत्यामश्विनौ तथा ।
वायव्यां पूजयेद्देवं मनुं वैवस्वतं विभुम् ॥ 7
1.150.m: In the southeast [he should worship] the Scribe, O hero; in the southwest, the Aśvins; / in the northwest he should worship the divine, all-pervading Manu Vaivasvata.

1.150.s:
aiśānyāṃ pūjayeddevīṃ yamunāṃ lokapāvanīm .
dvitīyāvaraṇe vīra pūrvataḥ pūjayedviyat . . 8
1.150.d:
ऐशान्यां पूजयेद्देवीं यमुनां लोकपावनीम् ।
द्वितीयावरणे वीर पूर्वतः पूजयेद्वियत् ॥ 8
1.150.m: In the northeast he should worship goddess Yamunā, who purifies the worlds. / In the second enclosure, O hero, he should worship Space in the east,

1.150.s:
dakṣiṇe ca tato devīṃ paścime garuḍaṃ tathā .
uttare nāgarājānaṃ putramairāvataṃ śubham . . 9
1.150.d:
दक्षिणे च ततो देवीं पश्चिमे गरुडं तथा ।
उत्तरे नागराजानं पुत्रमैरावतं शुभम् ॥ 9
1.150.m: and then the goddess in the south, Garuḍa in the west, / and in the north the serpent-king, the auspicious son Airāvata.

1.150.s:
āgneyyāṃ pūjayeddheliṃ praheliṃ nairṛte tathā .
vāyavyāmurvaśīṃ devīmīśāne vinatāṃ tathā . . 1.150.10
1.150.d:
आग्नेय्यां पूजयेद्धेलिं प्रहेलिं नैरृते तथा ।
वायव्यामुर्वशीं देवीमीशाने विनतां तथा ॥ 1.150.10
1.150.m: In the southeast he should worship Heli, and Praheli in the southwest, / goddess Urvaśī in the northwest, and Vinatā in the northeast.

1.150.s:
tṛtīyāvaraṇe pūrve pūjayedgurumādarāt .
paścime tvarkaputraṃ tu uttare dhiṣaṇaṃ tathā . . 11
1.150.d:
तृतीयावरणे पूर्वे पूजयेद्गुरुमादरात् ।
पश्चिमे त्वर्कपुत्रं तु उत्तरे धिषणं तथा ॥ 11
1.150.m: In the third enclosure, he should worship Guru in the east with reverence, / the son of the Sun in the west, and Dhiṣaṇa in the north.

1.150.s:
aiśāne śaśiputraṃ tu somamāgneyamaṇḍale .
pūjayeddakṣiṇe koṇe nairṛte rāhumādarāt . . 12
1.150.d:
ऐशाने शशिपुत्रं तु सोममाग्नेयमण्डले ।
पूजयेद्दक्षिणे कोणे नैरृते राहुमादरात् ॥ 12
1.150.m: In the northeast the son of the Moon, and Soma in the circle of the southeast; / he should worship in the southern corner, and Rāhu in the southwest with devotion.

1.150.s:
vāyavye vikacaṃ vīra pūjayetsatataṃ budhaḥ .
caturthāvaraṇe devaṃ pūjayellekhamādarāt . . 13
1.150.d:
वायव्ये विकचं वीर पूजयेत्सततं बुधः ।
चतुर्थावरणे देवं पूजयेल्लेखमादरात् ॥ 13
1.150.m: In the northwest the wise man should ever worship Vikaca, O hero. / In the fourth enclosure, he should worship the god Lekha with reverence.

1.150.s:
āgneye śāṇḍilīputraṃ dakṣiṇe dakṣiṇādhipam .
virūpākṣaṃ nairṛte devaṃ jaleśaṃ paścime tathā . . 14
1.150.d:
आग्नेये शाण्डिलीपुत्रं दक्षिणे दक्षिणाधिपम् ।
विरूपाक्षं नैरृते देवं जलेशं पश्चिमे तथा ॥ 14
1.150.m: In the southeast the son of Śāṇḍilī, in the south the lord of the south, / the god Virūpākṣa in the southwest, and the lord of the waters in the west.

1.150.s:
vāyuputraṃ ca vāyavyāṃ satataṃ pūjayennaraḥ .
īśāne devamīśānaṃ pūjayetsatataṃ budhaḥ . . 15
1.150.d:
वायुपुत्रं च वायव्यां सततं पूजयेन्नरः ।
ईशाने देवमीशानं पूजयेत्सततं बुधः ॥ 15
1.150.m: And in the northwest a man should always worship the son of Vāyu; / in the northeast the wise man should ever worship the god Īśāna.

1.150.s:
uttare yakṣarājānāṃ kuberaṃ pūjayedbudhaḥ .
pañcame pūjayedvīra sadā svāvaraṇe dvijāḥ . . 16
1.150.d:
उत्तरे यक्षराजानां कुबेरं पूजयेद्बुधः ।
पञ्चमे पूजयेद्वीर सदा स्वावरणे द्विजाः ॥ 16
1.150.m: In the north the wise man should worship Kubera, the king of yakṣas. / In the fifth enclosure, O hero, the twice-born should ever worship his own:

1.150.s:
pūrvataḥ paramāṃ devīṃ mahāśvetāṃ mahāmatiḥ .
śriyamṛddhiṃ vibhūtiṃ ca dhṛtiṃ caivonnatiṃ tathā . . 17
1.150.d:
पूर्वतः परमां देवीं महाश्वेतां महामतिः ।
श्रियमृद्धिं विभूतिं च धृतिं चैवोन्नतिं तथा ॥ 17
1.150.m: in the east the supreme goddess Mahāśvetā, the highly intelligent one; / Śrī, Ṛddhi, Vibhūti, Dhṛti, and Unnati.

1.150.s:
pṛthivīṃ yaduśārdūla mahākīrtiṃ tathaiva ca .
indraṃ viṣṇuṃ cāryamaṇaṃ bhagaṃ parjanyameva ca . . 18
1.150.d:
पृथिवीं यदुशार्दूल महाकीर्तिं तथैव च ।
इन्द्रं विष्णुं चार्यमणं भगं पर्जन्यमेव च ॥ 18
1.150.m: and Pṛthivī, O tiger among the Yadus, and Mahākīrti as well; / Indra, Viṣṇu, Aryaman, Bhaga, and Parjanya;

1.150.s:
vivasvantaṃ tathārkaṃ ca tvaṣṭāraṃ kiraṇojjvalam .
pūjayedvaruṇaṃ ṣaṣṭhe caivametāndivākarān . . 19
1.150.d:
विवस्वन्तं तथार्कं च त्वष्टारं किरणोज्ज्वलम् ।
पूजयेद्वरुणं षष्ठे चैवमेतान्दिवाकरान् ॥ 19
1.150.m: Vivasvat, Arka, and Tvaṣṭṛ, radiant with rays; / and in the sixth [enclosure] one should worship Varuṇa, and these [twelve] suns.

1.150.s:
śiro netre tathā varma astraṃ ca yadusattama .
aruṇaṃ sarathaṃ vīra saptame pūjayedbudhaḥ . . 1.150.20
1.150.d:
शिरो नेत्रे तथा वर्म अस्त्रं च यदुसत्तम ।
अरुणं सरथं वीर सप्तमे पूजयेद्बुधः ॥ 1.150.20
1.150.m: The head, the two eyes, armour, and the weapon, O best of Yadus; / in the seventh [enclosure], O hero, the wise man should worship Aruṇa together with his chariot,

1.150.s:
tathāśvānyaduśārdūla sadā cāvaraṇe budhaḥ .
yakṣarakṣāṃsi gandharvānmāsānpakṣānahāni tu . . 21
1.150.d:
तथाश्वान्यदुशार्दूल सदा चावरणे बुधः ।
यक्षरक्षांसि गन्धर्वान्मासान्पक्षानहानि तु ॥ 21
1.150.m: as well as the horses, O tiger among the Yadus, ever in the enclosure, the wise man [should worship]; / and the yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, months, fortnights, and days,

1.150.s:
saṃvatsaraṃ tathā putra hyetānsaṃpūjayetpurā .
ya evaṃ pūjayeddevaṃ bhāskaraṃ satataṃ naraḥ . .
sa gacchetparamaṃ sthānaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati . . 22
1.150.d:
संवत्सरं तथा पुत्र ह्येतान्संपूजयेत्पुरा ।
य एवं पूजयेद्देवं भास्करं सततं नरः ॥
स गच्छेत्परमं स्थानं यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ॥ 22
1.150.m: and the year, O son; indeed, he should worship these previously. / The man who thus constantly worships the god Bhāskara / goes to the supreme abode, having gone where he does not grieve.

1.150.s:
( oṃ khaṣolkāya namaḥ)
mūlamantrākṣarāṇīha cāṅgāni paricakṣate .
anena vidhinā yastu pūjayetsatataṃ ravim . . 23
1.150.d:
( ओं खषोल्काय नमः)
मूलमन्त्राक्षराणीह चाङ्गानि परिचक्षते ।
अनेन विधिना यस्तु पूजयेत्सततं रविम् ॥ 23
1.150.m: (Oṃ, homage to Khaṣolka!) / The syllables of the root mantra and the ancillary limbs are taught here. / He who constantly worships Ravi according to this rule,

1.150.s:
nityamubhayasaptamyāṃ sa gacchetparamaṃ padam .
ityuktvā bhagavāndevo jagāmāśu gṛhaṃ raviḥ . . 24
sauradharmavarṇanam
1.150.d:
नित्यमुभयसप्तम्यां स गच्छेत्परमं पदम् ।
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्देवो जगामाशु गृहं रविः ॥ 24
सौरधर्मवर्णनम्
1.150.m:
always on both saptamīs, goes to the supreme state. / Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord Ravi quickly departed to his home.
Description of the Saura Dharma

1.151.s:
sūta uvāca
atha rājā mahātejāḥ śatānīko dvijottamam .
praṇamya śirasā bhaktyā sumantuṃ vākyamabravīt . . 1
1.151.d:
सूत उवाच
अथ राजा महातेजाः शतानीको द्विजोत्तमम् ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा भक्त्या सुमन्तुं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 1
1.151.m: Sūta said: / Then the highly radiant King Śatānīka, / bowing his head with devotion to Sumantu, the best of twice-borns, spoke [these] words:

1.151.s:
aho devasya māhātmyaṃ bhāskarasyāmitaujasaḥ .
kīrtitaṃ bhavatā mahyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam . . 2
1.151.d:
अहो देवस्य माहात्म्यं भास्करस्यामितौजसः ।
कीर्तितं भवता मह्यं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥ 2
1.151.m: "Ah, the greatness of the god Bhāskara of boundless splendour, / which destroys all sins, has been proclaimed by you to me.

1.151.s:
tasmānnārkasamaṃ devaṃ loke paśyāmi suvrata .
na cāpyasya sthitā vipra gatirlokeṣu vidyate . . 3
1.151.d:
तस्मान्नार्कसमं देवं लोके पश्यामि सुव्रत ।
न चाप्यस्य स्थिता विप्र गतिर्लोकेषु विद्यते ॥ 3
1.151.m: Therefore I see no god equal to Arka in the world, O you of noble vows, / nor is his fixed course found [limited] among the worlds, O twice-born.

1.151.s:
pravartate jagadvipra sargakāle divākarāt .
sthitau pālayate cāpi kalpānte saṃharetpunaḥ . . 4
1.151.d:
प्रवर्तते जगद्विप्र सर्गकाले दिवाकरात् ।
स्थितौ पालयते चापि कल्पान्ते संहरेत्पुनः ॥ 4
1.151.m: The world proceeds from the Sun at the time of creation, O twice-born; / in preservation, he protects it, and at the end of the kalpa he destroys it again.

1.151.s:
śrutvaivaṃ devamāhātmyaṃ bhāskarasyāmitaujasaḥ .
kīrtitaṃ bhavatā mahyamaśvamedhaśatādvaram . . 5
1.151.d:
श्रुत्वैवं देवमाहात्म्यं भास्करस्यामितौजसः ।
कीर्तितं भवता मह्यमश्वमेधशताद्वरम् ॥ 5
1.151.m: Having heard this greatness of the god Bhāskara of boundless splendour, / proclaimed by you to me, which is superior to a hundred horse sacrifices,

1.151.s:
kiṃ tu me saṃśayo brahmansumahānhṛdi vartate .
kenopāyena viprendra mucyate sambhavārṇavāt . . 6
1.151.d:
किं तु मे संशयो ब्रह्मन्सुमहान्हृदि वर्तते ।
केनोपायेन विप्रेन्द्र मुच्यते सम्भवार्णवात् ॥ 6
1.151.m: a very great doubt, however, resides in my heart, O brāhmaṇa: / by what means, O chief of twice-borns, is one liberated from the ocean of rebirth?

1.151.s:
divākaraprasādādvai suprasannādvṛṣadhvajāt .
kathaṃ tuṣyetsadā devo dharmeṇa katareṇa tu . . 7
1.151.d:
दिवाकरप्रसादाद्वै सुप्रसन्नाद्वृषध्वजात् ।
कथं तुष्येत्सदा देवो धर्मेण कतरेण तु ॥ 7
1.151.m: By the grace of the Sun indeed, or from the well-pleased [Śiva] whose banner is a bull— / by which duty would the god always be satisfied?

1.151.s:
śrutā me bahavo dharmāḥ śrutismṛtyuditāstathā .
vaiṣṇavāḥ śaivadharmāśca tathā paurāṇikāḥ śrutāḥ . . 8
1.151.d:
श्रुता मे बहवो धर्माः श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितास्तथा ।
वैष्णवाः शैवधर्माश्च तथा पौराणिकाः श्रुताः ॥ 8
1.151.m: Many duties declared in the Śruti and Smṛti have been heard by me; / Vaiṣṇava and Śaiva duties, as well as Paurāṇika ones, have been heard.

1.151.s:
śrotukāmo hyahaṃ vipra sauraṃ dharmamanaupamam .
bhagavansarvadhanyāste sauradharmaparāyaṇāḥ . . 9
1.151.d:
श्रोतुकामो ह्यहं विप्र सौरं धर्ममनौपमम् ।
भगवन्सर्वधन्यास्ते सौरधर्मपरायणाः ॥ 9
1.151.m: I wish to hear, O twice-born, the incomparable Saura duty. / Blessed are all those, O venerable one, who are devoted to the Saura duty.

1.151.s:
brūhi me devadevasya bhānordharmamanaupamam .
śṛṇvato nāsti me tṛptiramṛtasyaivameva ca . . 1.151.10
1.151.d:
ब्रूहि मे देवदेवस्य भानोर्धर्ममनौपमम् ।
शृण्वतो नास्ति मे तृप्तिरमृतस्यैवमेव च ॥ 1.151.10
1.151.m: Tell me the incomparable duty of the Sun, the god of gods; / as I listen, there is no satiety for me, just as with nectar.

1.151.s:
aśvamedhādayo yajñā bahusambhāravistarāḥ .
na śakyāste yataḥ kartumalpavittadvijātibhiḥ . . 11
1.151.d:
अश्वमेधादयो यज्ञा बहुसम्भारविस्तराः ।
न शक्यास्ते यतः कर्तुमल्पवित्तद्विजातिभिः ॥ 11
1.151.m: Sacrifices such as the horse sacrifice involve extensive and numerous provisions, / since they cannot be performed by twice-borns of little wealth.

1.151.s:
sukhopāyamato brūhi dharmakāmārthasādhakam .
hitāya sarvamartyānāṃ sarvapāpabhayāpaham . . 12
1.151.d:
सुखोपायमतो ब्रूहि धर्मकामार्थसाधकम् ।
हिताय सर्वमर्त्यानां सर्वपापभयापहम् ॥ 12
1.151.m: Therefore, speak of an easy means that accomplishes righteousness, desire, and wealth, / for the welfare of all mortals, which removes the fear of all sins,

1.151.s:
sauradharmaparaṃ puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam .
śrutvā tu vacanaṃ rājño vyāsaśiṣyo mahāmuniḥ . .
praṇamya śirasā vyāsamidaṃ vacanamabravīt . . 13
1.151.d:
सौरधर्मपरं पुण्यं पवित्रं पापनाशनम् ।
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं राज्ञो व्यासशिष्यो महामुनिः ॥
प्रणम्य शिरसा व्यासमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 13
1.151.m: which pertains to the Saura duty, is meritorious, pure, and destroys sin." / Having heard the words of the king, the great sage, the disciple of Vyāsa, / bowing with his head to Vyāsa, spoke these words:

1.151.s:
sumanturuvāca
śrūyatāmabhidhāsyāmi sukhopāyaṃ mahāphalam .
paramaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sarvadharmamanaupamam . . 14
1.151.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
श्रूयतामभिधास्यामि सुखोपायं महाफलम् ।
परमं सर्वधर्माणां सर्वधर्ममनौपमम् ॥ 14
1.151.m: Sumantu said: / "Listen, I shall declare an easy means yielding great fruit, / the highest of all duties, the incomparable duty of all.

1.151.s:
raviṇā kathitaṃ pūrvamaruṇasya viśāṃpate .
kṛṣṇasya brahmaṇo vīra śaṅkarasya na vidyate . . 15
1.151.d:
रविणा कथितं पूर्वमरुणस्य विशांपते ।
कृष्णस्य ब्रह्मणो वीर शङ्करस्य न विद्यते ॥ 15
1.151.m: It was previously related by Ravi to Aruṇa, O ruler of the people; / it is not found among Kṛṣṇa, Brahmā, or Śaṅkara, O hero.

1.151.s:
saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināmayam .
sauradharmatamaḥ śrīmānhitāya jagatoditaḥ . . 16
1.151.d:
संसारार्णवमग्नानां सर्वेषां प्राणिनामयम् ।
सौरधर्मतमः श्रीमान्हिताय जगतोदितः ॥ 16
1.151.m: For all living beings sunk in the ocean of transmigration, / this most splendid supreme Saura duty was spoken for the welfare of the world.

1.151.s:
yairayaṃ śāntahṛdayaiḥ sūryabhaktairbhagārthibhiḥ .
saṃsevyate paro dharmaste saurā nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 17
1.151.d:
यैरयं शान्तहृदयैः सूर्यभक्तैर्भगार्थिभिः ।
संसेव्यते परो धर्मस्ते सौरा नात्र संशयः ॥ 17
1.151.m: Those who, with peaceful hearts, devoted to Sūrya and seeking prosperity, / diligently practice this supreme duty—they are Sauras, without doubt.

1.151.s:
ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ nityameva ca .
ye smaranti raviṃ bhaktyā sakṛdevāpi bhārata . .
sarvapāpairvimucyante saptajanmakṛtairapi . . 18
1.151.d:
एककालं द्विकालं वा त्रिकालं नित्यमेव च ।
ये स्मरन्ति रविं भक्त्या सकृदेवापि भारत ॥
सर्वपापैर्विमुच्यन्ते सप्तजन्मकृतैरपि ॥ 18
1.151.m: Whether at one time, two times, or three times, and always, / those who remember Ravi with devotion, even once, O Bhārata, / are liberated from all sins, even those committed in seven births.

1.151.s:
stuvanti ye sadā bhānuṃ na te prakṛtimānuṣāḥ .
svargalokātparibhraṣṭāste jñeyā bhāskarā bhuvi . . 19
1.151.d:
स्तुवन्ति ये सदा भानुं न ते प्रकृतिमानुषाः ।
स्वर्गलोकात्परिभ्रष्टास्ते ज्ञेया भास्करा भुवि ॥ 19
1.151.m: Those who constantly praise the Sun are not ordinary men; / having fallen from the heavenly world, they are to be known as suns upon the earth.

1.151.s:
nānarkaḥ smarate'rkaṃ vai nānarko'rkaṃ samarcayet .
nānarkaḥ kīrtayedarkaṃ nānarko'rkamavāpnuyāt . . 1.151.20
1.151.d:
नानर्कः स्मरतेऽर्कं वै नानर्कोऽर्कं समर्चयेत् ।
नानर्कः कीर्तयेदर्कं नानर्कोऽर्कमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 1.151.20
1.151.m: One who is not Arka does not remember Arka; one who is not Arka does not worship Arka; / one who is not Arka does not praise Arka; one who is not Arka does not attain Arka.

1.151.s:
sauradharmasya sāro'yaṃ sūryabhaktiḥ suniścalā .
ṣoḍaśāṅgā ca sā proktā raviṇeha divaukasām . . 21
1.151.d:
सौरधर्मस्य सारोऽयं सूर्यभक्तिः सुनिश्चला ।
षोडशाङ्गा च सा प्रोक्ता रविणेह दिवौकसाम् ॥ 21
1.151.m: This is the essence of the Saura duty: unwavering devotion to Sūrya; / and that sixteen-limbed [devotion] was proclaimed here by Ravi to the gods.

1.151.s:
prātaḥ snānaṃ japo homastathā devārcanaṃ nṛpa .
dvijānāṃ pūjanaṃ bhaktyā pūjā gośvatthayostathā . . 22
1.151.d:
प्रातः स्नानं जपो होमस्तथा देवार्चनं नृप ।
द्विजानां पूजनं भक्त्या पूजा गोश्वत्थयोस्तथा ॥ 22
1.151.m: Morning bath, recitation of mantras, fire oblation, and worship of the deity, O king; / worship of twice-borns with devotion, and worship of the cow and the aśvattha tree;

1.151.s:
itihāsapurāṇebhyo bhaktiśraddhāpuraskṛtam .
śravaṇaṃ rājaśārdūla vedābhyāsastathaiva ca . . 23
1.151.d:
इतिहासपुराणेभ्यो भक्तिश्रद्धापुरस्कृतम् ।
श्रवणं राजशार्दूल वेदाभ्यासस्तथैव च ॥ 23
1.151.m: listening to the Itihāsas and Purāṇas accompanied by devotion and faith, / O tiger among kings, and practice of the Veda as well;

1.151.s:
madbhaktyā janavātsalyaṃ pūjāyāṃ cānumodanam .
svayamabhyarcayedbhaktyā mamāgre vācakaṃ param . . 24
1.151.d:
मद्भक्त्या जनवात्सल्यं पूजायां चानुमोदनम् ।
स्वयमभ्यर्चयेद्भक्त्या ममाग्रे वाचकं परम् ॥ 24
1.151.m: affection toward people on account of devotion to me, and rejoicing in worship; / one should oneself worship with devotion the supreme reciter before me;

1.151.s:
pustakasya sadā śreṣṭha mamātīva priyaṃ surāḥ .
matkathāśravaṇaṃ nityaṃ svaranetrāṅgavikriyā . . 25
1.151.d:
पुस्तकस्य सदा श्रेष्ठ ममातीव प्रियं सुराः ।
मत्कथाश्रवणं नित्यं स्वरनेत्राङ्गविक्रिया ॥ 25
1.151.m: [worship] of the book, O best one, is always exceedingly dear to me, O gods; / constant listening to my stories; emotional alteration of voice, eyes, and limbs;

1.151.s:
mamānusmaraṇaṃ nityaṃ bhaktyā śraddhāpuraskṛtam .
ṣoḍaśāḍgā bhaktiriyaṃ yasminmlecche'pi vartate . .
viprendraḥ sa muniḥ śrīmānsajātyaḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ . . 26
1.151.d:
ममानुस्मरणं नित्यं भक्त्या श्रद्धापुरस्कृतम् ।
षोडशाड्गा भक्तिरियं यस्मिन्म्लेच्छेऽपि वर्तते ॥
विप्रेन्द्रः स मुनिः श्रीमान्सजात्यः स च पण्डितः ॥ 26
1.151.m: and constant remembrance of me accompanied by devotion and faith. / Even if this sixteen-limbed devotion exists in a mleccha, / he is a chief of twice-borns, he is a sage, he is prosperous, he is an equal in caste, and he is a learned man.

1.151.s:
na me pṛthakcaturvedā madbhaktaḥ śvapaco'pi yaḥ .
tasmai deyaṃ tato grāhyaṃ sa ca pūjyo yathā hyaham . . 27
1.151.d:
न मे पृथक्चतुर्वेदा मद्भक्तः श्वपचोऽपि यः ।
तस्मै देयं ततो ग्राह्यं स च पूज्यो यथा ह्यहम् ॥ 27
1.151.m: To me, those who know the four Vedas are not different from one who is my devotee, even if he is a dog-cooker; / to him should be given, from him should be accepted, and he is to be worshipped just like me.

1.151.s:
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati .
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa ca me na praṇaśyati . . 28
1.151.d:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति ।
तस्याहं न प्रणश्यामि स च मे न प्रणश्यति ॥ 28
1.151.m: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water— / I am not lost to him, and he is not lost to me.

1.151.s:
yo māṃ sarvagataṃ paśyetsarvaṃ ca mayi saṃsthitam .
tasyāhamāsthito nityaṃ sa ca nityaṃ mayi sthitaḥ . . 29
1.151.d:
यो मां सर्वगतं पश्येत्सर्वं च मयि संस्थितम् ।
तस्याहमास्थितो नित्यं स च नित्यं मयि स्थितः ॥ 29
1.151.m: He who sees me present in all things, and all things situated in me— / I am ever abiding for him, and he is ever abiding in me.

1.151.s:
aṣṭādaśārdhakakṣāyāḥ paraṃ cāṣṭabhirudbhavaiḥ .
rodhayitvā mahābāho tathā jñānatareṇa tu . . 1.151.30
1.151.d:
अष्टादशार्धकक्षायाः परं चाष्टभिरुद्भवैः ।
रोधयित्वा महाबाहो तथा ज्ञानतरेण तु ॥ 1.151.30
1.151.m: Beyond the ninth enclosure, having blocked [the mind] / with the eight manifestations, O mighty-armed one, and by supreme knowledge,

1.151.s:
durgapālaṃ vijityāśu bhāskarārdhaṃ tu durjayam .
jitvā ca purarājānāṃ mahātejamanaupamam . . 31
1.151.d:
दुर्गपालं विजित्याशु भास्करार्धं तु दुर्जयम् ।
जित्वा च पुरराजानां महातेजमनौपमम् ॥ 31
1.151.m: having quickly conquered the fortress guardian, and having conquered the invincible half of Bhāskara, / and the king of the city, of great splendour and incomparable,

1.151.s:
manasācalayā bhaktyā yo māṃ dhyāyati mānavaḥ .
ahaṃ tameva ciṃtāmi ātmavatsatataṃ naram . . 32
1.151.d:
मनसाचलया भक्त्या यो मां ध्यायति मानवः ।
अहं तमेव चिंतामि आत्मवत्सततं नरम् ॥ 32
1.151.m: the man who meditates on me with an unwavering mind and devotion— / on that very man do I always reflect, as on myself.

1.151.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sauradharmavarṇanaṃ
nāmaikapañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 151 .
sūradharmeṣu praśnavarṇanam
1.151.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे सौरधर्मवर्णनं
नामैकपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 151 ।
सूरधर्मेषु प्रश्नवर्णनम्
1.151.m:
Thus ends the hundred and fifty-first chapter, titled "Description of the Saura Dharma," in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa. 151.
Description of the Inquiries Concerning the Duties to the Sun

1.152.s:
sumanturuvāca
sūre ca durlabhā bhaktirdurlabhaṃ surapūjanam .
sūrāya durlabhaṃ dānaṃ sūrahomaśca durlabhaḥ . . 1
1.152.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
सूरे च दुर्लभा भक्तिर्दुर्लभं सुरपूजनम् ।
सूराय दुर्लभं दानं सूरहोमश्च दुर्लभः ॥ 1
1.152.m: Sumantu said: / "Devotion to the Sun is rare, worship of the gods is rare; / giving to the Sun is rare, and offering oblations to the Sun is rare.

1.152.s:
sudurlabhaṃ raverjñānaṃ tadabhyāso'pi durlabha .
sudurlabhataraṃ jñeyaṃ khaṣolkajñānamuttamam . . 2
1.152.d:
सुदुर्लभं रवेर्ज्ञानं तदभ्यासोऽपि दुर्लभ ।
सुदुर्लभतरं ज्ञेयं खषोल्कज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥ 2
1.152.m: Exceedingly difficult to attain is knowledge of the Sun, and its practice too is hard to attain; / even more difficult to attain, it should be known, is the supreme knowledge of Khaṣolka.

1.152.s:
sudurlabhataraṃ jñānaṃ sadā vai bhāskarasya tu .
pradakṣiṇāṃ cakraturvai pādau bhaktyā'rkamandire . . 3
1.152.d:
सुदुर्लभतरं ज्ञानं सदा वै भास्करस्य तु ।
प्रदक्षिणां चक्रतुर्वै पादौ भक्त्याऽर्कमन्दिरे ॥ 3
1.152.m: Ever indeed is knowledge of the Sun exceedingly difficult to attain. / Blessed are the two feet that have performed circumambulation with devotion in the temple of the Sun.

1.152.s:
tau karau ślāghyatāṃ prāptau yau pūjāṃ cakratū raveḥ .
saivaikā rasanā dhanyā stotraṃ yā kurute raveḥ . . 4
1.152.d:
तौ करौ श्लाघ्यतां प्राप्तौ यौ पूजां चक्रतू रवेः ।
सैवैका रसना धन्या स्तोत्रं या कुरुते रवेः ॥ 4
1.152.m: Those two hands have attained praiseworthiness that have performed the worship of the Sun; / that tongue alone is blessed which utters praise of the Sun.

1.152.s:
tanmanaḥ puṇyatāṃ prāptaṃ yaddhitvā viṣayaṃ nṛpa .
niścalā ca raverlīlā nirbhīkā krodhavarjitā . . 5
1.152.d:
तन्मनः पुण्यतां प्राप्तं यद्धित्वा विषयं नृप ।
निश्चला च रवेर्लीला निर्भीका क्रोधवर्जिता ॥ 5
1.152.m: That mind has attained merit, O king, which, abandoning worldly objects, / [remains] motionless, fearless, and free from anger in the sport of the Sun.

1.152.s:
śatānīka uvāca
sūryārcanavidhiṃ kurvañchrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ .
tvatprasādāddvijaśreṣṭha kautūhalamatīva me . . 6
1.152.d:
शतानीक उवाच
सूर्यार्चनविधिं कुर्वञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ।
त्वत्प्रसादाद्द्विजश्रेष्ठ कौतूहलमतीव मे ॥ 6
1.152.m:
Śatānīka said:
Performing the rite of worshipping the Sun, I desire to hear [it] as it truly is. / Through your favour, O best of twice-born, my curiosity is very great:

1.152.s:
yatpuṇyaṃ sthāpite sūrye kṛte sūryālaye ca yat .
sammārjane ca yatpuṇyaṃ yatpuṇyamupalepane. . 7
1.152.d:
यत्पुण्यं स्थापिते सूर्ये कृते सूर्यालये च यत् ।
सम्मार्जने च यत्पुण्यं यत्पुण्यमुपलेपने॥ 7
1.152.m: the merit gained when the Sun is installed, and when an abode for the Sun is built; / the merit gained in sweeping, and the merit gained in smearing [it with cow-dung];

1.152.s:
sthāne kṛte ca yatpuṇyaṃ tathā nīrājane kṛte .
nīlauṣadhipravāpena nṛtyamaṅgalavāditaiḥ . . 8
1.152.d:
स्थाने कृते च यत्पुण्यं तथा नीराजने कृते ।
नीलौषधिप्रवापेन नृत्यमङ्गलवादितैः ॥ 8
1.152.m: the merit gained when the pedestal is made, and likewise when the lustration with lamps is performed / with the scattering of blue medicinal herbs, accompanied by dances and auspicious instruments;

1.152.s:
arghyadānena yatpuṇyaṃ toyasnānena yadbhavet .
pañcāmṛtamayasnāne dadhisnāne ca yatphalam . . 9
1.152.d:
अर्घ्यदानेन यत्पुण्यं तोयस्नानेन यद्भवेत् ।
पञ्चामृतमयस्नाने दधिस्नाने च यत्फलम् ॥ 9
1.152.m: the merit gained by giving water for the arghya, and what comes from bathing [the icon] with water; / the fruit gained from bathing with the five nectars, and from bathing with curds;

1.152.s:
cakrābhyaṅge ca yatproktaṃ vajrasnāne ca yatphalam .
madhusnāne payaḥsnāne snāna ikṣurasasya tu . . 1.152.10
1.152.d:
चक्राभ्यङ्गे च यत्प्रोक्तं वज्रस्नाने च यत्फलम् ।
मधुस्नाने पयःस्नाने स्नान इक्षुरसस्य तु ॥ 1.152.10
1.152.m: and what is declared regarding anointing the discus, and the fruit from bathing [the icon] with vajra; / in bathing with honey, in bathing with milk, and in bathing with sugarcane juice;

1.152.s:
udvartanaṃ śucisthāne kuśapuṣpodakena tu .
suvarṇaratnatoyaiśca gandhacandanavāribhiḥ . . 11
1.152.d:
उद्वर्तनं शुचिस्थाने कुशपुष्पोदकेन तु ।
सुवर्णरत्नतोयैश्च गन्धचन्दनवारिभिः ॥ 11
1.152.m: the rubbing down in a pure place with water of kuśa grass and flowers, / with waters containing gold and jewels, and with fragrant sandalwood water;

1.152.s:
karpūrāgurutoyena svacchato yena yatphalam .
vilepanaiśca gandhāḍhyairvilepanaphalaṃ labhet . . 12
1.152.d:
कर्पूरागुरुतोयेन स्वच्छतो येन यत्फलम् ।
विलेपनैश्च गन्धाढ्यैर्विलेपनफलं लभेत् ॥ 12
1.152.m: and the fruit that one attains from water containing camphor and agallochum, with pure water, / and with ointments rich in fragrances—the fruit of applying ointments;

1.152.s:
tālapatrapradāne tu pradāne cāmarasya tu .
raktapuṣpārcane yacca dāmabhiḥ pūjanena ca . . 13
1.152.d:
तालपत्रप्रदाने तु प्रदाने चामरस्य तु ।
रक्तपुष्पार्चने यच्च दामभिः पूजनेन च ॥ 13
1.152.m: and upon offering a palm leaf, upon offering a chowrie, / upon worshipping with red flowers, and upon worshipping with garlands;

1.152.s:
sumānāṃ maṇḍape yacca puṣpamālāvalambanāt .
pūjābhaktiviśeṣaiśca gṛhamālāvalambane . . 14
1.152.d:
सुमानां मण्डपे यच्च पुष्पमालावलम्बनात् ।
पूजाभक्तिविशेषैश्च गृहमालावलम्बने ॥ 14
1.152.m: and what [is gained] from suspending garlands of flowers in the pavilion for the gods, / and through special acts of devotion and worship, from suspending garlands on the shrine;

1.152.s:
puṣpadānaviśeṣeṇa dhūpadīpaiśca yatphalam .
vastrālaṅkāradāne tu puṇyaśravaṇakīrtane . . 15
1.152.d:
पुष्पदानविशेषेण धूपदीपैश्च यत्फलम् ।
वस्त्रालङ्कारदाने तु पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तने ॥ 15
1.152.m: and the fruit gained through the special gift of flowers, through incense and lamps; / upon giving clothing and ornaments, and in listening to and reciting meritorious deeds;

1.152.s:
brahmaśravasya dāne tu avyaṅgasya ca gopate .
magānāṃ matprasādena abhivādanapūjane . . 16
1.152.d:
ब्रह्मश्रवस्य दाने तु अव्यङ्गस्य च गोपते ।
मगानां मत्प्रसादेन अभिवादनपूजने ॥ 16
1.152.m: and upon giving sacred Vedic hearing and the avyaṅga, O lord of rays, / and in saluting and worshipping the Magas through your favour;

1.152.s:
vyomapūjāphalaṃ yacca aruṇasya ca pūjanam .
tathānyadapi yatproktamajñānādbrāhmaṇottama . . 17
1.152.d:
व्योमपूजाफलं यच्च अरुणस्य च पूजनम् ।
तथान्यदपि यत्प्रोक्तमज्ञानाद्ब्राह्मणोत्तम ॥ 17
1.152.m: and what is the fruit of worshipping space, and the worship of Aruṇa; / and likewise whatever else has been spoken of out of ignorance, O best of Brahmins—
tell me all that, O Brahmin, out of compassion for the devotees.

1.152.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi sūradharmeṣu praśnavarṇanaṃ nāma
dvipañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 152 .
sūryatejovarṇanam
1.152.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सूरधर्मेषु प्रश्नवर्णनं नाम
द्विपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 152 ।
सूर्यतेजोवर्णनम्
1.152.m:
Thus ends the hundred and fifty-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Inquiry regarding the Duties towards the Sun', in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Splendour of the Sun

1.153.s:
sumanturuvāca
sumatiśca raverbhaktaḥ pāṇḍaveya mahāmate .
ataste nikhilaṃ vacmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā nṛpa . . 1
1.153.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
सुमतिश्च रवेर्भक्तः पाण्डवेय महामते ।
अतस्ते निखिलं वच्मि शृणुष्वैकमना नृप ॥ 1
1.153.m:
Sumantu said:
Wise and a devotee of the Sun are you, O wise descendant of Pāṇḍu! / Therefore I shall tell you everything; listen with one-pointed mind, O king.

1.153.s:
kalpādau sṛjato vīra brahmaṇo vividhāḥ prajāḥ .
ahaṃkāro mahānāsīnnāsti loke maduttamaḥ . . 2
1.153.d:
कल्पादौ सृजतो वीर ब्रह्मणो विविधाः प्रजाः ।
अहंकारो महानासीन्नास्ति लोके मदुत्तमः ॥ 2
1.153.m: At the beginning of the kalpa, O hero, as Brahmā was creating diverse creatures, / a great egotism arose [in him]: 'There is no one in the world superior to me!'

1.153.s:
tathā pālayato vīra keśavasya dharāpate .
tathā saṃharato jajñe'haṅkārastryambakasya ca . . 3
1.153.d:
तथा पालयतो वीर केशवस्य धरापते ।
तथा संहरतो जज्ञेऽहङ्कारस्त्र्यम्बकस्य च ॥ 3
1.153.m: Likewise, O hero, lord of the earth, as Keśava was preserving [the world], / and likewise as Tryambaka was destroying [it], egotism was born [in them].

1.153.s:
ciṃtayantotha te devāḥ keśavaśca narādhipa .
mithaste spardhayā yuktāḥ parasparavirodhinaḥ . . 4
1.153.d:
चिंतयन्तोथ ते देवाः केशवश्च नराधिप ।
मिथस्ते स्पर्धया युक्ताः परस्परविरोधिनः ॥ 4
1.153.m: Then those gods and Keśava, reflecting, O ruler of men, / were filled with rivalry towards one another, opposing each other.

1.153.s:
vivādastu mahānāsītkañjāmbunagaukasām .
parasparaṃ mahābāho manasāśritya kevalam . . 5
1.153.d:
विवादस्तु महानासीत्कञ्जाम्बुनगौकसाम् ।
परस्परं महाबाहो मनसाश्रित्य केवलम् ॥ 5
1.153.m: Indeed, a great dispute arose among those dwellers in the lotus, the waters, and the mountains, / simply by relying on their minds against one another, O mighty-armed one.

1.153.s:
ahaṃ kartā vikartā'haṃ pālako'haṃ jagatprabhuḥ .
ityāha bhagavānbrahmā kṛṣṇabhīmau samarcitau . . 6
1.153.d:
अहं कर्ता विकर्ताऽहं पालकोऽहं जगत्प्रभुः ।
इत्याह भगवान्ब्रह्मा कृष्णभीमौ समर्चितौ ॥ 6
1.153.m: 'I am the creator, I am the transformer, I am the protector, the lord of the universe!' / Thus spoke the blessed Brahmā to Kṛṣṇa and Bhīma, who were worshipped together.

1.153.s:
tathaitya śaṃkaraḥ kruddhaḥ kaḥ śakto madṛte bhuvi .
saṃhartuṃ jagadetaddhi sraṣṭuṃ pālayituṃ tathā . .7
1.153.d:
तथैत्य शंकरः क्रुद्धः कः शक्तो मदृते भुवि ।
संहर्तुं जगदेतद्धि स्रष्टुं पालयितुं तथा ॥7
1.153.m: Then Śaṅkara, arriving enraged, [said:] 'Who on earth other than me is capable / of destroying this universe, or of creating and preserving it?'

1.153.s:
nārāyaṇo'pyevameva manāk krodhasamanvitaḥ .
na vā śakto jagatsraṣṭuṃ saṃhartuṃ rakṣituṃ tathā . . 8
1.153.d:
नारायणोऽप्येवमेव मनाक् क्रोधसमन्वितः ।
न वा शक्तो जगत्स्रष्टुं संहर्तुं रक्षितुं तथा ॥ 8
1.153.m: Nārāyaṇa also, possessed of slight anger, [spoke] in the very same way: / 'Is anyone else able to create, destroy, or protect the universe?'

1.153.s:
evaṃ teṣāṃ pravadatāṃ kruddhānāṃ ca parasparam .
samāviśattadā'jñānaṃ tamo mohātmakaṃ vibho . . 9
1.153.d:
एवं तेषां प्रवदतां क्रुद्धानां च परस्परम् ।
समाविशत्तदाऽज्ञानं तमो मोहात्मकं विभो ॥ 9
1.153.m: As they were speaking thus and enraged at one another, / then, O lord, ignorance—darkness consisting of delusion—entered [them].

1.153.s:
tena krāntadhiyaḥ sarve na paśyanti parasparam .
atyarthaṃ mohamāpannā na jānantīha kiñcana . . 1.153.10
1.153.d:
तेन क्रान्तधियः सर्वे न पश्यन्ति परस्परम् ।
अत्यर्थं मोहमापन्ना न जानन्तीह किञ्चन ॥ 1.153.10
1.153.m: Their minds overcome by it, they could not see one another; / having fallen into extreme delusion, they knew nothing here.

1.153.s:
apaśyanto mithaste tu niṣaṇṇāḥ kṣmātale vibho .
āramanti hi ye cānye te divākaramāsthitāḥ . . 11
1.153.d:
अपश्यन्तो मिथस्ते तु निषण्णाः क्ष्मातले विभो ।
आरमन्ति हि ये चान्ये ते दिवाकरमास्थिताः ॥ 11
1.153.m: Unable to see one another, they sank down upon the surface of the earth, O lord; / and whatever other [beings] took delight, they took refuge in the Sun.

1.153.s:
tamasā mohitāḥ sarve nidrāvatkrāntacetasaḥ .
manāgjñānena cākrāntāḥ kiṃ kuryāmeti mohitāḥ . . 12
1.153.d:
तमसा मोहिताः सर्वे निद्रावत्क्रान्तचेतसः ।
मनाग्ज्ञानेन चाक्रान्ताः किं कुर्यामेति मोहिताः ॥ 12
1.153.m: All were deluded by darkness, their minds overcome as if by sleep; / overwhelmed with just a glimmer of consciousness, bewildered, [wondering:] 'What should we do?'

1.153.s:
atha bhūtādhipo devo gośrutābharaṇojjvalaḥ .
candrārdhakṛtaśobhastu śītalāṃśuviśodhitaḥ . . 13
1.153.d:
अथ भूताधिपो देवो गोश्रुताभरणोज्ज्वलः ।
चन्द्रार्धकृतशोभस्तु शीतलांशुविशोधितः ॥ 13
1.153.m: Then the god who is the lord of spirits, brilliant with an ornament [bright as] a cow's ear, / adorned with a crescent moon, purified by its cool rays,

1.153.s:
ārtimetya parāṃ vīra mohitastamasā vibho .
apaśyannabravīddevaṃ mādhavaṃ bhūdharaṃ harim . . 14
1.153.d:
आर्तिमेत्य परां वीर मोहितस्तमसा विभो ।
अपश्यन्नब्रवीद्देवं माधवं भूधरं हरिम् ॥ 14
1.153.m: having fallen into supreme distress, O hero, deluded by darkness, O lord, / unable to see, spoke to the god Hari, Mādhava, the upholder of the earth.

1.153.s:
mahādeva uvāca
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahābāho kva gatastvaṃ mahāmate .
brahmā ca kva gato vīra nāhaṃ paśyāmi vāṃ kvacit . . 15
1.153.d:
महादेव उवाच
कृष्ण कृष्ण महाबाहो क्व गतस्त्वं महामते ।
ब्रह्मा च क्व गतो वीर नाहं पश्यामि वां क्वचित् ॥ 15
1.153.m:
Mahādeva said:
O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, O mighty-armed one, where have you gone, O wise one? / And where has Brahmā gone, O hero? I do not see you two anywhere!

1.153.s:
mohena mahatāhaṃ vai tamasā ca vimohitaḥ .
kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kva cāhamadhunā sthitaḥ . . 16
1.153.d:
मोहेन महताहं वै तमसा च विमोहितः ।
किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि क्व चाहमधुना स्थितः ॥ 16
1.153.m: I am indeed utterly bewildered by great delusion and darkness. / What shall I do? Where shall I go? And where am I standing now?

1.153.s:
kṣmādharaṃ pṛthivīṃ vṛkṣān devagandharvadānavān .
vipulaṃ sāgaraṃ sindhūnnahi paśyāmi kiñcana . . 17
1.153.d:
क्ष्माधरं पृथिवीं वृक्षान् देवगन्धर्वदानवान् ।
विपुलं सागरं सिन्धून्नहि पश्यामि किञ्चन ॥ 17
1.153.m: The mountains, the earth, the trees, the gods, Gandharvas, and Dānavas, / the vast ocean, and the rivers—I see nothing at all!

1.153.s:
kenopāyena paśyeyaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam .
brūhi me devaśārdūla vrīḍā me'tīva jāyate . . 18
1.153.d:
केनोपायेन पश्येयं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
ब्रूहि मे देवशार्दूल व्रीडा मेऽतीव जायते ॥ 18
1.153.m: By what means might I behold the world of stationary and moving beings? / Tell me, O tiger among gods; shame rises within me exceedingly!

1.153.s:
śaṅkarasya vacaḥ śrutvā harirvacanamabravīt .
śokagadgadayā vācā tamasā mohito nṛpa . . 19
1.153.d:
शङ्करस्य वचः श्रुत्वा हरिर्वचनमब्रवीत् ।
शोकगद्गदया वाचा तमसा मोहितो नृप ॥ 19
1.153.m: Hearing the words of Śaṅkara, Hari spoke [these] words / with a voice faltering with grief, bewildered by darkness, O king.

1.153.s:
viṣṇuruvāca
bhīma bhīma na jāne'haṃ kva bhavānvartate'dhunā .
mamāpi mohitaṃ cetastamasātīva śaṅkara . . 1.153.20
1.153.d:
विष्णुरुवाच
भीम भीम न जानेऽहं क्व भवान्वर्ततेऽधुना ।
ममापि मोहितं चेतस्तमसातीव शङ्कर ॥ 1.153.20
1.153.m:
Viṣṇu said:
O Bhīma, Bhīma, I do not know where you are now! / My mind too, O Śaṅkara, is utterly bewildered by darkness.

1.153.s:
kva gacchāmi kva tiṣṭhāmi kathaṃ tatsvasthatāṃ vrajet .
tamasā pūritaṃ sarvaṃ jagaddhi parameśvara . . 21
1.153.d:
क्व गच्छामि क्व तिष्ठामि कथं तत्स्वस्थतां व्रजेत् ।
तमसा पूरितं सर्वं जगद्धि परमेश्वर ॥ 21
1.153.m: Where shall I go? Where shall I stand? How might [the mind] regain its composure? / For the entire world, O supreme lord, is filled with darkness!

1.153.s:
yadyasau dṛśyate devaḥ surajyeṣṭho'mbujodbhavaḥ .
pṛcchāvastaṃ mahātmānaṃ yadi te rocate hara . . 22
1.153.d:
यद्यसौ दृश्यते देवः सुरज्येष्ठोऽम्बुजोद्भवः ।
पृच्छावस्तं महात्मानं यदि ते रोचते हर ॥ 22
1.153.m: If that god, the eldest of the gods, born from the lotus, can be seen, / let us ask that great-souled one, if it pleases you, O Hara.

1.153.s:
hitvā darpamahaṅkāraṃ samamāsthāya kevalam .
padmānanaṃ padmayoniṃ padmapatranibhekṣaṇam . . 23
1.153.d:
हित्वा दर्पमहङ्कारं सममास्थाय केवलम् ।
पद्माननं पद्मयोनिं पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणम् ॥ 23
1.153.m: Casting aside pride and egotism, and adopting only equanimity, / [let us ask] him whose face is like a lotus, whose origin is the lotus, whose eyes resemble the petals of a lotus.

1.153.s:
ityevaṃ gadato vākyaṃ viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ .
śrutvovāca vibhurbrahmā gaṅgādharamahīdharau . . 24
1.153.d:
इत्येवं गदतो वाक्यं विष्णोरमिततेजसः ।
श्रुत्वोवाच विभुर्ब्रह्मा गङ्गाधरमहीधरौ ॥ 24
1.153.m: Hearing Viṣṇu of boundless splendour speak words in this manner, / the all-pervading Brahmā spoke to the bearer of the Gaṅgā and the upholder of the earth:

1.153.s:
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa mahābāho bhīma bhīma mahāmate .
kva bhavantau brūta kiṃ ca kiṃ yuvāmūcathurmithaḥ . . 25
1.153.d:
कृष्ण कृष्ण महाबाहो भीम भीम महामते ।
क्व भवन्तौ ब्रूत किं च किं युवामूचथुर्मिथः ॥ 25
1.153.m: 'O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, O mighty-armed one! O Bhīma, Bhīma, O wise one! / Where are you two? Speak! What have you two been saying to one another?

1.153.s:
mamātīva manobuddhī tamasā vaśamāgate .
na śṛṇomi na paśyāmi nidrāmohavaśaṃ gataḥ . . 26
1.153.d:
ममातीव मनोबुद्धी तमसा वशमागते ।
न शृणोमि न पश्यामि निद्रामोहवशं गतः ॥ 26
1.153.m: My mind and intellect have completely come under the sway of darkness; / I hear nothing, I see nothing, fallen under the power of sleep and delusion.

1.153.s:
aho bata jagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam .
tamasā vyāṣṭataṃ devau na jāne kva gataṃ mahaḥ . . 27
1.153.d:
अहो बत जगत्सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम् ।
तमसा व्याष्टतं देवौ न जाने क्व गतं महः ॥ 27
1.153.m: Alas, the entire universe, with its gods, Asuras, and human beings, / is pervaded by darkness, O two gods! I do not know where the light has gone!'

1.153.s:
atha teṣāṃ pravadatāṃ brahmādīnāṃ divaukasām .
darpakrodhabhayārtānāṃ tamasākrāntacetasām . . 28
1.153.d:
अथ तेषां प्रवदतां ब्रह्मादीनां दिवौकसाम् ।
दर्पक्रोधभयार्तानां तमसाक्रान्तचेतसाम् ॥ 28
1.153.m: Then, as those dwellers of heaven headed by Brahmā were speaking, / afflicted by pride, anger, and fear, their minds overwhelmed by darkness—

1.153.s:
teṣāṃ darpāpahārāya prabodhārthaṃ ca gopateḥ .
tejorūpaṃ samudbhūtamaṣṭaśṛṅgamanaupamam . . 29
1.153.d:
तेषां दर्पापहाराय प्रबोधार्थं च गोपतेः ।
तेजोरूपं समुद्भूतमष्टशृङ्गमनौपमम् ॥ 29
1.153.m:
To take away their pride and to enlighten the lord of cattle,
an incomparable form of splendor arose, possessing eight peaks.

1.153.s:
alakṣyaṃ pāpatamasā mahadvyoma narādhipa .
jvālāmālāvṛtaṃ vīra bahurūpaṃ ca bhāsate . . 1.153.30
1.153.d:
अलक्ष्यं पापतमसा महद्व्योम नराधिप ।
ज्वालामालावृतं वीर बहुरूपं च भासते ॥ 1.153.30
1.153.m:
The vast sky, unperceived because of the evil darkness, O king,
encompassed by garlands of flames, multiform, shone forth, O hero.

1.153.s:
śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ gatamūrdhvaṃ bhramattathā .
gomadhyato mahārāja karṇikevāmbujasya tu . . 31
1.153.d:
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं गतमूर्ध्वं भ्रमत्तथा ।
गोमध्यतो महाराज कर्णिकेवाम्बुजस्य तु ॥ 31
1.153.m:
Extending for a hundred yojanas, rising upward and whirling,
out from the midst of the rays, O great king, like the pericarp of a lotus.

1.153.s:
prakāśaṃ tejasā tasya jagatsarvamidaṃ nṛpa .
pureṣvantaryathā vīra ambujasyārcibhiḥ sadā . . 32
1.153.d:
प्रकाशं तेजसा तस्य जगत्सर्वमिदं नृप ।
पुरेष्वन्तर्यथा वीर अम्बुजस्यार्चिभिः सदा ॥ 32
1.153.m:
All this world was illumined by its splendor, O king,
just as within lotus cities [it is illumined] continually by rays, O hero.

1.153.s:
dṛṣṭvā parasparaṃ sarve huṅkārādivikāriṇaḥ .
tejasā mohitāstasya jagatsarvamidaṃ nṛpa . . 33
1.153.d:
दृष्ट्वा परस्परं सर्वे हुङ्कारादिविकारिणः ।
तेजसा मोहितास्तस्य जगत्सर्वमिदं नृप ॥ 33
1.153.m:
Seeing one another, they were all overcome with roars and other agitations,
bewildered by its splendor, along with this entire world, O king.

1.153.s:
tejasā mohitaṃ tasya mahadvyoma narādhipa .
tato vismayamāsīnaḥ dṛṣṭagopatayo nṛpa . . 34
1.153.d:
तेजसा मोहितं तस्य महद्व्योम नराधिप ।
ततो विस्मयमासीनः दृष्टगोपतयो नृप ॥ 34
1.153.m:
The vast sky was bewildered by its splendor, O lord of men.
Then, seated in astonishment, seeing the lords of rays, O king,

1.153.s:
paśyamānā maho vyomni mitho vacanamabruvan .
aho tejaḥ samuddhūtamasmākaṃ śreyase nṛpa . . 35
1.153.d:
पश्यमाना महो व्योम्नि मिथो वचनमब्रुवन् ।
अहो तेजः समुद्धूतमस्माकं श्रेयसे नृप ॥ 35
1.153.m:
looking at the splendor in the sky, they spoke words to one another:
"Aha! A splendor has arisen for our welfare, O king,

1.153.s:
prakāśāya ca lokānāṃ sarve paśyāma kiṃ nvidam .
jñānāyordhvaṃ gato brahmā cādhastāttripurāntaka. . . 36
1.153.d:
प्रकाशाय च लोकानां सर्वे पश्याम किं न्विदम् ।
ज्ञानायोर्ध्वं गतो ब्रह्मा चाधस्तात्त्रिपुरान्तक॥ । 36
1.153.m:
and for the illumination of the worlds! Let us all see: what indeed is this?"
To ascertain it, Brahmā went upward, and the destroyer of Tripura [went] downward.

1.153.s:
tiryagjagāma deveśaścakrāmbujagadādharaḥ .
alabdhvā tasya te sarve pramāṇaṃ gairikādhipāḥ . . 37
1.153.d:
तिर्यग्जगाम देवेशश्चक्राम्बुजगदाधरः ।
अलब्ध्वा तस्य ते सर्वे प्रमाणं गैरिकाधिपाः ॥ 37
1.153.m:
The lord of gods, bearer of the discus, lotus, and mace, went transversely.
Not finding its measure, all those lords of mountains,

1.153.s:
vismayotphullanayanā samāgamya parasparam .
sarve kañjādikā devā idaṃ vacanamabruvan . . 38
1.153.d:
विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयना समागम्य परस्परम् ।
सर्वे कञ्जादिका देवा इदं वचनमब्रुवन् ॥ 38
1.153.m:
with eyes wide open in wonder, coming together,
all the gods, beginning with the lotus-born [Brahmā], spoke this word:

1.153.s:
ko'yaṃ kimātmakaścāyaṃ kimidaṃ tejasāṃ nidhiḥ .
aho'sya darśanātsarve sañjātā jñānino vayam . . 39
1.153.d:
कोऽयं किमात्मकश्चायं किमिदं तेजसां निधिः ।
अहोऽस्य दर्शनात्सर्वे सञ्जाता ज्ञानिनो वयम् ॥ 39
1.153.m:
"Who is this? Of what nature is he? What is this treasury of splendors?
Ah, by the sight of him we all have become possessors of knowledge!

1.153.s:
tasmātsarve praṇamyainaṃ stuvīmo'dbhutadarśanam .
kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve cāstuvaṃstridivaukasaḥ . . 1.153.40
1.153.d:
तस्मात्सर्वे प्रणम्यैनं स्तुवीमोऽद्भुतदर्शनम् ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे चास्तुवंस्त्रिदिवौकसः ॥ 1.153.40
1.153.m:
Therefore, having bowed to him, let us all praise this wondrous sight!"
With palms joined in reverence, all the dwellers of heaven praised [him].

1.153.s:
stuvatāmapyathaiteṣāṃ sahasrakiraṇo raviḥ .
ātmānaṃ darśayāmāsa kṛpayā parayā vṛtaḥ . . 41
1.153.d:
स्तुवतामप्यथैतेषां सहस्रकिरणो रविः ।
आत्मानं दर्शयामास कृपया परया वृतः ॥ 41
1.153.m:
And while they were praising him, the thousand-rayed sun,
filled with supreme compassion, revealed himself.

1.153.s:
jñātvā bhaktiṃ mahābāho brahmādīnāṃ mahopamām .
atha te vyomni deveśaṃ dadṛśuḥ parameśvaram . . 42
1.153.d:
ज्ञात्वा भक्तिं महाबाहो ब्रह्मादीनां महोपमाम् ।
अथ ते व्योम्नि देवेशं ददृशुः परमेश्वरम् ॥ 42
1.153.m:
Recognizing the devotion of Brahmā and the others, O mighty-armed one, to be great,
they then beheld the lord of gods, the supreme lord, in the sky:

1.153.s:
khaṣolkalokanātheśaṃ sahasrakiraṇojjvalam .
kṛttikābhirasaṃspṛṣṭaṃ yadvā tatkārtikāsthitam . . 43
1.153.d:
खषोल्कलोकनाथेशं सहस्रकिरणोज्ज्वलम् ।
कृत्तिकाभिरसंस्पृष्टं यद्वा तत्कार्तिकास्थितम् ॥ 43
1.153.m:
Khaṣolka, the lord and ruler of the worlds, radiant with a thousand rays,
untouched by the Kṛttikās, or abiding in Kārtika,

1.153.s:
durjayaṃ kṛttikānāṃ tu tathaikena vivarjitam .
tathā hastavihīnaṃ ca saptarṣirahitaṃ tathā . . 44
1.153.d:
दुर्जयं कृत्तिकानां तु तथैकेन विवर्जितम् ।
तथा हस्तविहीनं च सप्तर्षिरहितं तथा ॥ 44
1.153.m:
invincible to the Kṛttikās, yet devoid of one;
likewise devoid of Hasta, and devoid of the seven sages,

1.153.s:
varṣābdarahitaṃ devaṃ saptasvaravivarjitam .
sakalaṃ niṣkalaṃ caiva sadaikākārarūpiṇam . .45
1.153.d:
वर्षाब्दरहितं देवं सप्तस्वरविवर्जितम् ।
सकलं निष्कलं चैव सदैकाकाररूपिणम् ॥45
1.153.m:
the god devoid of rain and clouds, devoid of the seven musical notes,
with parts and without parts, having an eternally uniform form.

1.153.s:
taddṛṣṭvānekaśirasamanekacaraṇaṃ tathā .
anekodarabāhvaṃsamanekābharaṇānvitam . .4 6
anekānanamakṣībaṃ sahasrākṣamanaupamam .
anekavarṇarūpaṃ ca anekamukuṭojjvalam . .47
1.153.d:
तद्दृष्ट्वानेकशिरसमनेकचरणं तथा ।
अनेकोदरबाह्वंसमनेकाभरणान्वितम् ॥4 6
अनेकाननमक्षीबं सहस्राक्षमनौपमम् ।
अनेकवर्णरूपं च अनेकमुकुटोज्ज्वलम् ॥47
1.153.m:
Having seen that [form] with many heads and many feet,
with many bellies, arms, and shoulders, endowed with many ornaments, / with many faces, not intoxicated, thousand-eyed, incomparable,
of many colors and forms, radiant with many diadems,

1.153.s:
dṛṣṭvaivaṃ devadevasya rūpaṃ bhānormahātmanaḥ .
vismayotphullanayanāstuṣṭavuste divākaram . . 48
1.153.d:
दृष्ट्वैवं देवदेवस्य रूपं भानोर्महात्मनः ।
विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयनास्तुष्टवुस्ते दिवाकरम् ॥ 48
1.153.m:
having thus seen the form of the god of gods, the great-souled sun,
their eyes wide open in wonder, they praised the maker of day.

1.153.s:
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā brahmā stotuṃ pracakrame .
praṇamya śirasā bhānumidaṃ vacanamabravīt . . 49
1.153.d:
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा ब्रह्मा स्तोतुं प्रचक्रमे ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा भानुमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 49
1.153.m:
Joining his palms in reverence, Brahmā began to praise him;
bowing his head to the sun, he spoke this word:

1.153.s:
brahmovāca
namaste devadeveśa sahasrakiraṇojjvala .
lokadīpa namaste'stu namaste koṇavallabha . . 1.153.50
1.153.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नमस्ते देवदेवेश सहस्रकिरणोज्ज्वल ।
लोकदीप नमस्तेऽस्तु नमस्ते कोणवल्लभ ॥ 1.153.50
1.153.m:
Brahmā said:
"Obeisance to you, O lord of the gods of gods, radiant with a thousand rays!
O lamp of the world, obeisance be to you! Obeisance to you, O beloved of Koṇa!

1.153.s:
bhāskarāya namo nityaṃ khaṣolkāya namonamaḥ .
viṣṇave kālacakrāya somāyāmitatejase . . 51
1.153.d:
भास्कराय नमो नित्यं खषोल्काय नमोनमः ।
विष्णवे कालचक्राय सोमायामिततेजसे ॥ 51
1.153.m:
Obeisance perpetually to Bhāskara! Obeisance, obeisance to Khaṣolka,
to Viṣṇu, to the wheel of time, to Soma of boundless splendor!

1.153.s:
namaste pañcakālāya indrāya vasuretase .
khagāya lokanāthāya ekacakrarathāya ca . . 52
1.153.d:
नमस्ते पञ्चकालाय इन्द्राय वसुरेतसे ।
खगाय लोकनाथाय एकचक्ररथाय च ॥ 52
1.153.m:
Obeisance to you, the five periods of time, to Indra, whose seed is Vasu,
to the sky-traveler, the lord of the world, and whose chariot has a single wheel!

1.153.s:
jagaddhitāya devāya śivāyāmitatejase .
tamoghnāya surūpāya tejasāṃ nidhaye namaḥ . . 53
1.153.d:
जगद्धिताय देवाय शिवायामिततेजसे ।
तमोघ्नाय सुरूपाय तेजसां निधये नमः ॥ 53
1.153.m:
To the god who works the welfare of the world, to Śiva of boundless splendor,
to the destroyer of darkness, the handsome one, obeisance to the treasury of splendors!

1.153.s:
arthāya kāmarūpāya dharmāyāmitatejase .
mokṣāya mokṣarūpāya sūryāya ca namonamaḥ . . 54
1.153.d:
अर्थाय कामरूपाय धर्मायामिततेजसे ।
मोक्षाय मोक्षरूपाय सूर्याय च नमोनमः ॥ 54
1.153.m:
To wealth, to the one whose form is desire, to dharma of boundless splendor,
to liberation, to the embodiment of liberation, and to Sūrya, obeisance, obeisance!

1.153.s:
krodhalobhavihīnāya lokānāṃ sthitihetave .
śubhāya śubharūpāya śubhadāya śubhātmane . . 55
1.153.d:
क्रोधलोभविहीनाय लोकानां स्थितिहेतवे ।
शुभाय शुभरूपाय शुभदाय शुभात्मने ॥ 55
1.153.m:
To the one free from anger and greed, the cause of the stability of the worlds,
to the auspicious, the auspicious-formed, the giver of auspiciousness, the auspicious self!

1.153.s:
śāntāya śāntarūpāya śāntaye'smāsu vai namaḥ .
namaste brahmarūpāya brāhmaṇāya namonamaḥ . . 56
1.153.d:
शान्ताय शान्तरूपाय शान्तयेऽस्मासु वै नमः ।
नमस्ते ब्रह्मरूपाय ब्राह्मणाय नमोनमः ॥ 56
1.153.m:
To the peaceful, the peaceful-formed, to the peace within us, indeed, obeisance!
Obeisance to you whose form is Brahman, obeisance, obeisance to the Brāhmaṇa!

1.153.s:
brahmadevāya brahmarūpāya brahmaṇe paramātmane .
brahmaṇe ca prasādaṃ vai kuru deva jagatpate . . 57
1.153.d:
ब्रह्मदेवाय ब्रह्मरूपाय ब्रह्मणे परमात्मने ।
ब्रह्मणे च प्रसादं वै कुरु देव जगत्पते ॥ 57
1.153.m:
To the god of Brahmā, whose form is Brahman, to Brahman, the supreme self;
and grant grace to Brahmā, O god, O lord of the universe!"

1.153.s:
evaṃ stutvā raviṃ brahmā śraddhayā parayā vibho .
tūṣṇīmāsīnmahābhāga prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā . . 58
1.153.d:
एवं स्तुत्वा रविं ब्रह्मा श्रद्धया परया विभो ।
तूष्णीमासीन्महाभाग प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना ॥ 58
1.153.m:
Having thus praised the sun with supreme faith, O all-pervading one,
Brahmā remained silent, O fortunate one, with an inner self exceedingly delighted.

1.153.s:
brahmaṇo'nantaraṃ rudraḥ stotraṃ cakre vibhāvasoḥ .
tripurārirmahātejāḥ praṇamya śirasā ravim ..59
1.153.d:
ब्रह्मणोऽनन्तरं रुद्रः स्तोत्रं चक्रे विभावसोः ।
त्रिपुरारिर्महातेजाः प्रणम्य शिरसा रविम् ॥59
1.153.m:
After Brahmā, Rudra composed a hymn of praise to the luminous one;
the foe of Tripura, of great splendor, bowed his head to the sun:

1.153.s:
mahādeva uvāca
jaya bhāva jayājeya jaya haṃsa divākara .
jaya śambho mahābāho khaga gocara bhūdhara ..1.153.60
1.153.d:
महादेव उवाच
जय भाव जयाजेय जय हंस दिवाकर ।
जय शम्भो महाबाहो खग गोचर भूधर ॥1.153.60
1.153.m:
Mahādeva said:
"Victory, O source of existence! Victory, O unconquerable one! Victory, O swan, O day-maker!
Victory, O Śambhu, O mighty-armed one, sky-traveler, sphere of the rays, supporter of the earth!

1.153.s:
jaya lokapradīpena jaya bhāno jagatpate .
jaya kāla jayānanta saṃvatsara śubhānana ..6 1
jaya devāditeḥ putra kaśyapānandavardhana .
tamoghna jaya sapteśa jaya saptāśvavāhana ..62
1.153.d:
जय लोकप्रदीपेन जय भानो जगत्पते ।
जय काल जयानन्त संवत्सर शुभानन ॥6 1
जय देवादितेः पुत्र कश्यपानन्दवर्धन ।
तमोघ्न जय सप्तेश जय सप्ताश्ववाहन ॥62
1.153.m:
Victory through the lamp of the world! Victory, O sun, O lord of the universe!
Victory, O time! Victory, O endless one, year, auspicious-faced one! / Victory, O son of divine Aditi, increaser of the joy of Kaśyapa!
O destroyer of darkness, victory, O lord of the seven! Victory, O you whose mount is seven horses!

1.153.s:
maheśa jaya kāntīśa jaya kāleśa śaṅkara .
arthakāmeśa dharmeśa jaya mokṣeśa śarmada ..63
1.153.d:
महेश जय कान्तीश जय कालेश शङ्कर ।
अर्थकामेश धर्मेश जय मोक्षेश शर्मद ॥63
1.153.m:
O great lord, victory, O lord of splendor! Victory, O lord of time, O Śaṅkara!
O lord of wealth and desire, lord of dharma! Victory, O lord of liberation, bestower of happiness!

1.153.s:
jaya vedāṅgarūpāya graharūpāya vai namaḥ .
satyāya satyarūpāya surūpāya śubhāya ca ..64
1.153.d:
जय वेदाङ्गरूपाय ग्रहरूपाय वै नमः ।
सत्याय सत्यरूपाय सुरूपाय शुभाय च ॥64
1.153.m:
Victory to the embodiment of the Vedāṅgas! Obeisance indeed to the embodiment of the planets,
to truth, to the embodiment of truth, to the handsome and the auspicious one!

1.153.s:
krodhalobhavināśāya kāmanāśāya vai jaya .
kalmāṣapakṣirūpāya yatirūpāya śambhave ..65
1.153.d:
क्रोधलोभविनाशाय कामनाशाय वै जय ।
कल्माषपक्षिरूपाय यतिरूपाय शम्भवे ॥65
1.153.m:
Victory indeed to the destroyer of anger and greed, to the destroyer of desire,
to the one in the form of the spotted bird, the one in the form of an ascetic, to Śambhu!

1.153.s:
viśvāya viśvarūpāya viśvakarmāya vai jaya .
jayoṅkāra vaṣaṭkāra svāhākāra svadhāmaya ..66
1.153.d:
विश्वाय विश्वरूपाय विश्वकर्माय वै जय ।
जयोङ्कार वषट्कार स्वाहाकार स्वधामय ॥66
1.153.m:
Victory indeed to the all, to the embodiment of the all, to Viśvakarman!
Victory, O Oṃkāra, Vaṣaṭkāra, Svāhākāra, you whose essence is Svadhā!

1.153.s:
jayāśvamedharūpāya cāgnirūpāryamāya ca .
saṃsārārṇavapītāya mokṣadvārapradāya ca ..67
1.153.d:
जयाश्वमेधरूपाय चाग्निरूपार्यमाय च ।
संसारार्णवपीताय मोक्षद्वारप्रदाय च ॥67
1.153.m:
Victory to the embodiment of the horse-sacrifice, and to Aryaman whose form is fire,
to the one who has drunk the ocean of worldly existence, and to the bestower of the door of liberation!

1.153.s:
saṃsārārṇavamagnasya mama deva jagatpate .
hastāvalambano deva bhava tvaṃ gopate'dbhuta ..68
1.153.d:
संसारार्णवमग्नस्य मम देव जगत्पते ।
हस्तावलम्बनो देव भव त्वं गोपतेऽद्भुत ॥68
1.153.m:
For me, sunken in the ocean of worldly existence, O god, O lord of the universe,
become a support of the hand, O god, O wondrous lord of rays!

1.153.s:
īśo'pyevamahīnāṅgaṃ stutvā bhānuṃ prayatnataḥ .
virarāma mahārāja praṇamya śirasā ravim ..69
1.153.d:
ईशोऽप्येवमहीनाङ्गं स्तुत्वा भानुं प्रयत्नतः ।
विरराम महाराज प्रणम्य शिरसा रविम् ॥69
1.153.m:
Having thus assiduously praised the sun who has flawless limbs,
Īśa too ceased, O great king, having bowed his head to the sun.

1.153.s:
atha viṣṇurmahātejāḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo ravim .
uvāca rājaśārdūla bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ ..1.153.70
1.153.d:
अथ विष्णुर्महातेजाः कृताञ्जलिपुटो रविम् ।
उवाच राजशार्दूल भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्वितः ॥1.153.70
1.153.m:
Then Viṣṇu of great splendor, with joined palms, spoke to the sun,
O tiger among kings, endowed with devotion and faith:

1.153.s:
viṣṇuruvāca
namāmi devadeveśaṃ bhūtabhāvanamavyayam .
divākaraṃ raviṃ bhānuṃ mārtaṇḍaṃ bhāskaraṃ bhagam ..71
1.153.d:
विष्णुरुवाच
नमामि देवदेवेशं भूतभावनमव्ययम् ।
दिवाकरं रविं भानुं मार्तण्डं भास्करं भगम् ॥71
1.153.m:
Viṣṇu said:
"I bow to the lord of the gods of gods, the source of beings, the imperishable,
the day-maker, Ravi, Bhānu, Mārtaṇḍa, Bhāskara, Bhaga,

1.153.s:
indraṃ viṣṇuṃ hariṃ haṃsamarkaṃ lokaguruṃ vibhum .
trinetraṃ tryakṣaraṃ tryaṅgaṃ trimūrtiṃ trigatiṃ śubham . .72
1.153.d:
इन्द्रं विष्णुं हरिं हंसमर्कं लोकगुरुं विभुम् ।
त्रिनेत्रं त्र्यक्षरं त्र्यङ्गं त्रिमूर्तिं त्रिगतिं शुभम् ॥72
1.153.m:
Indra, Viṣṇu, Hari, the swan, Arka, the teacher of the world, the all-pervading one,
three-eyed, three-syllabled, three-limbed, three-formed, of threefold course, the auspicious one.

1.153.s:
ṣaṇmukhāya namo nityaṃ trinetrāya namonamaḥ .
caturviṃśatipādāya namo dvādaśapāṇaye . 73 .
1.153.d:
षण्मुखाय नमो नित्यं त्रिनेत्राय नमोनमः ।
चतुर्विंशतिपादाय नमो द्वादशपाणये । 73 ।
1.153.m:
Obeisance perpetually to the six-faced one! Obeisance, obeisance to the three-eyed one!
Obeisance to the one with twenty-four feet! Obeisance to the twelve-handed one!

1.153.s:
namaste bhūtapataye lokānāṃ pataye namaḥ .
devānāṃ pataye nityaṃ varṇānāṃ pataye namaḥ . .74
1.153.d:
नमस्ते भूतपतये लोकानां पतये नमः ।
देवानां पतये नित्यं वर्णानां पतये नमः ॥74
1.153.m:
Obeisance to you, the lord of beings! Obeisance to the lord of the worlds!
Obeisance perpetually to the lord of the gods! Obeisance to the lord of the social classes!

1.153.s:
tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ jagannātho rudrastvaṃ ca prajāpatiḥ .
tvaṃ somastvaṃ tathādityastvamoṃkāraka eva hi . . 75
1.153.d:
त्वं ब्रह्मा त्वं जगन्नाथो रुद्रस्त्वं च प्रजापतिः ।
त्वं सोमस्त्वं तथादित्यस्त्वमोंकारक एव हि ॥ 75
1.153.m:
You are Brahmā, you are the lord of the universe, and you are Rudra, Prajāpati;
you are Soma, and likewise you are Āditya; you are indeed Oṃkāra itself."

1.153.s:
bṛhaspatirbudhastvaṃ hi tvaṃ śukrastvaṃ vibhāvasuḥ .
yamastvaṃ varuṇastvaṃ hi namaste kaśyapātmaja . . 76
1.153.d:
बृहस्पतिर्बुधस्त्वं हि त्वं शुक्रस्त्वं विभावसुः ।
यमस्त्वं वरुणस्त्वं हि नमस्ते कश्यपात्मज ॥ 76
1.153.m: You indeed are Bṛhaspati, you are Budha, you are Śukra, you are Vibhāvasu; / you are Yama, you are Varuṇa; homage to you, O son of Kaśyapa!

1.153.s:
tvayā tatamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam .
tvatta eva samutpannaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam . . 77
1.153.d:
त्वया ततमिदं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
त्वत्त एव समुत्पन्नं सदेवासुरमानुषम् ॥ 77
1.153.m: By you is all this universe pervaded, both moving and unmoving; / from you alone has it arisen, together with gods, asuras, and mortals.

1.153.s:
brahmā cāhaṃ ca rudraśca samutpannā jagatpate .
kalpādau tu purā deva sthitaye jagato'nagha . . 78
1.153.d:
ब्रह्मा चाहं च रुद्रश्च समुत्पन्ना जगत्पते ।
कल्पादौ तु पुरा देव स्थितये जगतोऽनघ ॥ 78
1.153.m: Brahmā, myself, and Rudra have also arisen, O Lord of the universe, / at the beginning of the kalpa long ago, O sinless god, for the preservation of the universe.

1.153.s:
namaste vedarūpāya ahorūpāya vai namaḥ .
namaste jñānarūpāya yajñāya ca namonamaḥ . .79
1.153.d:
नमस्ते वेदरूपाय अहोरूपाय वै नमः ।
नमस्ते ज्ञानरूपाय यज्ञाय च नमोनमः ॥79
1.153.m: Homage to you whose form is the Veda, homage indeed to you whose form is the day; / homage to you whose form is knowledge, and homage, homage to sacrifice!

1.153.s:
prasīdāsmāsu deveśa bhūteśa kiraṇojjvala .
saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ prasādaṃ kuru gopate . .1.153.80
1.153.d:
प्रसीदास्मासु देवेश भूतेश किरणोज्ज्वल ।
संसारार्णवमग्नानां प्रसादं कुरु गोपते ॥1.153.80
1.153.m: Be gracious to us, O Lord of gods, Lord of beings, radiant with rays; / grant your grace, O Lord of rays, to those immersed in the ocean of saṃsāra!

1.153.s:
vedāntāya namo nityaṃ namo yajñakalāya ca . .
sumanturuvāca
stutvaivaṃ bhāskaraṃ bhaktyā viṣṇurbharatasattama .
pradadhyau nṛpaśārdūla raviṃ tadgatamānasaḥ . 81
1.153.d:
वेदान्ताय नमो नित्यं नमो यज्ञकलाय च ॥
सुमन्तुरुवाच
स्तुत्वैवं भास्करं भक्त्या विष्णुर्भरतसत्तम ।
प्रदध्यौ नृपशार्दूल रविं तद्गतमानसः । 81
1.153.m: Homage continually to the culmination of the Vedas, and homage to the portion of sacrifice! / Sumantu said: / Having thus praised the sun with devotion, O best of Bharatas, / Viṣṇu meditated upon the sun, O tiger among kings, with mind fixed on him.

1.153.s:
evaṃ te naraśārdūla devā brahmādayo'nagha .
stuvanti taṃ mahātmānaṃ sahasrakiraṇaṃ ravim . . 82
1.153.d:
एवं ते नरशार्दूल देवा ब्रह्मादयोऽनघ ।
स्तुवन्ति तं महात्मानं सहस्रकिरणं रविम् ॥ 82
1.153.m: In this manner, O tiger among men, those gods led by Brahmā, O sinless one, / praised that great-souled, thousand-rayed sun.

1.153.s:
ityevaṃ stuvatāṃ teṣāṃ raviṃ bhaktyā mahātmanām .
atha tuṣṭo ravisteṣāṃ brahmadīnāṃ jagatpatiḥ . 83
1.153.d:
इत्येवं स्तुवतां तेषां रविं भक्त्या महात्मनाम् ।
अथ तुष्टो रविस्तेषां ब्रह्मदीनां जगत्पतिः । 83
1.153.m: As those great-souled ones thus praised the sun with devotion, / the sun, the Lord of the universe, was pleased with them, led by Brahmā.

1.153.s:
vijñāya bhaktiṃ paramāṃ śraddhāṃ ca paramāṃ vibhuḥ .
uvāca sa mahātejāḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā .84
1.153.d:
विज्ञाय भक्तिं परमां श्रद्धां च परमां विभुः ।
उवाच स महातेजाः प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना .84
1.153.m: Recognising their supreme devotion and supreme faith, the all-pervading, / immensely resplendent lord spoke with a rejoicing inner soul.

1.153.s:
graheśo vyoma cārūḍhastejasā prajvalandiśaḥ .
brahmāṇaṃ viṣṇumīśānamāmantryaitānviśāṃpate . .85
1.153.d:
ग्रहेशो व्योम चारूढस्तेजसा प्रज्वलन्दिशः ।
ब्रह्माणं विष्णुमीशानमामन्त्र्यैतान्विशांपते ॥85
1.153.m: The Lord of the planets, mounted in the sky, setting all directions ablaze with splendour, / addressed Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Īśāna, O ruler of people,

1.153.s:
dṛṣṭvā tānpraṇatāntsarvāñchirobhiravaniṃ gatān .
tuṣṭo'smi te surajyeṣṭha caturmukha jagatpate . .
varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te manasā tvaṃ yadicchasi ..86
1.153.d:
दृष्ट्वा तान्प्रणतान्त्सर्वाञ्छिरोभिरवनिं गतान् ।
तुष्टोऽस्मि ते सुरज्येष्ठ चतुर्मुख जगत्पते ॥
वरं वरय भद्रं ते मनसा त्वं यदिच्छसि ॥86
1.153.m: Seeing them all bowed down, touching the earth with their heads: / “I am pleased with you, O eldest of the gods, four-faced Lord of the universe; / choose a boon—may it be well with you—whatever you desire in your mind.”

1.153.s:
kṛtvā tu vacanaṃ bhānorbrahmā lokagururnṛpa .
jagāma śirasā bhūmāvuvāca sa kṛtāñjaliḥ ..87
1.153.d:
कृत्वा तु वचनं भानोर्ब्रह्मा लोकगुरुर्नृप ।
जगाम शिरसा भूमावुवाच स कृताञ्जलिः ॥87
1.153.m: Accepting the words of the sun, O king, Brahmā, the guru of the worlds, / went to the ground with his head and, folding his hands, said:

1.153.s:
brahmovāca
kṛtakṛtyo'smi deveśa pūtaścāsmi khagādhipa .
dhanyo'smyanugṛhīto'smi gato'smi paramāṃ gatim . .88
1.153.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कृतकृत्योऽस्मि देवेश पूतश्चास्मि खगाधिप ।
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि गतोऽस्मि परमां गतिम् ॥88
1.153.m: Brahmā said: / “My purpose is fulfilled, O Lord of gods; I am purified, O Lord of the sky-goers; / I am blessed, I am favoured, I have attained the supreme goal,

1.153.s: sahasrakiraṇairyanme bhavāndarśanamāgataḥ ..89
1.153.d: सहस्रकिरणैर्यन्मे भवान्दर्शनमागतः ॥89
1.153.m: in that you, with your thousand rays, have come into my sight.

1.153.s:
apaśyataśca deveśa mūḍhamāsīnmano mama .
bhagavansamprasīda tvaṃ mamopari vibhāvaso . .1.153.9 0
prayaccha tvaṃ balaṃ bhaktimātmano mama gopate .
gatvā śirobhiravanimaṣṭāṅgaiḥ patitasya ca . .
bhaktyā vijñaptimākarṇya prasādaṃ kuru gopate . . 91
1.153.d:
अपश्यतश्च देवेश मूढमासीन्मनो मम ।
भगवन्सम्प्रसीद त्वं ममोपरि विभावसो ॥1.153.9 0
प्रयच्छ त्वं बलं भक्तिमात्मनो मम गोपते ।
गत्वा शिरोभिरवनिमष्टाङ्गैः पतितस्य च ॥
भक्त्या विज्ञप्तिमाकर्ण्य प्रसादं कुरु गोपते ॥ 91
1.153.m: Not seeing you, O Lord of gods, my mind was bewildered. / O Lord, be fully gracious unto me, O Vibhāvasu! / Grant strength, and devotion to yourself, unto me, O Lord of rays! / To one who has touched the earth with his head and fallen with eight limbs, / hearing my petition made with devotion, grant your grace, O Lord of rays!”

1.153.s:
brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā pūṣā devo jagatpatiḥ .
tathetyāha mahārāja virāṭa praśrayānvitam . . 92
1.153.d:
ब्रह्मणो वचनं श्रुत्वा पूषा देवो जगत्पतिः ।
तथेत्याह महाराज विराट प्रश्रयान्वितम् ॥ 92
1.153.m: Hearing the words of Brahmā, the divine Pūṣan, Lord of the universe, / said ‘So be it,’ O great king, with majestic reverence.

1.153.s:
brahmaṇe ca varaṃ dattvā rājandevo divākaraḥ .
uvāca tryambakaṃ devaṃ śaśāṅkakṛtaśekharam . . 93
1.153.d:
ब्रह्मणे च वरं दत्त्वा राजन्देवो दिवाकरः ।
उवाच त्र्यम्बकं देवं शशाङ्ककृतशेखरम् ॥ 93
1.153.m: Having granted the boon to Brahmā, O king, the divine maker of day / spoke to the god Tryambaka, whose crest is adorned by the crescent moon:

1.153.s:
varaṃ varaya bhūteśa bhūbhṛjjādayitānagha .
yamicchasi mahādeva dade'haṃ tadaśeṣataḥ . . 94
1.153.d:
वरं वरय भूतेश भूभृज्जादयितानघ ।
यमिच्छसि महादेव ददेऽहं तदशेषतः ॥ 94
1.153.m: “Choose a boon, O Lord of beings, beloved of the mountain’s daughter, O sinless one! / Whatever you desire, O Mahādeva, I grant entirely.”

1.153.s:
bhāskarasya vacaḥ śrutvā īśvarastripurāntaka .
gatvā tu śirasā bhūmau praṇamyovāca bhāskaram . . 95
1.153.d:
भास्करस्य वचः श्रुत्वा ईश्वरस्त्रिपुरान्तक ।
गत्वा तु शिरसा भूमौ प्रणम्योवाच भास्करम् ॥ 95
1.153.m: Hearing the words of the sun, Īśvara, the destroyer of Tripura, / touched the ground with his head, bowed, and addressed the sun:

1.153.s:
mahādeva uvāca
puṇyo'haṃ puṇyakarmāhaṃ nāsti dhanyataro mama .
gato'haṃ paramāṃ siddhiṃ gataśca paramāṃ gatim . . 96
1.153.d:
महादेव उवाच
पुण्योऽहं पुण्यकर्माहं नास्ति धन्यतरो मम ।
गतोऽहं परमां सिद्धिं गतश्च परमां गतिम् ॥ 96
1.153.m: Mahādeva said: / “I am meritorious, I have performed holy deeds; no one is more blessed than I; / I have reached supreme perfection, and I have attained the supreme goal.

1.153.s:
nāprāpyamasti deveśa nāsādhyaṃ mama kiṃcana .
yasya me bhagavāndevaḥ prasādapravaṇaḥ sthitaḥ . . 97
1.153.d:
नाप्राप्यमस्ति देवेश नासाध्यं मम किंचन ।
यस्य मे भगवान्देवः प्रसादप्रवणः स्थितः ॥ 97
1.153.m: Nothing is unattainable for me, O Lord of gods, nothing is impossible for me, / for whom the divine Lord stands inclined to grant grace.

1.153.s:
tvayā tatamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam .
tvatta eva samutpannaṃ layaṃ ca tvayi yāsyati . . 98
1.153.d:
त्वया ततमिदं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
त्वत्त एव समुत्पन्नं लयं च त्वयि यास्यति ॥ 98
1.153.m: By you is all this universe pervaded, both moving and unmoving; / from you alone has it arisen, and into you it shall dissolve.

1.153.s:
yadi tuṣṭo mama vibho anugrāhyo'smi te yadi .
acalāṃ dehi me bhaktimātmanaścaraṇaṃ naya . . 99
1.153.d:
यदि तुष्टो मम विभो अनुग्राह्योऽस्मि ते यदि ।
अचलां देहि मे भक्तिमात्मनश्चरणं नय ॥ 99
1.153.m: If you are pleased with me, O all-pervading lord, if I am worthy of your favour, / grant me unswerving devotion and lead me to your feet.”

1.153.s:
vyomakeśavacaḥ śrutvā pūṣā devo divākaraḥ .
tathetyāha haraṃ vīra tato harimuvāca . . 1.153.100
1.153.d:
व्योमकेशवचः श्रुत्वा पूषा देवो दिवाकरः ।
तथेत्याह हरं वीर ततो हरिमुवाच ॥ 1.153.100
1.153.m: Hearing the words of Vyomakeśa, the divine Pūṣan, the maker of day, / said ‘So be it’ to Hara, O hero, and then addressed Hari:

1.153.s:
nārāyaṇa mahābāho varaṃ varaya godhara .
parituṣṭo'smi te deva yamicchasi mahābala . . 101
1.153.d:
नारायण महाबाहो वरं वरय गोधर ।
परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते देव यमिच्छसि महाबल ॥ 101
1.153.m: “O Nārāyaṇa of mighty arms, O supporter of the earth, choose a boon! / I am exceedingly pleased with you, O god; choose whatever you desire, O one of mighty strength!”

1.153.s:
śrutvā tu bhāskaravacaḥ kīlālajanako hariḥ .
uvāca parayā bhaktyā natvā ca śirasā ravim . . 102
1.153.d:
श्रुत्वा तु भास्करवचः कीलालजनको हरिः ।
उवाच परया भक्त्या नत्वा च शिरसा रविम् ॥ 102
1.153.m: Hearing the words of the sun, Hari, the progenitor of the waters, / spoke with supreme devotion, bowing with his head to the sun:

1.153.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca
jaya deva jagannātha jaya deva guro rave .
prasīda mama deveśa bhaktiṃ yacchātmano rave . . 103
1.153.d:
नारायण उवाच
जय देव जगन्नाथ जय देव गुरो रवे ।
प्रसीद मम देवेश भक्तिं यच्छात्मनो रवे ॥ 103
1.153.m: Nārāyaṇa said: / “Hail, O divine Lord of the universe! Hail, O divine guru, O Sun! / Be gracious to me, O Lord of gods; grant me devotion to yourself, O Sun,

1.153.s:
yenāhaṃ sarvadevānāmuttamaḥ syāṃ jagatpate .
ajeyaśca tathā deva daityadānavarakṣasām . . 104
1.153.d:
येनाहं सर्वदेवानामुत्तमः स्यां जगत्पते ।
अजेयश्च तथा देव दैत्यदानवरक्षसाम् ॥ 104
1.153.m: so that I may become foremost among all gods, O Lord of the universe, / and also invincible, O god, to daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas.

1.153.s:
tvadbhaktyā bṛṃhitabalastejasā mahatānvitaḥ .
tato mayā mahatkarma kartavyaṃ tava śāsanāt . . 105
1.153.d:
त्वद्भक्त्या बृंहितबलस्तेजसा महतान्वितः ।
ततो मया महत्कर्म कर्तव्यं तव शासनात् ॥ 105
1.153.m: Strengthened in might through devotion to you, endowed with great splendour, / I must then perform a great task by your command:

1.153.s:
prajānāṃ pālanaṃ deva devānāṃ ca grahādhipa .
varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca varṇadharmasya vā vibho . . 106
1.153.d:
प्रजानां पालनं देव देवानां च ग्रहाधिप ।
वर्णानामाश्रमाणां च वर्णधर्मस्य वा विभो ॥ 106
1.153.m: the protection of creatures, O god, and of the gods, O Lord of planets, / and of the varnas and āśramas, and of the varna duties, O all-pervading lord.

1.153.s:
duṣṭadaityavināśāya lokānāṃ pālanāya ca .
sṛṣṭo'haṃ bhavatā pūrvaṃ kalpādau ca kṛto'nagha . . 107
1.153.d:
दुष्टदैत्यविनाशाय लोकानां पालनाय च ।
सृष्टोऽहं भवता पूर्वं कल्पादौ च कृतोऽनघ ॥ 107
1.153.m: For the destruction of wicked daityas and for the protection of the worlds, / I was created by you long ago and ordained at the beginning of the kalpa, O sinless one.

1.153.s:
yasya ruṣṭo bhavānsyādvai kathañcitpuruṣasya tu .
vyādhirduḥkhaṃ manorogaṃ dāridryaṃ santatikṣayaḥ . . 108
1.153.d:
यस्य रुष्टो भवान्स्याद्वै कथञ्चित्पुरुषस्य तु ।
व्याधिर्दुःखं मनोरोगं दारिद्र्यं सन्ततिक्षयः ॥ 108
1.153.m: For whatever person you might become angry with in any way, / disease, sorrow, mental affliction, poverty, and loss of offspring—

1.153.s:
